TECH01's delivery repeats every 150.0 s: a 12 s rise 400–600 ms above its floor, 10 s on the floor (170 ms under its usual level), then that level. A lock near the floor relocks on the rise (an envelope step), its new epoch seeded on a late sample; the dip lies more than `backlog_ns` under that seed, so the line moves onto it (the 560–660 ms overlap 6.6 s on); the usual level steps again 20 s after the first. The fixed core's PCR lock does exactly that: 10 relocks in the fixture's 734 s (12 in the 930 s, about 46 an hour), 4.75 s dropped, 5.1 s of gaps. The standalone recorder's reference lock, seeded high at its one relock and never moved, absorbed the rises; the engine's lay on the floor (its residual p99 above 0 in 94 % of run 2's reports, median +145 ms; ε −113 and −242 ppm). Not changed here (the floor rules of B-45 and B-48, with a trade-off): moving, in an epoch an envelope step opened, only past `lead_max_ns` (B-48's recorded fallback, scoped to such epochs) or only once the deeper floor has held `step_hold_ns`, both prototyped: on TECH01 2 relocks and 0.08 s dropped in 930 s, the median lead 80 → 392 ms (the latency its rises need anyway), every other trace and unit test unchanged; the first keeps a later fall's latency for hours (20 ppm), the second drops it once after 10 s; seeding a step's relock on the step's floor instead adds relocks on the gate traces (1 → 3–7). **Tests:** `ts_stc_test` 175 → 188 (validator: a 100 ms stream lead delivered 400 ms late for 8 s passes, the stream lead below −200 ms fails at 15.5 s; per row, two frozen pairs, two crossings, two leaps, a 4 s excursion and a rate fit short of its hold leave the recovery clock running, the third or the hold restarts it; `VirtualStc`: a 100 ms mux delivered 400 ms late for 8 s, acquiring and locked, no event; the same rise held, one envelope-step relock 10 s on, never degraded; PTS 300 ms behind its PCR, degraded (lead) at 5 s and recovered 30 s after it is back; the same from a 90 s backlog drained in 5 s, degraded 5 s after the drain starts, the stale PES kept in the stream half; a PCR stuck 1 s, then a 250 ms stall every 2 s: recovered 30 s after the freeze row last failed; the PCR fed as a PID's lead no longer degrades); `ts_restamp_test` 277 → 280 (a 125 ms lead, the path 450 ms higher for 8 s every 20 s: never degraded, no relock, gap or drop; the core before degrades at 15.7 s); `trace_cli_test` 63 → 64; vitest `ingestTimingReporter.test.ts` 21 → 22. Mutants caught: the bound back on arrival (the core before: seven checks, the relay case, the TECH01 expectation), the bound removed, the stale exclusion on both halves, the upper bound on the stream lead, and the old exit rule row by row. Checksum `ts_stc` c04aa45e23902500 (without the new cases 34d1bc5cd406b9a6, every earlier scenario bit-identical); `asrc_servo` unchanged. Texts: part 4.3 (the Lead row, the return), part 7.2, part 10's alarm table, chapter 10.2, ADR-0029 Phase 1 (the validation bullet, degraded mode's return, the traces, two open items), the fixtures README, the release notes. **Device check** on .108 (to do): the srt-input on TECH01 for 1 h with the profile, one engine restart and a 2 min load burst (run 1's test modules): never `degraded (lead)`, the Clock badge Locked within 330 s of each start (B-100; about 190 s before it, on a lucky start); at most 3 relocks per 10 min and no pair signature hold with B-95 (the floor change above, built as its window rule; without it the replay predicts about 8 relocks per 10 min in the 150 s pairs). |
| B-91 | Finding: one fd per bus buffer under a lagging consumer (n1x16 on .108) | Measured 2026-10-22 (the wf11 CPU round; read-only on .108), as designed. Each bus buffer crosses an edge as memfd memory of its own: `unixfdsink` keeps it until the consumer's release, and `unixfdsrc` holds its fd until the buffer is freed (the native mr-tssplit and mr-bus-fanout close theirs at once). The count per edge is bounded by the consumer's ingress queue (5 s, or 40 MB when stamps stall). n1x16's probe reached 15,466–16,223 fds = 16 inputs × 5 s × about 195 buffers/s of 1,316 bytes, with the runner shedding; the first runs died at the login shell's soft limit of 1,024. | B-94 | Finding: a producer's `unixfdsink` keeps a stall's high-water mark for the life of the edge (the B-68 triage); fixed in GStreamer by meta-custom's plugins-bad patch 0009 | **Found** 2026-10-22 on the dev Pi by the B-68 triage (engineering item, for the owner's veto). Each copy the consumer releases goes back to the unixfd allocator's pool, which nothing bounds or trims (gst-plugins-bad 1.28.2 `gstunixfdallocator.c:36–103`), and the pool is freed (:138–150) only when the sink stops or takes new caps (`gstunixfdsink.c:819, 759`; a bus edge's caps do not change). So after one stall the producer keeps every fd, mapping and page of its high-water mark: a 2,850/s edge stalled at its 5 s ingress left +14,433 fds and 225 MiB of Shmem in the producer once the consumer had recovered (+1 in the consumer), all freed at the sink's stop. Each copy is also a mapping (the shm allocator keeps it mapped), and the image does not set `vm.max_map_count`, so one GStreamer producer process passes the kernel's 65,530 at its fifth stalled 30 Mbit/s edge; three stalled edges under a bytes-only ingress reached 65,531 mappings and all three appsrcs failed ("Internal data stream error … reason error (-5)", the copy failing), and every mmap of that process would fail with them (inferred, not run). mr-tssplit and mr-bus-fanout close their copies at once and hold none (B-91). **As built** 2026-10-26 (WY1 p4-2b): meta-custom's gstreamer1.0-plugins-bad patch 0009 "unixfd: trim the allocator's pool after a stall" (yocto `feat/house-clock-timing`: `gstreamer1.0-plugins-bad/0009-unixfd-allocator-trim-the-pool-after-a-stall.patch` and its `SRC_URI` line after 0008's; Upstream-Status Pending), `gstunixfdallocator.c` only: 0001 and the sink are untouched. The allocator counts the copies it has handed out and not had back (in flight) and keeps the most in flight in the current second and in each of the eight before it (a new second starts at the count it inherits). At each release, when the copies in flight and released number more than 64, it frees the oldest released copies while they number more than the larger of 64 and twice that peak, at most 16 per release; a copy in flight is not in the pool and is never touched. The pool becomes a `GQueue` (alloc still reuses the most recently released copy; the trim takes the oldest). Each trim is logged at DEBUG in a new debug category, `unixfdallocator`, which exists once the sink has made its first copy and so marks the patch. **Tests** (the dev Pi, 16 KiB pages, all passing): a two-process harness (`${CAP}/wf13/wy1/p4-2b/harness/pool_trim_test.py`): `appsrc ! unixfdsink` pushing 1,316-byte buffers in real time, each with its sequence number, a crc32 of its content and a content made from that number, its PTS tied to the number; `unixfdsrc ! queue leaky=2 max-size-time=5 s max-size-bytes=40 MB` (the bus ingress) `!` a C test sink that holds buffers while told to stall and checks every buffer it takes (crc, content, PTS against the number, order; gaps counted as lost); new copies counted at `memfd_create` (an `LD_PRELOAD` shim); the producer's fds every 50 ms and its `Pss_Shmem` (smaps_rollup, a page walk: the status file's `RssShmem` is a per-CPU batched counter on 6.x, up to ≈ 2 MiB off at 16 KiB pages) every 0.25 s; producer and consumer at `SCHED_FIFO` 1 so a steady edge is steady, the harness at nice 10; the image's plugin today (0001–0008) run beside it. 15 of 15 runs pass (five cases, three times each), and under AddressSanitizer 5 of 5 with no report: a steady 2,850/s edge made 0–3 new copies after a 5 s warm-up against 0–3 for the image's plugin beside it (13–16 copies in all); a bursty one (the consumer taking its buffers 100 ms at a time, ≈ 290 in flight) 0–2 against 0–4; an edge stalled 6 s at 2,850/s (its ingress full at 5 s and leaking 2,842–2,849 buffers, the field's shape) held +14,260–14,267 fds and 223 MiB of `Pss_Shmem`, kept them until the 9 s window had passed and gave them back in 0.3–0.4 s (once 1.3 s, in two steps): fds ≤ steady + 64 8.5–9.1 s and Shmem ≤ steady + 2 MiB 8.6–9.3 s after the consumer had caught up (0.19–0.22 s after the release), 8.8–9.7 s after the release, ending at +65 fds and +1,024 KiB over the producer's start (steady +14–15 fds, 208–224 KiB), and staying there; a second 6 s stall 3 s after the first made 0–3 new copies; at 195/s (a 302M-like edge) +979–980 fds and 15.3 MiB came back to +65 fds and 1,024 KiB 8.3–8.9 s after; every buffer was checked, none corrupt, out of order or lost but to the stall's leak; all copies were freed at the sink's stop; no error or critical. The image's plugin today in the same cases: the stall's +14,264 fds and 223 MiB (+979 and 15.3 MiB at 195/s) stay to the end (B-94). With the trim log on: 888 trims of 16 in 0.31 s, the last leaving 64 copies. Without real-time scheduling (informational, one run at nice 10, load ≈ 1.6): 4 of 5, the restall's consumer lagging ≈ 240 copies in the 9 s after its recovery, which left 487 copies (twice that peak, 7.6 MiB), as the rule gives. **Mutants** (scratch builds, never shipped), each caught: the trim disabled (the image's behaviour: stall and stall195 fail "within 10 s" and "stays"); the trim taking its victims among the copies in flight (the producer logs "object finalizing but still has parent" criticals and dies: copies not freed at its stop, the stream cut short, so "the producer ran to the end" and "no error" fail; the consumer holds its own fds, so its payload stays intact and the sink's error, not the payload check, catches it, as the brief allows); the limit without the peak (64 flat: bursty makes 17,564 new copies against 0, the stall's copies go at once, a second stall makes 17,725); the peak without its window (bursty 16,948 against 0, a second stall 14,199). An earlier mutant run also found that the trim loop could run past an empty pool when the copies in flight alone exceed the limit, which the real limit (≥ twice those in flight) never allows; the loop now stops at an empty pool as well. The patch applies with fuzz 0 and no offset on the recipe's own 1.28.2 tarball in the recipe's order (oe-core 0001, 0002, 0004, meta-custom 0001–0008, 0009) and without 0008; the tree is the tested one, and a fresh build of it gives the same machine code. Engineering calls, for the owner's veto: the 9 s window (below); the limit over the copies in flight and released (below); 16 per release; 64 and 2× as the brief gives them; the debug category; the harness's real-time scheduling. | The pool spares an allocation per buffer in steady state, where a handful of copies are in flight; a stall is the only time it grows, and then it stays, up to 223 MiB on a Pi 5 or 56 MiB on a Pi 4 for one stalled 30 Mbit/s edge. It is bounded by the consumer's ingress (5 s, unchanged by B-68's patch), so it is a budget that stays spent, not a leak. The trim keeps the stall's copies 8–9 s after the consumer has caught up, so a stall that comes back soon makes no new copies, and keeps twice a busy consumer's peak, so a steady or bursty edge makes none it would not make without it. 16 per release keeps the sink's thread taking releases as fast as they come: at 64 per release (≈ 0.6 ms of frees) it fell behind a 2,850/s edge, the count in flight grew by ≈ 550 with the release backlog, and the limit that raised stopped the trim at 1,104 copies until that false peak aged out (measured with the 10 s window). | Chapter 8 and the p4-2b brief read as built. "Twice the in-flight peak of the last 10 s" reads "of the last 9 s (the current second and the eight before it)": the copies then come back 8–9 s after the consumer has caught up and the trim takes ≈ 0.3–0.4 s, inside the brief's "within 10 s"; with 10 s (the window counts whole seconds) they would come back 9–10 s after and the trim end up to 10.4 s after, past that bound in part of the runs, so the brief's rule and its test bound cannot both hold. "When the pool holds more than … free released copies down to it" reads "when the copies in flight and released number more than … free released copies while they do": with the released copies alone held to the limit, 64 released plus those in flight left the producer 67 fds above steady (measured), past "steady + 64". After a stall the producer holds the larger of 64 copies and twice its recent peak: 64 while 32 or fewer are in flight (the harness's 2,850/s edge keeping up: 4–16), up to twice the peak for a busier consumer (at nice 10 on the shared dev Pi, lags of 30–240 copies in the 9 s after recovery left up to twice that, 487 copies and 7.6 MiB once, until the peak aged out), so "steady + 64" holds for a consumer that keeps up within 32. During a stall the copies are in flight and stay: stalls of five 30 Mbit/s edges of one process at once (within 9 s of each other) still pass `vm.max_map_count`, as B-91's bound decides. A producer idle after a stall keeps its copies until its next release or its stop (the trim runs at releases). The fix reaches a box with the image that carries 0009; this app on an older image keeps B-94. `edge-stall-fds` (B-68) reads the feeder's high-water as it stands (14,250 + 300) and its release at the sink's stop; its recovery read is p4-5's (below). ADR-0015's 40 MB bullet carries the pool and the mapping limit. Not operator-visible; no release-notes line. |
| B-95 | TECH01's 150 s relock pairs: a step epoch's floor (B-90's finding 1; B-45 (2), B-48) | Designed 2026-10-22 (read-only on the B-86 core: scratchpad/wf12/triage/b95-step-epoch.md, revised after two critic rounds, a recheck and a final check; revision 2's leap-fall hold reverted in revision 3, the held line's drop at a leap relock stated and pinned in revision 4), built 2026-10-23 (the design's REC3, ported by hand); the owner chose it over `step_hold_ns` 20 s (2026-10-22 19:40 SAST) and asked for the relay's bursts to be investigated apart: bccsa/media-router#847 (its first finding, 2026-10-22: the 150 s cycle is already in NO-OCC-Gate01's RIST output; TECH01 only relays it). **Seen:** the PCR lock of the srt-input on TECH01 relocks in pairs every 150 s (12 relocks, 6.5 s of gaps, 6.0 s dropped in the 930 s recording; 7.8 relocks per 10 min on .108 live; the engine's degraded reference lock 53 an hour before B-90). **Cause:** the delivery bursts 400–600 ms for 12 s every 150 s, then runs 190 ms under its usual level for 6–7 s; the burst's envelope step relocks on the sample that fired it (136–438 ms above the usual level), the dip then lies more than `backlog_ns` under that seed, so B-45 (2) moves the line onto it 6.6 s on (555–640 ms dropped per PID) and the usual level steps again 20 s after the first step. about 0.26 s at a PCR fault: 258 ms at a degraded entry with a freeze); B-48's 490 ms and clause stay. Lengthening the span to the late threshold (500 ms, the first design) only moves the half-speed threshold: TECH01's fold at a 1.6 s burst height fails it every cycle (55 degrades in 13 starts, 194 s dropped) and TECH01's own residual at one 2.2 s stretch (10 of 13 starts), while a stuck PCR's report slows to 1.56 s (clean) and 1.3-1.8 s on TECH01's path (a 1.6 s freeze caught on 5 of 10; the revision's coupled form with the cadence test 1.6-2.3 s, a 2 s freeze on 4 of 10). **Rule:** a freeze pair spans 30 ms as before and is frozen when the PCR did not advance at all over it (`Δσ <= 0`: the same value again, or an earlier one); three in a row fail the row as before. | B-102 | The engine's gst-inspect probes on a cold GStreamer registry: a crash loop at start (`Engine.start`'s `unixfdsrc` check), and a probe that timed out read as "not installed" | Found 2026-10-23 on .108 (Pi 4) in B-97's field test (scratchpad wf12/b97dev: D1, the cold check's F2), fixed 2026-10-23 (engineering choice, for the owner's veto). **Seen:** after B-97's install script removed the user registry (`~/.cache/gstreamer-1.0/registry.aarch64.bin`) the engine crash-looped 8 times in 77 s (03:58:06–03:59:23Z: 16 "GStreamer unixfdsrc not available" journal lines, NRestarts 8, down 77 s instead of about 7) until `gst-inspect-1.0 unixfdsrc` was run once by hand (2 s); before the final restart at 05:17Z the registry was rebuilt by hand the same way (3 s). **Cause:** `Engine.start` checks the bus element with `probeGstElement('unixfdsrc')` (`gstInspect.ts`, `execFile` timeout 2,000 ms) before it loads a plugin. A gst-inspect that finds the registry missing or stale rescans every plugin first (2–3 s on that Pi 4 at 72–87 % busy) and saves the registry only at the end, so the kill at 2 s left none (once a full-size `.tmp` file, 1,559,230 B) and every restart scanned cold again. The probe read a run it killed as "not installed" and cached it for the process. **Exposure:** a box whose registry is lost or stale for most plugins (a fresh /home after a flash; an update that changes most plugins, such as a GStreamer upgrade), worst on a Pi 4: the engine does not start; and any probe that timed out at plugin load (2 s for an element, 5 s for caps and channel counts, 10 s for LADSPA; the manager's `PluginRegistry`, which has no first check, runs its hooks' probes cold and at once) hid an encoder, a hardware scaler, a decoder, a sink or 302M support, or capped audio-encoder's channels at 2, for the process's life. **As built:** every gst-inspect run goes through one runner in `gstInspect.ts`, bounded by `GST_INSPECT_TIMEOUT_MS` 30 s. A run killed at the bound rejects with `GstInspectTimeoutError` (its message names the run and says the answer is not known; `isGstInspectTimeout` tells it by name, across package copies) and no probe caches it: `probeGstElement` and `gstElementSupportsCaps` drop it, `findLadspaElement` keeps not caching a failure and no longer reads a timeout as "not installed", `gstInspectMaxChannels` no longer reads it as 2 channels; a failed exit is still cached as absent. A run killed by a signal (`err.signal` set, not by the bound: an OOM kill during a cold scan) is no answer too, its message naming the signal (B-103's build, from this row's review). **Narrowed by h2** (2026-10-23, an engineering call for the owner's veto): only SIGKILL and SIGTERM (an OOM kill, a stop) are no answer; a run ended by any other signal (SIGSEGV, SIGABRT, SIGBUS: a broken element or driver, which crashes at every run, so as b103 built it every start of its plugin's modules failed through `settle`) is a failed run, the element absent and cached as before B-102, with a warning naming the signal ('gst-inspect-1.0 X crashed (SIGSEGV), so X is taken as not installed'), and a plugin falls back as it always did; our own bound (`err.killed`) is unchanged. A process's first run goes alone and the rest wait for it, so a cold registry is rescanned once, not once per concurrent probe. `Engine.start` lets the error through: its start error names the timed-out probe instead of a missing unixfdsrc. The callers catch nothing (`probeEncoderAvailability`, `ProbedEncoders.probe`, `probeDecoderAvailability`, `probe302mSupport` and the `initManifest` hooks of video-encoder, transcoder, video-player, audio-encoder and the four 302M modules), so a timeout fails the hook, before it narrows the manifest or sets its statics. `PluginLoader` records a hook a timeout cut short and runs it again before each start of a module of that plugin (`settle`, which `ModuleInstance.start` awaits through a hook `ModuleManager.createModule` passes) until it runs through; a timeout again fails that start with the timeout's message, and the next start runs it again. The hook contract (`PluginClassStatics`) says so: an `initManifest` must be safe to run twice and must let the error through. The manager's `PluginRegistry` keeps such a plugin's fallback schema un-narrowed (nothing hidden). | **Measured** (dev Pi 5, gst 1.28.2, a private `GST_REGISTRY` per run, every process at nice 19; its 278 plugin libraries make a registry of 1,636,979 B, .108's 1,559,230 B; scratchpad/wf12/b102, mr-captures/wf12/b102: measure-cold.txt): a cold `gst-inspect-1.0 unixfdsrc` takes 1.68–1.71 s idle, 3.44–3.55 s on half a core, 7.02–7.13 s on a quarter (busy loops pinned with it), 2.13–2.20 s and 3.54–3.61 s beside 4 and 8 busy loops on the 4 cores: the scan is CPU-bound. .108's 2 s with the engine down and 3 s at 72–87 % busy (timestamps 1 s apart) make a Pi 4 about 1.5x the dev Pi, so about 11 s on a quarter of a core, more on a first boot with nothing in the page cache: 30 s is 10x the field's 3 s and about 3x that case, and costs only a real hang's wait (GStreamer's plugin loader never gives up on a hung scanner, 1.28.2 `gstpluginloader.c:1042`; a run that hangs is killed at the bound). A timeout says nothing about the element, so caching it, or reading it as absent, turns a slow scan into a missing feature for the process's life. 8 cold runs at once on one absent registry took 8.41 s against 1.7 s alone: the first-run gate keeps one cold scan per process whatever the order of the probes (the engine's bus check comes first; the manager's hooks have none) and costs nothing after it (warm runs 19–97 ms; the engine's 24 warm probes 0.32 s at once, 0.77 s one at a time, so not one at a time). Built 2026-10-23. **Before:** `MrInput` emitted every keystroke (a number once the partial value was inside its bounds; an empty box, or the "-" of a negative number, as 0, so a negative value could not be typed over a stored one) and clamped at the commit. Only Ingest Offset, Smoothing Cooldown and the per-PID trims committed on change (B-12), clamped at the commit, a cleared box writing 0 (for Smoothing Cooldown: smoothing off). **As built:** one rule reader (`utils/entryRules.ts`, `readEntry`) and one draft (`composables/useEntryDrafts.ts`, which replaces `useNumberBoxDrafts` and `commitNumberBox`). While typing nothing is checked, shown as an error or written, and no re-render resets the text (B-12's draft, for every box). At the change event (Enter, leaving the box, a spinner step) a valid value that differs from the stored one is written once and an unchanged one writes nothing. An invalid one is not written: the box keeps the text, the reason shows under it ("Must be between -10000 and 10000 ms", "Enter a whole number", "Enter a number"), the stored value stays in force, and the refused text gives way if the stored value changes under it (another writer). `MrInput` works so for every number box and for a text box given a rule; a text box without one (a dialog's field, read by its own button) still follows each keystroke. Escape closes the panel; what was typed is not written. A box removed while focused (the panel opening another module) writes nothing. **Engineering calls (for the owner's veto):** refuse with the reason instead of clamping, so a mistyped value is never written as the nearest bound (a live Ingest Offset at its bound is a gap or a drop on the stream); refuse an empty or unparseable number box the same way instead of writing 0 (a cleared Smoothing Cooldown box turned smoothing off), except an inheritable array override, which a cleared box returns to "Inherit (global)" as its placeholder says; a trim is removed by typing 0. **Inventory, changed:** the module settings form (number, integer and text settings, live and restart-requiring; Ingest Offset and Smoothing Cooldown fold in, their unit still beside the box; dialog fields read by their own button (Add Module's name, Edit Engine, Register Engine, the names of new and copied dashboards and in Dashboard settings, profiles, engine groups, the link label: nothing there is checked or written while typing, the button checks and writes once); the module's display name and the group and interlock renames (already written at Enter or on leaving the box); the dashboard editor's text options and literal texts (its draft, which nothing reads until Save, follows the typing); pickers, toggles, selects and sliders (no typing; they write on change as before). **Device Manager half** (the owner, 2026-10-23 about 21:47 SAST, verbatim: "yes, apply the same rule to the device manager pages"; Save, in the top bar and the firewall dialog, is never disabled by a check: its press keeps focus in the box (the mousedown's default is prevented), so a reason appearing under the box cannot move Save from under the pointer, and its click commits the focused box, then saves or says why (a toast, the dialog's footer). A box whose check ignores the spaces around an entry (addresses, mask, gateway, DNS, hostname, firewall ports and source, NTP servers) drops them when it commits, so what is checked is what is saved (a `trim` flag in the rule reader). Setup and Account show "At least 8 characters." and "Passwords don't match." once a box is left or Enter is pressed (the B-104 rule for dialogs). NTP, DNS and firewall rows keep a draft with its row when a row above is removed (they were keyed by index). **Engineering calls (for the owner's veto):** Save holds while any box keeps a refused entry and names it, unlike the manager's per-module Save, because the Device Manager's Save writes the whole config at once (network, firewall, PTP, time, manager profiles) and a half-applied network change can cut the box off; | B-105 | A setting changed in the settings panel but not saved yet was lost when another setting of the same module changed | Found 2026-10-23 by B-104's build (scratchpad wf12/b104), fixed 2026-10-23 by h1 (engineering fix). **Seen:** the settings panel keeps a restart-requiring setting in its copy of the module's settings (`localSettings`) until Save writes it (B-104 commits a typed one there at Enter or on leaving the box; a choice or a toggle goes there at once). That copy went back to the stored settings, silently, whenever they changed: a live setting of the same module moved in the panel itself (`usePatch` applies a write to the store before sending it), in its right-click menu or on a dashboard, or another operator's write arriving through the tree. B-104 did not cause it, but with a typed value committed at Enter an operator is likelier to commit one, move on and meet it. **Cause:** `useModuleSettingsForm`'s deep watch on `module.settings` rebuilt the copy from the defaults and the stored settings at every change; the store changes that object in place (`applyTreeOp`), so the watch is handed one object as old and new and had nothing to tell the operator's change from the stored value. **Fix:** at each sync the panel keeps a copy of what it took (the stored settings over the schema's defaults, display-only fields out) and the module it belongs to. When the same module's stored settings change, a key whose value in the panel differs from that copy keeps the panel's value, and every other key takes the new stored one; the copy is then taken afresh. Values compare by content (shared-types' `diffValues`), so a map rebuilt by its widget, or changed in place by a write to one of its entries, follows as a whole. Save writes the operator's values with the others as they now are; last writer wins, as before, so a key changed both in the panel and elsewhere keeps the panel's value. A dependent whose controlling setting the operator changed here stays within the maximum it sets (B-103). Kept as before: B-104's drafts (typing not yet committed) survive any write; the panel switching to another module (one panel, its module changed) takes that module's stored settings whole, so unsaved changes are dropped and are not back when it returns. **Device Manager half** (the owner, 2026-10-24 about 01:20 SAST, verbatim: "yes, fix the config-push problems too"; built 2026-10-24 as dm105 in the Yocto repo's device-manager app and API, notes scratchpad wf12/dm105; found by dm104): the same rule, ported, over the whole config. `socketClient` keeps a copy of the device's config as of the last sync (each `config` push, and this session's own successful save); a push (each connect and reconnect, another session's save, the API's start) takes the device's value wherever the session's config still equals that copy and keeps every value changed there, and Save writes them together, last writer wins (`configMerge.ts`). It merges objects value by value and lists row by row on a row's identity: network interfaces by device name, displays by connector, manager profiles by name. A profile not yet saved belongs to the session. Lists without one are one value: the NTP servers, each interface's DNS servers and firewall rules, a profile's paths. A display's content is one value too, and the active profile one choice over the list. A push fills the rows already shown instead of re-creating them, so typing in progress keeps its box and row (DNS rows, firewall rules, profile cards) and an unsaved new profile stays. After the session's own save succeeds, the copy becomes what it sent, and a new profile in it locks its Username. The API answers a save to the saving session only (it broadcast `saveStatus`, so another session's save showed "Settings saved successfully" over edits it had just discarded). The firewall dialog's Close puts back only what was edited in the dialog, to what it would show had nothing been edited, so another session's rules pushed meanwhile stay (it used to write its pre-push copy back). Close takes one click after a refused port (its press is prevented, as Save's), and the Logs and PTP rows with a label and description beside the box align on the label's line, so a reason never moves the box. **Engineering calls (for the owner's veto):** the merge units above; the toast decided by the API rather than guessed by the client, because a client cannot tell another session's status from its own while its own save is in flight; no notice of another session's save, since the app cannot tell that push from a reconnect; a value a page fills in because the device left it out counts as changed (the API always sends every section). **Tests** (vitest): 22 files / 120 cases -> 24 / 149, the API's socket spec 4 -> 7, 19 mutants caught, a real Chromium check over CDP against a mock backend 60 of 60 (the new checks fail on the previous build). Committed as the Yocto repo's `2de1b941` (local, not pushed). **Device check** (.103, to do: DEV2b had no Device Manager login on 2026-10-26; scratchpad wf12/dm105/device-steps.txt, two sessions and an API restart). | What the operator changed is theirs until they save or close the panel; a write elsewhere, even one by the same panel, must not undo it. The watch gives no old value to compare with, so the reference has to be a copy taken at the sync. | **Tests** (vitest): `ModuleSettingsPanel.test.ts` +7 (a B-105 block; writes go to the store first, as `usePatch` does): a committed restart-requiring number, choice and toggle survive a volume slider moved in the panel and Save writes them with the volume; they survive another operator's write too, which the key it wrote follows, and Save writes both; a key changed in the panel and twice from outside keeps the panel's value; once saved a key follows the next write from outside (a refusal put back); a trim map changed in place from outside reaches the panel beside a committed Latency and Save writes both; typing not yet committed survives a write to its own key and commits over it; another module starts from its own stored settings and coming back drops the change, as before. Since B-107 (i1) Save writes only what the panel changed since that copy, and these tests expect so. Mutants caught (scratchpad wf12/h1): 5 of 5 (the copy rebuilt at every change, as before; the reference the store's own object; a change judged by identity; another module merged into; a dependent moved from outside not held within the panel's maximum). **Device check** (DEV2b, after h1's commit, the Pi 5 test box .103 on its own manager): type and commit a restart-requiring value, move a live slider of the same module, then Save: the typed value is written. | B-106 | A live write held back by the settings panel went to whatever module the panel showed when it went out: a quick switch to another module wrote one module's change into the other, or lost it | Found 2026-10-23 by h1 (pre-existing), fixed 2026-10-23 by i1 (engineering fix). **Seen:** `useModuleSettingsForm` holds a live write back in two ways: a throttle (the first value at once, the latest of each 50 ms window when it closes) and a debounce (`x-debounceMs`: Audio Processing's and Audio Dynamics' controls 100 ms, Audio Encoder's and Video Encoder's bitrates 300 ms, HLS Player's URL 800 ms). Both read the engine and module ids when they went out, the debounce the panel's copy of the value too, and the routing editor keeps one settings panel and changes its module (B-105). So a switch inside the window wrote a throttled value into the new module's setting of the same name, and a debounced one wrote the new module's own value and dropped the old module's change. The panel's one window served every key: a second slider moved inside it took the first one's held value's place, which was lost. The same fault in three more places: the module menu's inline slider (100 ms, in `RoutingEditor`), whose window kept the module of its first value and the latest value of any module, so a value made on another module inside it went to the first, and the first's own held value was lost (it also wrote its first value twice, at once and when the window closed); a dashboard fader or slider (`LinearControl`, 100 ms or `x-debounceMs`), whose value went to the binding its host had when it went out, a host being kept by widget id, which a dashboard's copy keeps (another dashboard on the router's own screen, another router in the manager, a widget re-bound by a save elsewhere); and an image upload (`ModuleSettingsForm`, up to 5 min), whose result went into whatever module the panel showed then, which that module's Save wrote. **Cause:** a held write kept its value only and found its target when it went out. **Fix:** `utils/liveWrites.ts` (`createLiveWrites`): every held value keeps its target (engine id, module id, key) and goes there; one window per target. The panel writes everything it holds at once, to the module it was made on, when it switches to another module or engine and when it closes (an engineering call: the operator is done with that module, so a debounce has nothing more to wait for, and no timer outlives the module the panel shows; closing did so already). The module menu's inline controls moved from `RoutingEditor` into `useContextMenu`, where the menu's state is, and its sliders use the same, written at once when the editor goes. A dashboard host is one per widget and value (DashboardView's key: widget id, source prefix, binding), and a fader or slider gone mid-drag writes its held value at once to its own value, as a release does (before, Vue dropped an unmounted control's emit). An upload that finishes after the panel moved on is dropped: it was the old module's unsaved change, which goes with its others at a switch (B-105), and an upload setting is restart-requiring in every manifest (Video Player's fallback image). Checked, not the fault: `MrSlider` (no timer; a typed box belongs to one module, as the form keys its fields by engine, module and key and B-104's box removed while focused writes nothing); the delete confirmation (`RoutingView` keys the editor by engine, so the dialog goes with it); a rename (the name box is reset at a switch); a dashboard's toggles, dropdowns, number boxes and buttons (they write at once). | A value belongs to the module it was made on; on a production box a write to the wrong module changes a setting nobody touched there, and the change made is lost. | **Tests** (vitest, fake timers): `liveWrites.test.ts` 6 (new: the throttle's first value at once and the latest at the close; a window with nothing held sends nothing; another module's value inside a window its own write, each held value to its module; another engine's same module id and another key other targets; the debounce, per target; a flush to each own target, no window left); `ModuleSettingsPanel.test.ts` +7 (a B-106 block: a throttled value held at a switch to A at once, never to B; a debounced one waiting at a switch to A, B no write; each of the two at a close; both held, the panel moved to B and closed; A → B → A inside the window; the same module id on another engine); `useContextMenu.test.ts` +3 (a value held when the menu reopens on another module to its own module; one held when the editor goes; a toggle at once, nothing without a menu); `DashboardView.test.ts` 2 (new: a fader re-bound mid-drag by a copy's dashboard, the held value to A at once and nothing to B; the same widget and value on the next dashboard keeps its host); `ModuleSettingsForm.test.ts` 2 (new: an upload on its module sets it; one finishing after a switch is not set on the new module). The composable as it was (992cf065) fails 5 of the 7 panel cases (the two closes on A pass there: it flushed at unmount to the module shown). Mutants caught (scratchpad wf12/i1): 12 of 12 (no flush at a switch; none at a close; the target read when the write goes out; one window for every target; the engine left out of a target; a flush dropping a held throttle value; one dropping a waiting debounce; the menu as before, one window with its trailing value to the first module; no flush when the editor goes; hosts keyed by widget id only; no write of a drag at unmount; an upload set on any module). **Device check** (DEV2b, the Pi 5 test box .103 on its own manager, CDP with real events): move a slider of module A and switch the panel to module B within 50 ms: A has the value, B is unchanged (tree reads).
