| B-107 | A setting stored above its maximum (its Volume Range lowered alone, from a dashboard for one) made every later Save of its module fail on it, with nothing shown | Found 2026-10-23 by h1, fixed 2026-10-23 by i1 (engineering fix; the calls below are the orchestrator's, for the owner's veto). **Seen:** a stored value can sit above its effective maximum: a dashboard (a dropdown bound to Volume Range, a button's Set to), a script or a router's own screen writes the range alone and the manager clamped no stored volume; the engine's start check brings a value down (B-103) without telling the manager; a profile stored before the manager's check. From then on every Save in the settings panel carried the unchanged value, and the manager refused that op each time ('above maximum 150'; `TreeWrites.config` checks per op and applies the others); `usePatch` only logged it (`console.warn`), the echo put the slider back, and the operator saw nothing. **Cause:** only the settings form brought a dependent down with its source (B-103's form rule lived in the form), and Save wrote every key of the panel's copy (the stored settings over the schema's defaults), changed or not. **Fix**, the orchestrator's calls: (1) **The manager's write path brings a dependent down, for every writer.** After a batch is applied, each stored setting above the maximum that a setting written in the batch now sets (`x-maxFrom`: Volume Range; `x-maxBy`: a codec) is brought down to it in the same write, as a cascade: stored, sent to the engine (a router that made the write gets only the cascade), and published to every client (the writer included, untagged). Built in `PatchRouter.onPatch`, not `TreeWrites`: every writer reaches the manager's store there, the settings panel, the module menu, a manager dashboard, a manager script and any tree client through `TreeWrites`, and a router's own screen (its dashboards at :8081/d/) and its scripts through the router's tree, and its local panel, whose writes the router applies and forwards as engine patches that never pass `TreeWrites`; a profile rollback too. One rule, shared-types' `dependentsOverMaximum` (with `settingMaximum`), which the settings form's clamp now calls as well, on the schema the write check reads (the engine's reported one, else the manifest's). Only a write of the source moves a dependent, and only one above the new maximum: a raised range moves no volume within the old one; a volume left above its range from before comes down to a range written over it, even a higher one; a write of any other setting moves nothing; a dependent set within the new maximum in the same batch keeps its value, in either order. (2) **Save sends only what the operator changed** since the panel last took the stored settings (B-105's copy, compared by content); nothing changed, nothing sent. Before, it sent every key of the copy, defaults included, so an unchanged value above its maximum went out with every Save; a value already written live is not sent again either. (3) **A refusal is shown.** In the manager app each refused op of a `usePatch` write (the panel's Save and live writes, the module menu's) is a toast, the app's notice for a failed action (`useToast`), naming the setting by its label, its module and the reason: 'Input Volume (Mic 1) not saved: above maximum 150' (`console.warn` kept). A dashboard control's refused write shows '<its label>: <reason>' over its foot for 8 s beside its border flash (on the router's own screen too, which has no toasts); a button's refused Set to shows '<path>: <reason>' on its failure line, as a script's failed step does. (4) **Not built:** the engine reporting its start clamp (B-103) to the manager, a wire change; until a write of its source, the manager keeps the value it stored. | A value the manager stores above its maximum is one no writer can send back, so each Save failed on it; the rule h1 gave the settings form has to hold for every writer, and every writer meets in `PatchRouter.onPatch`. A Save that sends what did not change can only repeat a value or fail on it; a refusal the operator cannot see reads as the setting snapping back for no reason. | **Tests** (vitest): `managerTree.test.ts` +6 (a dashboard write lowering Volume Range 500 → 150 with the volume at 300: 150 for both in the same write, the engine sent both, the writer its op tagged and the volume, another client both; with the volume at 100: 100, the range alone sent; a script's write likewise, a volume at the new maximum kept and a later lowering to 200 from 400; a raised range moves no volume; another write moves none and the check's refusals stand, a range written under a volume left above it brings it within; the engine's own schema read, its codec's `x-maxBy` pulling a bitrate from 400 to 320); `PatchRouter.test.ts` +5 (a router's own write: stored at 150, the router sent the cascade only; a codec change pulls an AAC bitrate down, Opus keeps it; a dependent set in the batch within the new maximum kept in either order; only a write of the source moves it, and a volume at the maximum stays; a plugin the manager does not know is left alone); `describe.test.ts` +2 (`dependentsOverMaximum`); `ModuleSettingsPanel.test.ts` +2 (a B-107 block: a Save after a stored volume went over its range sends nothing unchanged and no op the manager's `ModuleWriteCheck` refuses; nothing changed, nothing written), 10 Save expectations moved to the new rule and 6 more made exact (each test's point kept; titles where it moved: a changed trim map with a changed offset; the volume written live already; only the panel's values; the Latency alone; another setting's change sends only itself); `useModuleSettingsForm.test.ts` 1 changed (a plain Apply writes nothing, a changed one only the change, never the graph key); `usePatch.test.ts` +3 (each refused op named by label, module and reason; a write taken shows nothing; an unknown module named by its id); `WidgetHost.test.ts` +3 (a control's refusal, its label and reason over it with the flash; a write taken shows none; a button's Set to on its failure line). The manager's write-check tests pass unchanged. Mutants caught (scratchpad wf12/i1): 16 of 16 (no manager clamp; the clamp not a cascade; not published; not sent for a browser write; worked on the settings before the batch; any write clamping every dependent; no `x-maxBy`; the manifest's schema only; a value at the maximum moved; Save sending everything; changes judged by identity; an empty Save written; a refusal logged only; one without its setting; a control's flash only; a Set to's flash only). **Device check** (DEV2b, .103 on its own manager): on a TEMP Audio Input with the volume at 300, lower Volume Range 500 → 150 from a dashboard dropdown: the tree holds 150 for both; a later Save in its settings panel shows no refusal. Texts: this row and the intro, B-103's and B-105's rows (one sentence each), FDS §9.3 and the FDS's tree checks (one sentence each), `docs/tree-api.md` (Dependents), the release notes (Fixed; B-103's and B-105's bullets where this moved them), `plugins/README.md` (`x-maxFrom`, `x-maxBy`). |
| B-108 | A slider change was written twice: every commit in a module's right-click menu, and in the menu, the settings panel and on a dashboard a value moved and moved back inside a throttle's window | Found 2026-10-23 by DEV2 on the Pi 5 test box .103 (pre-existing since 2026-03), the single commit fixed 2026-10-23 by i1's move for B-106, completed 2026-10-24 by j1 (engineering fix; the calls below are engineering calls, for the owner's veto). **Seen:** in Chromium on .103, an Input Volume of 120 typed into a module's right-click menu and committed by a click on the empty canvas wrote two identical ops, volume = 120, 126 ms apart (B-104's check 'one write' failed on it). **Cause:** the menu's slider throttle (`RoutingEditor.onContextSliderChange`, 7800e4c2 2026-03-20 and b379a9e2 2026-04-01) kept each value as pending before its leading send and never cleared it, so its 100 ms trailing edge sent the same value again: every commit and every lone slider step went twice. i1 (e7c865b8) moved it onto `createLiveWrites` in `useContextMenu`, which holds a value only when a second one comes inside the window, so one commit was one op there. Left open, there and in the settings panel (the same helper, 50 ms): a held value equal to the one its window sent at once (a value moved and moved back inside the window) went again when the window closed or at a flush. A dashboard fader or slider (`LinearControl` with `drag.ts` `throttled`, 100 ms) had the same trailing edge, and its control pushed every pointer move once the drag had moved, so a slow drag of a value with a step wrote each value at the start of a window and again at its close. **Fix:** a throttle's window keeps the value its first edge sent, and the latest value held in it goes when it closes, or at a flush, only if it differs (`createLiveWrites` by content, with the panel's `diffValues`; `throttled` from the value just sent). The first edge always sends: a value that differs from what the control shows is a change, whatever was sent before, as another writer may have moved the stored value since (a call). Each window is judged by its own first value, one window per target (B-106). The dashboard's throttle takes the same rule, and a fader or slider pushes only a value that changed: a move inside one step sends nothing (a call: it is the same fault, and the release-notes line covers every slider). Checked, not the fault: `MrContextMenu` and `MrSlider` emit once per commit (a range input fires only on a change; the typed box returns only a changed entry, B-104); a debounce writes once per rest. | B-104's rule is one write per change; each write goes to the engine, which applies it again, and to every client, and the second was the same value. | **Tests** (vitest, fake timers): `liveWrites.test.ts` 6 → 15 (one value one write; n steps inside one window, the first and the last once each; moved back to the window's first value, nothing more; moved back to where it started, written; away and back over two windows, each a write; a flush of a value equal to the one sent, nothing; another module's equal value its own write; each window judged by its own first value; a list moved back to the same content); `useContextMenu.test.ts` 18 → 22 (one commit one op through the real `MrContextMenu` and `MrSlider`, 120 typed and a press outside the menu, DEV2's case; a drag of n steps inside one window; moved and moved back; a module switch inside the window, A's moved-back value nothing more and C's first its own write); `ModuleSettingsPanel.test.ts` 58 → 61 (the panel's Volume slider: one step one write; moved and moved back inside the 50 ms window; moved back, then a switch, nothing more to A and nothing to B); `logic.test.ts` 13 → 14 (`throttled`: moved back inside the window, nothing more; away and back over two windows, each); `LinearControl.test.ts` 7 → 9 (a slow drag of a value with a step of 10, each value once; moved and moved back inside one window). The sources as at e7c865b8 fail 11 of these 19 cases; the 8 others pin what was right there already, one commit one op among them. Mutants caught (scratchpad wf12/j1): 7 of 7 (a held value sent with no comparison, the helper as i1 left it; compared by identity; a flush with no comparison; one last-sent value for every target; the menu's old throttle, its first value held for the close too; the dashboard's trailing edge with no comparison; the fader's old guard). **Device check** (DEV2b, .103 on its own manager, CDP with real events, the tree watched as DEV2 did): an Input Volume typed into a module's right-click menu and committed by an outside click gives one op. Texts: this row and the intro, B-106's row, FDS §9.3 and the dashboard widgets paragraph (one sentence each), the release notes (Fixed). |
| B-109 | A stream's secret was in the logs in plain text: every RIST input's launch string with its passphrase in the engine journal at each start, and the same for SRT and on four more paths | Found 2026-10-23 by DEV2 on the Pi 5 test box .103, fixed 2026-10-24 by j2 (engineering fix; the calls below are engineering calls, for the owner's veto). **Seen:** at each start of a RIST input's pipeline (every engine start; .103's two RIST inputs call the gate) the engine journal held `[gst-runner] Starting pipeline (…): mrristsrc … secret="…"` with the passphrase in plain text; DEV2's saved journal windows held it on the dev Pi from 18:12Z until they were scrubbed at 19:33Z. Anyone with journal access, a log bundle from the Device Manager's Logs page or a saved log could read the stream's secret. **Cause:** nothing stood between a secret and a log. The runner host (`PythonProcess.start`) logs each launch string whole (on purpose: a rejected parse shows the failing element), and the RIST and SRT builders put the secret into it (`secret="…"` on `mrristsrc` and `mrristsink`, `passphrase=` in the `uri` of `srtsrc` and `srtsink`). The same value could reach a log on four more paths: both runners print the whole rewritten launch string when the native TS module is missing (`native TS module not loaded, parsing with stand-ins: …`) and pass on librist's and GStreamer's lines, which the engine logs as `[gst-py] …`; a runner's error that quotes the pipeline or a URL (the python runner's librist path quotes each URL with its `secret=`) is logged and becomes the module's health text, which every viewer of the tree reads; pino lines carry settings objects (`changes`), helper command lines and helper output (hls-pipe's `HTTP 403 for <signed URL>`), and they also feed the router's and the manager's log lists; the manager keeps and republishes each engine's log entries as they come, from an engine of any release. **Fix:** one redaction step, shared-types' `redact.ts`: `redactSecrets` for text and `redactValue` for JSON data put `<redacted>` in place of each secret's value and leave everything else as it was (the same object when nothing changed). What marks a secret is its name, as no manifest carries a marker (no `x-secret`, `format: password` or `writeOnly`; a call): a setting, element property, URI parameter, environment variable or field whose name, case, `-_.` and spaces aside, ends in secret, passphrase, password, passwd, token, apikey, secretkey (since B-112), streamkey, privatekey, encryptionkey, signature, credential(s) or authorization, or is user-pw, proxy-pw, pwd, psk, sig, hdnts or hdnea. In the manifests that is exactly RIST Input's and RIST Output's Passphrase (`secret`) and SRT Input's and SRT Output's `passphrase`, which a manifest test pins. The text forms: a launch-string property, quoted (with escapes) or bare; a URI parameter (after `?`, `&` or `;`; a secret's value runs to the next `&`, `#`, double quote or line end, a space, `;` or `'` in it included, and only a secret's value is read, so a second URI on the line is still searched); `user:password@` in any URI (the password); an RTMP or RTMPS stream key (the path after the application); `Bearer <token>` and any `Authorization:` value; `"name": value` in JSON or a printed object; `--name value` and `NAME=value` (the Cloudflare tunnel token's forms, `TUNNEL_TOKEN=` and `--token`). JSON data: a secret field's value, the `value` of an op or of a property set on a secret name, the argument after a secret flag, and every string as text. Applied at (a call: the choke points, not each log call): every pino line (the tee of `createLogger`, before both the journal and the log tap, so the engine, the plugins, the manager and both log lists); the runner host for both runners (`PythonProcess`: the start line and its pad-link rules, every relayed stderr line, each event's `message` and `debug`, so the logs and the module's health text); and the manager's store of an engine's log entries (for an engine of an earlier release, a call). The runners print to the journal only through the engine, so they keep no copy of the step. The pipeline itself gets the real value. Checked, nothing reaches a log around these points: the engine's other console lines print fixed texts, ids and socket paths, dgram-comms prints client ids; hls-player's URL can carry `user:password@` and a signed query (`token=`, `Signature=`), which the text forms cover; no code in this repo holds an RTMP key, a bearer token or the Cloudflare token (the Device Manager keeps the token in `/data/cloudflared/token.env`, cloudflared reads it from its environment, and neither logs it); the dgram-comms password is never logged. **Served, not logged** (findings, not changed here): the manager's tree serves every module's settings, a passphrase included, to every client (`/engines/<id>/modules/<m>/settings/…` and a profile's `config` call), as does the router's own tree (port 8081, the LCP and its dashboards); the engine's local API (port 3001) answers only the box itself since B-114. **Limits:** the SRT modules percent-encode the passphrase since B-112, so it is redacted whole; one typed into a URI by hand is redacted up to its first `&`, `#` or double quote (a space, `;` or `'` in it included); a runner's stderr line longer than one pipe read (over 4 KB) can arrive in pieces that are redacted apart (no secret-bearing launch string comes near that); GStreamer's own debug log (`GST_DEBUG` set by hand) is not covered; journal lines written before the update keep their secrets until the journal rotates. | A passphrase is a stream's access control: whoever reads it can receive or send the stream. The journal leaves the box (the Device Manager's log bundle, saved windows, notes), so a log must hold no secret, whatever path a launch string, a URI or a settings object takes into it, and the pipeline must still get the value. | **Tests** (vitest): `redact.test.ts` 57 (new: each name kind and each text form with its exact logged line, idempotent; a launch string escaped inside JSON text; an SRT passphrase typed with a space, a `;` or a `'`, between parameters and last, and one holding a secret parameter of its own, each redacted whole; a secret parameter after another URI on the line; a signed URL in an error, redacted up to the line end; lines left as they are, an empty secret and an empty secret parameter among them; settings, ops, a property set and a command line by `redactValue`, the identity of what holds no secret); `logger.test.ts` 3 (new: a settings object, an error quoting a launch string and a signed URL in a message, redacted alike on stderr and at the tap; a line that is not JSON, redacted as text); `runnerRedaction.test.ts` 3 (new, a stand-in `mr-gst-runner` through `MR_NATIVE_BIN_DIR`: for a RIST and an SRT launch string the start line, its pad-link rules, the runner's stand-in line and its warning, command-error and error events carry `<redacted>` while the runner receives the real pipeline and rules; a warning, a command error and an error quoting the launch string, through `GstRunner`, are logged, and the error posted to the module, with `<redacted>`); the builders of RIST Input and RIST Output +1 each and of SRT Input and SRT Output +4 each (a passphrase as one word and, for SRT, typed with a space, a `;` or a `'`: the pipeline holds the value, its logged form `<redacted>` and nothing else changed); `EngineEventForwarder.test.ts` +1 (an engine's log entries stored and published redacted); `manifestHelpText.test.ts` +1 (the four secret settings). Mutants caught (scratchpad wf12/j2): 37 of 37 (each text rule off; names without their endings or not normalised; an empty value redacted; quotes not kept; `redactValue` without keys, op targets or flags, or always copying; a URI value running past `&`; a bare value stopping at a quote; souphttpsrc's names dropped; a bare `key` ending; the logger's journal or tap given the raw line; the runner host's start line, relay, event texts or event debug raw; the manager's store raw; from the review's fix round: a secret's URI value stopping at a space, a `;` or a `'`, or running past the line end; the one-regex URI rule, which reads every parameter's value; a match inside a redacted value read again; an empty URI value redacted; the logger's line that is not JSON, the pad-link rules and the texts of events other than `error` given raw). No test secret is in the gate's test output (searched). **Device check** (DEV2b, .103): a RIST input restarted logs its launch string with `secret="<redacted>"`, and the box's journal since that restart holds the secret's value nowhere; a TEMP SRT Output and Input on the box with one passphrase typed with a space, a `;` and a `'` connect, and the journal holds no word of it. Texts: this row and the intro, FDS §11.1 (one bullet), plugins/README.md (what marks a secret), the release notes (Fixed). |
| B-110 | An Engine Comms listener could not move between all interfaces and one address: the manager refused the change as 'address in use' | Found 2026-10-23 by DEV2 on .103, fixed 2026-10-24 by j1 (engineering fix; the calls below are engineering calls, for the owner's veto). **Seen:** in Settings → Engine Comms on .103, port 3001 moved from all interfaces to 127.0.0.1 and applied: 'Could not bind listeners: bind EADDRINUSE 127.0.0.1:3001', and nothing applied, though the card offers the change. **Cause:** `EngineConnectionManager.setListeners` probe-binds each listener the live set does not hold at the same address and port before it stops the live server (#692: a port taken by another program is refused while the engines are still connected). A port the live server holds at another address cannot be bound beside it: Linux refuses a specific address under a held wildcard on the same port, and a wildcard over a held specific one. So the probe failed on the manager's own socket, and a move to or from all interfaces, or a swap of ports or addresses between two listeners, could never apply. The real bind came after every listener had closed, as it still does. A set of the same sockets (a script's write, a second browser) stopped and rebuilt the server all the same, and every engine reconnected. **Fix:** the probe binds what can be bound beside the live server: a port it does not hold, whole, as before; a port it holds at another address, the address alone (port 0), which still refuses an address this host lacks before anything is touched, the port being the live server's until it closes (since B-113 only where all interfaces is one of the two addresses; a move between two addresses probes the new one with its port). Then the live server closes, the new set binds, and a bind that still fails re-binds the old set and reports the error as before ('Could not bind listeners: …'); if even that fails, the manager logs that it is not listening and must be restarted, as before. A set of the same sockets, in any order or spelling (a port with no address and with 0.0.0.0), is taken as written and nothing is rebound (a call). Kept (a call): the whole server rebinds at an applied change, as the card says, rather than listener by listener, which would keep the sessions on unchanged listeners but changes dgram-comms' Server (its sessions and retransmits hold the listeners' transports); an option for the owner. **What the engines see:** these listeners are the engines' only link to the manager (config, state, logs, levels). At an applied change the manager ends every engine's session at once, each engine's next packet draws a reset and it re-handshakes by itself, offline 0.19 to 1.17 s on the dev Pi (median 0.53 s with 10 Hz traffic, 0.65 s idle, 10 moves each); the manager then pushes the active profile, which the engine applies as a difference, so nothing restarts and its modules run throughout. Meanwhile the manager shows the engine offline and its modules stopped, their stats blank (`TreePublisher.offline`), until the engine's states come back with it; the engine's log list in the manager starts afresh from the reconnect (its own journal keeps the lines), as at any reconnect. A port moved to 127.0.0.1 is no longer reachable from other hosts: an engine there that used it loses that path and keeps any other (the card's warning that removing the port drops engines that only reach the manager through it shows before Apply); one with no other path is off the manager until the port moves back, its modules running. | The card offers the move, and narrowing a listener to one address (loopback for the box's own engine, one network of a box on two) is ordinary hardening. The probe is there to refuse a bad set with the engines still connected, not a good one on the manager's own socket. | **Tests** (vitest, real sockets on the dev Pi): `EngineConnectionManager.test.ts` 4 → 9 (a port moved from all interfaces to 127.0.0.1 and back, an engine on it back within 3 s each time; the addresses of two listeners swapped on their ports, then their ports swapped; a move to an address this host lacks, refused with the live server, its sockets and the engine untouched; a bind failing after the old set closed, with a program at 127.0.0.2 on the same port, the old set re-bound, the error reported and the engine back; a no-op in the same order, another order and another spelling: the same server and sockets, no engine offline). The code as at e7c865b8 fails 4 of these 5; an address this host lacks was refused up front before and still is. Mutants caught (scratchpad wf12/j1): 6 of 6 (the old probe; no no-op; a moved port not probed; no restore; the no-op judged in order; no address and 0.0.0.0 taken as different). **Device check** (DEV2b, .103 on its own manager): a TEMP listener port added on all interfaces, moved to 127.0.0.1 and back, then removed, each applied with no error and the tree's `/settings/dgramListeners` following; after each apply the engines are connected again within a few seconds, their paths on 3000 and 3001 back. Run 2026-10-26 (DEV2b): four applies as above with no error; at each one every module of the engine read stopped in the manager for 0.12–1.12 s while its session was down (the whole-server rebind of #692, pre-existing), and none restarted. Texts: this row and the intro, ADR-0023 (the rebind bullet), FDS (Engine Comms, one sentence), the release notes (Fixed). |
| B-111 | Audio captures keep their timing on a heavily loaded box: each streaming task from a `pipewiresrc` down to its mux at SCHED_RR 19 through rtkit (B-88's contingency; V-P1-7) | Found 2026-10-23 by DEV2 on .108 (lane-108b, B-88's device check: the loaded hour 22:09–23:09Z), fixed 2026-10-26 by k3 (engineering fix; the calls below are engineering calls, for the owner's veto). **Seen:** with B-88 in, the hour under the profile's load (HDMI video player on; busy 92 %, 1-min load 10–19) had S1–S3 true (each capture runner's `data-loop.0` at RR 20, one rtkit grant each) and failed V-P1-7: a1 51 and a2 53 relocks (`envelope-step`) and 13 `ratio-out-of-bounds` each (H1); 49 and 53 PES pairs off ±1 tick, each a DISCONT and a gap (H2); ERR +11 and +4 (H3). a1 and a2, two captures of the same ATEM node, carried the same sound up to 77–78 ms apart, their `asrcRatio` on the ±1,000 ppm rail in 12–16 % of the polls (F2). **Cause, measured** (schedstat every 2 s over 2,948 s): the capture runners' source task `pipewiresrc0:src` (SCHED_OTHER), which runs `mrasrc` and the 302M encoder, waited for a CPU 25 % of the hour (a1 25.1 %, a2 24.9 %), over 0.5 s of a 2 s interval in 63 % of the intervals and up to 1.2–1.3 s; the mux task `mpegtsmux0:src` (OTHER), which runs the restamp and the bus egress, 14.4–14.5 % (up to 0.64–0.79 s); the RT `data-loop.0` 0.1 %. Each of `mrasrc`'s 44 and 48 events in that record followed source-task waits of median 0.58–0.60 s in the two intervals before it (0.54 s over all intervals): the task was starved throughout. It has 16 PipeWire buffers (≈ 0.68 s at quantum 2048) behind the RT node, and a cycle it is later than that for is lost, a PTS step against the sample count. The mux's sink pad holds about two buffers before it stops the source task, so the mux task's waits spend the same slack. **As built:** both runners (`capture_rt.cpp` in mr-gst-runner, its twin inline in `gst-pipeline-runner.py`) mark, before PLAYING, every element from each `pipewiresrc` down to its first muxer (a factory of class Muxer: `mpegtsmux` in both captures), that muxer included, and connect to the bus's `stream-status` sync message; a pipeline without a `pipewiresrc` marks nothing and connects nothing. A marked element's task, as it enters (ENTER, on its own thread), hands its thread id to the main loop, which bounds RLIMIT_RTTIME to 200 ms when it is unlimited or higher (rtkit's RTTimeUSecMax, the value module-rt sets; a tighter limit is kept, as rtkit refuses an unbounded process) and asks rtkit on the system bus as module-rt does for the data loop: `MakeThreadRealtimeWithPID(pid, tid, 19)`, asynchronously, with a 5 s timeout, so neither a slow rtkit nor a wedged bus holds a task. audio-input-302m: the source task and the mux task; audio-encoder: also its encoder's task, behind the 50 ms leaky queue. A grant is one log line per task (`real-time: pipewiresrc0:src at SCHED_RR 19 (rtkit)`); a refusal (rtkit's error, no bus, no answer) is one warning per runner (`real-time priority refused for … (…): the capture runs at normal priority`), and the capture runs as before. The shared bus connection's exit-on-close is off, so a bus that goes away cannot SIGTERM the runner. Not raised: the bus egress after the mux (the tee, each consumer edge's queue task: stamped TS, where lateness costs latency only); mrtsrestamp's outage task (no pad, no stream-status; it acts on an outage only). aes67-input captures with `udpsrc`: no PipeWire capture. No flag. **Priority** SCHED_RR 19 (a call): below PipeWire's data loops (RR 20, rtkit's maximum, to which module-rt clamps its 83), so a cycle always preempts a capture task; above every SCHED_OTHER thread, which is all the task needs. Between the kernel's lowest RT threads (the GPU's job threads at FIFO 1 on the dev Pi's kernel; its IRQ threads run at 50, above both) and the data loops nothing else runs RT, so any value from 2 to 19 orders the same today; 19 keeps the audio capture directly under PipeWire. **Inside B-88's limits:** with its data loop a capture runner holds 3 rtkit threads (302M) or 4 (encoder), so the drop-in (`57a27e4`: 64 processes, 128 threads and 128 actions per 20 s per user; the daemons hold 3 and 6) takes a Master box's 12 audio-encoders (6 + 48) and up to 30 encoder runners; each RT thread keeps the 200 ms RLIMIT_RTTIME, so a task that runs 200 ms without sleeping is killed rather than starving the box, the bound B-88's data loop already has. | A capture's samples are lost when its source task runs later than its buffers last, and on a box this busy SCHED_OTHER gives no bound; the PTS are the cycle's, so nothing downstream mends a lost cycle. The mux task holds the source task back once its pads are full, and the encoder's task sits behind 50 ms of leaky queue: the source task alone would move the starvation there. rtkit is the route the image already proves for the daemons and B-88's data loop (polkit's group `audio`, the drop-in's limits). The request runs on the main loop, never on the task, so a capture starts at its own pace whatever rtkit does. Rejected: the source task alone (above); every task in the runner (the edges come after the restamp, and each consumer would add an rtkit thread); a synchronous request on the entering task (a bus that never answers holds it: `g_bus_get_sync` has no timeout); `nice` or a CPU weight (no deadline; no cpu controller under #748); `LimitRTPRIO` on the user units (the runner would set its own priority outside rtkit's bookkeeping, RLIMIT_RTTIME unbounded unless set, and module-rt would leave rtkit). | **Tests:** `gst_capture_rt_test.py` (new, 156 PASS): both runners over their protocol, a fake rtkit on a private dbus-daemon through `DBUS_SYSTEM_BUS_ADDRESS` that checks as rtkit does (a bounded RLIMIT_RTTIME, priority ≤ 20) and on a grant sets the thread itself, a real `pipewiresrc` on the dev Pi session's dummy sink (B-88's probe). The 302M and encoder shapes ask once per capture task and for no other, `MakeThreadRealtimeWithPID(runner pid, tid, 19)` with RLIMIT_RTTIME at 200 ms, and those threads alone run SCHED_RR 19 after the grant (`chrt -p`: `SCHED_RR\|SCHED_RESET_ON_FORK`, priority 19); a queue after the mux and a consumer edge attached later stay SCHED_OTHER and ask nothing; an `audiotestsrc` with the same tail asks nothing and leaves RLIMIT_RTTIME as it was; a refusal, no bus and an rtkit that never answers each give one warning (the last on the 5 s timeout, the capture flowing meanwhile), and the capture runs on; a tighter RLIMIT_RTTIME (100 ms) is kept and granted; the bus closing after the grants leaves the runner capturing. Mutants caught: 20 of 20, 10 per runner (every source marked, not only a `pipewiresrc`; only the source marked; the walk not ending at the muxer; priority 20; every refusal logged; RLIMIT_RTTIME not bounded; bounded over a tighter limit; raised at CREATE; the process id for the thread; exit-on-close left on). The dev Pi's own rtkit refuses this remote session through polkit (as B-88 found): one warning with rtkit's `AccessDenied`, the capture on. **Risks:** the source task takes the PipeWire thread loop's lock, which the plugin's SCHED_OTHER main loop holds while it dispatches a protocol event (rare once the node is on the data loop), and the mux task the restamp's stream lock, which the restamp's outage task takes for a tick about once a second: a short inversion each, inside the buffers. The capture's processing now takes its CPU before every ordinary thread: on .108 the source task ran 6.4 % and the mux task 3 % of a core per 302M capture (an encoder adds its codec), far from starving rtkit's canary (an ordinary thread its watchdog wants run once in 10 s). A raised thread keeps its priority when its task ends, and GStreamer's task pool could hand it to a later task; a capture runner's tasks end only at its stop, after which it exits. On stock rtkit (25 threads and 25 actions per 20 s per user, the daemons holding 6) the runners share 19, four per encoder runner and three per 302M capture: five encoders, seven 302M captures or a mix such as two encoders and four 302M captures run out, and the later requests are refused, the data loops' among them, so such a box can lose B-88's grant on a runner that B-88 alone gave it (it had room for 12): this needs the image with `57a27e4`, which the release's bundle carries. In the Python runner a Python probe on a raised task would wait for the interpreter lock; the one there, the egress tee's throughput probe, exists only without the stamper plugin, whose counter replaces it. **Device check** (DEV3 on .108, to do): lane-108b's loaded hour exactly (the same load, captures and taps, `tools/schedmon.sh`). Pass: V-P1-7 H1–H3; a1 against a2 within V-P1-7's bound; the source task's runnable wait under 1 %. Recorded: the mux task's wait, one rtkit grant per raised task in the journal, the runner's grant lines, the video player's 'can't keep up' polls against DEV2's 200 of 360. Texts: part 4.1's capture rows, V-P1-7, ADR-0029 (the capture thread's CPU line), `plugins/README.md` (linking a stream to device channels), the release notes. |
| B-112 | An SRT passphrase may contain any character: SRT Input and SRT Output put the passphrase and the stream ID into the `srt://` URI as typed, so a `#`, `&`, `\`, `%` or `"` in it cut it, changed it or failed the start without a word; RIST's passphrase and a link's CNAME the same way | Found 2026-10-24 by j2 (while building B-109), fixed 2026-10-26 by k2 (engineering fix; the calls below are engineering calls, for the owner's veto). **Seen:** `buildPipeline` of SRT Input and SRT Output wrote `streamid=` and `passphrase=` into `uri="srt://…?…"` as typed. GStreamer reads that URI as a URI (1.28.2, `gsturi.c`): the query ends at a `#`, splits at each `&` and then at the first `=`, and each value is percent-decoded; before that the launch-string parser ends the quoted `uri` at a `"` followed by a space and drops each `\`. So a `#` cut the passphrase and lost every parameter after it (SRT Input's key length among them), an `&` cut it, a `%` and two hex digits became another character, a `%` without them left no passphrase, a `\` was dropped and a `"` followed by a space failed the start; a stream ID the same (an access-control ID such as `#!::r=…,m=publish` was cut at its `#`). Nothing said so: two boxes cut a passphrase alike and could connect on what was left, while another make of encoder or decoder refused it as a wrong passphrase. Measured on the dev Pi (srtsrc and srtsink on loopback, the other end given the passphrase as typed): `#`, `&`, `%41` and `\` passed nothing; a space, `;`, `'` and a `"` with no space after it passed. **Checked, every other builder that puts free text into a URI:** RIST Input and RIST Output put a link's CNAME into its `rist://` URL as typed, and `mrristsrc` and `mrristsink` (C++, `mrrist_common.cpp`) folded the passphrase into each URL as `secret=`. librist splits a URL's query at each `&` and decodes nothing (`udpsocket_parse_url_parameters`; librist 0.2.7 on the dev Pi, the image's 5f6abd5), and the elements split their URL list at each space and comma. So a RIST passphrase was cut at its first `&` on both ends alike (measured: two that differ only after an `&` connected), and librist printed the part after it up to an `=` to the log as an unknown parameter (measured); a CNAME with a space or a comma split its URL in two and failed the start, one with an `&` was cut. The IP outputs put no free text into a URI (`udpsink host=… port=…`). A host or address field goes into a URI as typed, as before (an address, not free text). **Fix:** the SRT modules percent-encode the stream ID and the passphrase (`encodeURIComponent`, of the UTF-8 bytes), which srtsrc and srtsink decode back to what was typed, whatever it holds: `#`, `&`, `"`, a space, `;`, `%`, `+`, `=`, `?`, `/`, `\`, `'` and any character beyond ASCII. The RIST modules percent-encode a link's CNAME, and the elements decode it once librist has parsed the URL (a call); the elements put the passphrase on each peer's configuration whole and never into the URL (a URL that carries its own `secret=` keeps it, as before; librist keeps at most 127 bytes of it, as before). **With B-109:** the redaction reads the encoded passphrase as one value, so the log shows `passphrase=<redacted>` and nothing of it, after `?`, `&` or `;`; after a `;` the parameters that follow are kept (the assignment rule read on to the next space before); a name ending in `secretkey` is a secret (j2's review; `sig` and `pwd` stay over-redacted, harmless). **Mixed versions:** a link between two boxes whose SRT passphrase holds a `#`, an `&`, a `\` or a `%`, or whose RIST passphrase holds an `&`, ran on the cut or changed value (a stream ID is not checked between two boxes); after the update each end uses the value as typed, so update both ends together (or set the passphrase on both again). | A passphrase is typed by an operator, often generated, and shared with other makes of equipment: the box must use exactly what was typed, and a stream ID is often an access-control path. Percent-encoding is what the srt elements decode; librist decodes nothing, so its passphrase does not travel in a URL at all. | **Tests** (vitest): `SrtInputModule.test.ts` 24 → 41 and `SrtOutputModule.test.ts` 15 → 32 (each of 15 characters in a passphrase and a stream ID: the exact encoded URI, the values GStreamer's URI reading gives back, the logged form; B-109's cases on the encoded form; where GStreamer's srt elements are present, the builder's own element on loopback, `gst-launch-1.0`, against a peer given the passphrase as typed, every character at once, passes data, SRT Output's stream ID arrives whole, and a passphrase one character longer passes nothing); `RistInputModule.test.ts` 34 → 35 and `RistOutputModule.test.ts` 24 → 25 (a CNAME holding a space, a comma, an `&`, `%41` and `é`, encoded); `redact.test.ts` 57 → 62 (the encoded passphrase; after a `;`, encoded and not, the parameters after it kept; `secret_key` and `X-Secret-Key`); `runnerRedaction.test.ts` +1 case (an encoded passphrase through the start line, the pad-link rules, a runner line and the events). Python: `gst_mrrist_element_test.py` (the dataflow case with a passphrase holding a space, `&`, `=`, `#`, `%41`, `"`, `\` and `é` and a CNAME holding a space, a comma, `&`, `%41` and `é`, which the receiver names whole; two passphrases that differ only after an `&` pass nothing). Mutants caught (scratchpad wf13/k2): 14 of 14 (each SRT module's passphrase and stream ID raw, and one of each by `encodeURI`; each RIST module's CNAME raw; `secretkey` not an ending; no URI parameter after `;` (j2's surviving mutant); an assignment the URI rule redacted read again; in C++, the passphrase folded into the URL again, the CNAME not decoded, the passphrase on neither). **Device check** (DEV3, the Pi 5 test box, to run): a TEMP SRT Output and SRT Input pair with a generated passphrase holding a space, `;`, `#`, `&` and a quote connects and shows data; the box's journal shows `<redacted>` for it and holds none of it. Texts: this row and the intro, B-109's row (the names, the Limits), plugins/README.md (free text in a URI), the release notes (Fixed). |
| B-113 | Two Engine Comms listener applies that overlapped interleaved: one apply at a time now, and B-110's probe refined | Found 2026-10-24 by j1 and its review (pre-existing since #692), fixed 2026-10-26 by k2 (engineering fix; the calls below are engineering calls, for the owner's veto). **Seen** (in the code): `EngineConnectionManager.setListeners` ran each apply as it came, and nothing above it puts writes in order (two browsers, a script). A second apply made while the first was probing stopped the same server and started its own beside the first's: the sockets of one stayed bound, owned by no one, an engine able to connect to them; or the second failed, and its restore collided with the first's sockets. One made after the first had stopped the server found nothing started, swapped the set only and was answered as applied, while the first's set went live; one made during a restore did the same and left the restored server bound beside it. **Fix:** each apply runs after the one before has settled, on one promise (a call: in order, not coalesced to the latest set, so each write has its own answer, applied or refused with its error, and the stored set and the tree follow the live one in write order; coalescing would answer a skipped write as applied though it was never bound, and an apply takes about a second). A failed apply holds up none after it. B-110's restore holds: an apply made meanwhile waits for it and runs on the set it restored. Start and stop are not chained: the manager takes writes only once its listeners are up, and stops at shutdown. **B-110's probe, refined (j1's review; a behaviour change):** a move between two addresses on one port, neither of them all interfaces, now probes the new address with its port, so a program holding that address and port is refused while the engines are still connected (before, the address alone was probed, and the move failed after every engine had dropped, then restored); the address alone is probed only where all interfaces and an address would share the port, which Linux refuses while the live server holds it. `setListeners`' doc comment is 3 lines (j1's review). | Two people, or a person and a script, may apply at once: each must learn what happened to their own change, and the manager must hold exactly one set of listeners. | **Tests** (vitest, real sockets on the dev Pi): `EngineConnectionManager.test.ts` 9 → 15 (two overlapping applies end in the second set, nothing of the first left bound; an apply its probe refuses, then a good one, which applies; an apply made during a restore, which runs after it and leaves the restored port free; the same set applied twice, one rebind, the engine offline once; a move between two addresses with a program on the new one, refused before the live server is touched, no engine offline; moves between two addresses and to and from all interfaces spelled `0.0.0.0`). Mutants caught (scratchpad wf13/k2): 5 of 5 (no chain; a failure stalling the chain; B-110's probe as it was; a whole probe always; `0.0.0.0` spelled out not taken as all interfaces). **Device check** (DEV3, the Pi 5 test box, to run): two TEMP listener sets written at once over the tree both get an answer, the second set is live and nothing of the first stays bound (`ss -lun`); B-110's moves (DEV2b) as before. Texts: this row and the intro, B-110's row (the probe), ADR-0023 (the rebind bullet), FDS (Engine Comms, one clause). |
| B-114 | The engine's local API answers only the box itself: it listens on 127.0.0.1 and ::1, refuses any other peer and sends no CORS headers (the owner's decision) | **The owner**, 2026-10-24, verbatim: "Make it accessible from only the box itself. Remember that TEST-NET-3 routes to a loopback address on the box, so only allow from traffic originating from the box itself (if that would be a concern)." (The magic IP is an address the box holds on `lo`, from `media-router-audio-magic-ip.service`, which the site routers route to the box.) Built 2026-10-26 by k1; the calls below are engineering calls, for the owner's veto. **Seen:** `createApiServer` (`packages/engine/src/api/server.ts`) listened on `0.0.0.0` with `@fastify/cors` at `origin: true` and no login. **Callers** (inventoried before the change): the Device Manager's API, server side, at `http://localhost:3001/api/v1` (its Manager Profile page and its manager status), and nothing else. No browser page calls it: the Device Manager's app goes through its own API, the LCP and the dashboards use Socket.IO on :8081, the manager UI the manager's tree. Neither the ClarioCast app nor its proxy calls it, and no nginx vhost, unit or script on the image does. profile-manager is a placeholder whose dev-server proxy is the only thing that points at it; its build lands in /opt and nothing serves it. **Cause:** the listener stayed on all interfaces and CORS open to any origin, while the FDS's login for a peer that is not loopback (§7.1, §10.1.2) was never built. **Fix:** the server listens on 127.0.0.1 (Fastify) and ::1 (a second HTTP server on the same routes, Fastify's `routing`) and on nothing else, so no other address of the box is bound, the magic IP included. Fastify binds both only for `localhost`, which follows `/etc/hosts`: the image's hosts file gives both, the dev Pi's (127.0.0.1 named `mr-test`) ::1 alone, so both are named (a call). A host without IPv6 (`::1` refused with EADDRNOTAVAIL or EAFNOSUPPORT) starts on 127.0.0.1 alone and logs it once. Any other error on `::1` (EADDRINUSE: another program there) fails the start, as one on 127.0.0.1 does, after 127.0.0.1 is closed (a call: that program would otherwise answer whoever reaches `localhost` as ::1). Every request whose peer is not loopback (127.0.0.0/8, ::1, ::ffff:127.0.0.0/104) gets 403 with no body, on any path, an unknown one included, before any handler runs. The peer is the raw socket's address, never a forwarded header, so a DNAT to loopback is refused too. A refused peer is logged (`Local API refused a request from another host`, with its address) at most once a minute per address. CORS is gone and with it `@fastify/cors` (the engine was its only user; the lockfile drops it and `fastify-plugin`): every caller is server side, and no response carries an `Access-Control-*` header. **Limit:** anything on the box that forwards requests to the API (a proxy, a tunnel route) is the box itself to the check. None in the repo does, and a Cloudflare tunnel's routes, which are set in Cloudflare, must not lead to port 3001. | The owner's decision. The API's one caller runs on the box, so no other host needs it. A listener on loopback alone is out of every other host's reach, the magic IP included, and the peer check still holds if traffic is ever redirected to loopback. The URS's remote access with a login (UR-API-008 and -009, UR-SEC-031 and -034) stays unbuilt. | **Tests** (vitest): `server.test.ts` 13 → 25, now on the real `createApiServer` with a stand-in engine (its 13 route cases ran on a copy of the routes before): it listens on 127.0.0.1 and ::1 only (read from `/proc/net/tcp` and `tcp6`, as `ss -ltn` shows them), and the host's own LAN address does not connect; 127.0.0.1, another address in 127/8, ::1 and ::ffff:127.0.0.1 are served (inject's `remoteAddress`), and real sockets on 127.0.0.1 and ::1 are served; a private address (10/8), the magic IP, the IPv4-mapped form of each and an IPv6 documentation address get 403 with no body on seven requests (health, the profile list, a profile added, activated and deleted, an engine stop, an unknown path) and no handler runs; a forwarded header changes nothing either way; no response carries an `Access-Control-*` header; a cross-origin preflight is not granted (404); a refused peer is logged once per address and minute (on a fake clock since 2026-10-27, k1's review: none at 59 s, again at 61 s, none at 62 s, so a window of 1 s or 2 min fails it, where the first form let a 1 s one pass); a host without IPv6 (EADDRNOTAVAIL, EAFNOSUPPORT) starts on 127.0.0.1 alone with one warning; another program on ::1's port fails the start and leaves 127.0.0.1 free; a close closes both listeners. Mutants caught (scratchpad wf13/k1): 13 of 13 (the brief's four: the host back to 0.0.0.0, the peer check removed, the IPv4-mapped form not matched, CORS registered again; and a forwarded header read, a host without IPv6 failing, ::1 not bound, every refusal logged, 127.0.0.1 alone taken as loopback, 127.0.0.1 left bound after a failed start, ::1 not closed, any ::ffff: address taken as loopback, one log window for all addresses). **Device check** (DEV3, .103, to run): `ss -ltn` shows 3001 on 127.0.0.1 and ::1 only; from the dev Pi `curl -m 3 http://<box>:3001/api/v1/health` fails; on the box `curl http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/v1/health` answers and the same call to the magic IP fails; the Device Manager's Manager Profile page lists, adds, edits and activates a TEMP profile as before (removed after). Texts: this row and the intro, FDS §7.1 and §10.1.2 (as built), README.md and plugins/README.md (the port tables), B-109's row (the listener), the release notes (Fixed). The Yocto recipe's comment on the engine's ports (`media-router.bb`) is in the Yocto repo and unchanged. |

| B-116 | The gate feed's late bursts at three points of its 150 s holding loop (#847; B-99's cycle traced to the gate) | Measured 2026-10-23 to 2026-10-26, read only (the stall notes, scratchpad wf12/stall150: the receivers' journals and polls, the gate's journal, its module chain read from the manager's database, a CPU sample on the gate). **Seen:** NO-OCC-Gate01's feed is a 150 s holding loop played upstream of the gate (the OCC's; its phase moved +17 s twice with nothing on the gate changing, and the gate's own simulator loop runs at 428 s). At three fixed points of each loop every RIST output of the gate runs up to about 0.75 s late, then bursts: TECH01's relay and the Pi 5 test box's two gate pulls show each event at the same gate second, a receiver's buffer later, as a RIST receiver releases at the sender's stamps plus its buffer. The gate's ingest is clean at those seconds: its TS Splitter's input rate is flat (28.6 Mbps, 0.07 % spread in 2 s windows) and its teletext cues keep their 2.64 s cadence to within a frame. The late outputs come from both of the gate's video transcoders (the English and the French one), and each decodes the same source in software on one core: their CPU Decode Threading is set to Single core, against the default Multi-core. **Ruled out** (2026-10-26, a read-only CPU sample of the gate over three loops): the transcoders' CPU. The box was at most 24 % busy and no thread went above about half a core, so Multi-core decode would not change the bursts. **Seen in that sample:** both transcoders' work rises and falls in lockstep at the loop's event points. **Our side:** at those events a receiver's ingest restamp steps its envelope in answer to the source (B-95's window rule then holds the bursts' height, the stutter at its lock is those steps), and B-83's fades smooth the edges where a mixer input drops out. | The bursts are in the gate's send timing and common to every output, so a receiver can only absorb them; which stage makes them decides where the fix goes, the OCC source or the gate. | **Open** (#847). The cause lies between the OCC source's video timing inside its constant-rate stream at the loop's joins (the decoders work less there, then catch up in a burst) and the gate's shared GPU encoder stalling at those content points (four 50 fps hardware encodes, which CPU statistics do not show). The decisive test is a short passive capture of the gate's input at an event, the video PID's PTS against the PCR, which needs the owner's OK for a tap on the gate. Until then a test receiver keeps its margin with its input's settings: B-95's Smoothing Cooldown holds the bursts' full height once they have stepped it, and a positive Ingest Offset of about their height (0.75 s) lands its content late enough that a late burst still arrives in time downstream (an engineering call for a test box; on a production receiver the owner's). The decode threading is left as the gate has it. No release-notes line (nothing changed). |

The prototype's sweep, 1 h each on 48 kHz exact, 44.1 kHz quantised at two offsets, 44.1 kHz MP2, 32 kHz, Opus and a ±1-tick wobble: no count from 3 to 30 engages a house-rate stream (\|ε\| at most 9 ppb once locked); +3 ppm engages at 18.0 s with 3 buckets, 25.0 s with 10, 31.0 with 15, 46.0 with 30 (the capture lock). 10, not the smallest: a ±0.2 ms PTS wobble lifts \|ε\| to 0.86 ppm with 3 (past the bound, held off only by the hold) and 0.20 ppm with 10, and the device lock shares the configuration. **Engage** (C-7's 0.5 ppm, 1 ms, 10 s): the phase is the lock's content time of the next frame less the counter from the epoch's first PTS; engaged once \|ε\| has stayed past the bound for 10 s of lock (+3 ppm: 25.0 s) or the phase passes 1 ms (+40 ppm: 24.9 s; +0.3 ppm: 55.4 min). Passing (bypassed at equal rates without a device term), each buffer leaves as it came, the same buffer and memory; an engage resets the resampler, feeds it the last 64 passed frames at the commanded rate and drops as many outputs, so its next output is the engaging buffer's first frame (⅛ frame early, where GStreamer's resampler centres every output; its first 64 frames within 0.0002 of full scale of the source's, where an unprimed filter's read 0.01 to 0.11 off with the tone's phase), labelled with its PTS, no DISCONT. Where a resampler already runs (a rate conversion, a device term) the engage only hands the ratio to the servo, its counter continuing and its phase (up to 1 ms) steered out with τ = 10 s. **Breaks:** at a GAP event and before a DISCONT buffer the element ends the epoch (`end_epoch`): the resampler's tail leaves on the old counter and is reset, the lock relocks without its rate, and the next buffer opens an epoch at its PTS (`relock`, its jump against the tail's end, negative when the timeline steps back). An envelope step (the timeline moved, not the content) re-anchors the labels on the lock's new floor and keeps the resampler and the state. **Device term:** at READY→PAUSED the element downstream named `device-sink` must be a `GstAudioBaseSink` with `slave-method=custom`, else an error naming it; its custom-slaving callback feeds `AsrcDeviceLock` (on the decode lock's configuration) and answers `requested_skew` 0; the transform reads the device ε atomically; the output counter runs on from the first PTS, re-anchored at a DISCONT or GAP (device-time labels); a sink discontinuity relocks the device lock keeping its rate (`mrasrc-event` `device-relock`, its reason). Found building it: (1) the sink reads `etime`, then `itime`, so a preemption between the two reads makes a pair early, which the lower envelope follows (one pair 0.48 ms early held the device rate 6 ppm off for a minute): the callback reads the house clock again and places the pair there, the latest instant `itime` can have been read, so every pair is late; (2) the sink's first callback after its calibration reads the device up to 0.33 ms early: a (re)lock's first 100 ms of pairs are left out. On the same readings either rule left out leaves the rate 11–14 ppm off at 15–30 s, both within 0.04 ppm. the ring's fill against the device model's own play position, so no read races the ring's advance, each 5 s window keeping its top, its most punctual render's, with their percentiles; resyncs, the provided clock's calibration changes, underruns) and `MrTestClock` (`speed` times real time, its waits in its own time); Phase 4 reuses both. **Engine:** `buildAsrc` gains `bypassBelowPpm` (above 0, at most 1,000) and `deviceSink`. **Found:** `cap-mux-align7-aac-opus`'s AAC, the brief's house-rate decode, is not one: its timeline steps back 14–18 ms inside its segments around B-121's two 100 ms gaps (its Opus is exact), so the element's house-rate decodes are `tp-hevc-aac`, `cap-mux-align7`'s Opus and a 35 s `avenc_aac` encode (and its `fixture_gen --respace 40` copy for the foreign case); `ModuleTimingInput.demux?`, `.clockCorrection?`; `ModuleTimingSummary.clockCorrection?`, `.deviceClockPpm?`): per input Demux rate (PES/s from the `pes` deltas over the last 10 s of interval reports, by arrival, from the second report), Demux gaps (holes: a jump or a marker; a sparse pad's filler GAPs are not counted by the core), Demux CC lost (packets) and Demux unknown streams (the current program's, not the cumulative counter, which counts each plan's again); Clock correction `none (house rate)` or `+23.4 ppm (source)` (source-ppb, positive fast) on the input row of an ASRC placed on one, else on the `timing` section; Device clock `−12.1 ppm` (device-ppb) on the `timing` section; a ppm change of 0.1 or a counter's is a change for the throttle. `mode` reads `device` for a decode + device ASRC whose source still passes (B-125), so the terms are read off the description at start (`launchElements`: `bypass-below-ppm` > 0 a decode term, `device-sink` a device term; a live branch's ASRC by its mode alone); so is a demux's `media`, which its message does not carry (`select` it does). **Which input:** the module's `demuxInputOf(element)` (`{ tap }`, `{ connection }`, `{ port }` (the one connection on that sink port), `{ label }`, `null`), else the engine's rule: an element named for a bus connection (`…_<shortHash(connectionId)>`, as the live fan-in branches' demuxes are) serves that edge, else a demux serves the module's one input (the tap that reports, whatever its name) and an ASRC the module; a demux with no place has a row of its own. mpegts-muxer maps `demux_<i>` to branch i's tap; audio-processing and audio-output-302m, whose fan-ins name a static branch's demux by its place (`<mixer>_demux<i>`), map them by connection through audio-302m-core's `mixInputDemuxes` (the names built by the fan-in's own rule; no string changes); the subtitle renderers (video-player, transcoder) map `subdemux` to Subtitles In and their own demux to their video input through subtitle-core's `renderDemuxInput`; audio-mixer and n1-mixer-302m need nothing (live branches, the engine's rule). **Log:** a demux-mode program after the first (generation > 0) is `Input <n>: program changed (generation g)` (info, with pads and PCR PID); select mode has no generation (−1). A consumer ASRC's events are lines of their own, an engage `Input <n>: source clock +x ppm: resampling` (part 10), `ratio-out-of-bounds` at warn. **Warnings**, owned by the module, one health text with the aligners' (the first part's kind owns it; taken only over ok or its own text, ADR-0010 rule 2; never over a stopped or errored module, where the aligners' rule took a directly set error back while its latch stood): `demux-unknown-stream` `Input <n>: PID 0x0123: stream type 0x06 with no known descriptor is not demuxed` (a registration named when there is one, "no known descriptor" only for 0x06); `input-not-house-time` `Input <n> is <x> s off house time — its producer does not stamp house time` (the furthest PID of the input); `input-no-stream` `Input <n> carries no audio stream` (the kind from `select`, `302M audio` for the 302M fan-ins, or `media`; none named for every class); `asrc-out-of-bounds` `Input <n>: source clock +x ppm off house time, past the ASRC's 1000 ppm — check the source's sample rate` (no input named for the module's own ASRC). Cleared: each at the demux's next generation (a re-plan posts the new program's unknown streams ahead of its program message, so those stay; not-house-time carries no generation and is held to the demux's latest), a module start, a respawn (the generation or `pes` back down), or the element going quiet (6 s); no-stream also once a report says the stream is found; out-of-bounds once a stats report has the source locked and below 900 ppm, the element's own hysteresis (it posts no end, and a relock keeps its flag, so a relock clears nothing). **Protocol:** `plugins/mpegts-core/tests/fixtures/forwarded-messages.json` holds one payload per reason and kind as both runners forward them (recorded from mrtsdemux-messages and mrasrc-device; both gave the same); the engine's tests feed it through the readers, and the two protocol cases hold every forwarded payload to its entry's fields and their types (the engine's shape). mrasrc-device runs without `busReports` and waits for the second stats post instead of 6 s (p3-5's carried minor; | B-161 | WI-P4-3, prototype first (p4-3a): VideoPace's Python reference, the rules `mrvideopace` will run | Orchestrator's plan (scratch wf13/p4plan: E1, E2, E11; the owner's OQ-1), built by p4-3a (2026-10-26); the cadence hold is chapter 13.6's engineering choice and the deviations below are engineering calls, all for the owner's veto. **As built:** `plugins/mpegts-core/py/video_pace.py`, never loaded (ADR-0029 choice 1), integer ns throughout (arrivals and releases on the element clock, PTS only differenced) so the C++ port agrees exactly: `VideoPace(gap_threshold_ns)` with `on_frame(pts, dur, arrival, discont) → (release, rate_drop)`, `on_gap()`, `set_display(period, source)` (`measured`, `nominal`, `none`) and `take()` (released, late, rate-drops, gaps-collapsed, the content and display periods, the display source, the mean hold since the last take); `display_period_from_feedback(pairs)` and `display_period_from_returns(times, prior)`, each giving the period and a `short` flag (under 60 s of steps); run as a script it replays a recorded call sequence, one JSON object per line, in the line format p4-3b's `mrts_cli pace` reads. **Cadence** (chapter 8 part 4.2): Δ_k = p_k − p_(k−1) when 0 < Δ_k ≤ min(`gap-threshold-ms` 250, 4 × nominal) and no GAP or DISCONT came since the last frame, else the nominal duration (the buffer's, else the caps', else the content period); r_k = max(a_k, r_(k−1) + Δ_k). A GAP, a DISCONT, a step back or a step past the threshold collapses (`gaps-collapsed`), so the backlog drains into it; a repeated PTS (B-160's F7: a decoder holds a decreasing PTS) takes the nominal uncounted. `late` counts a frame not collapsed whose arrival set its release: its lateness stepped up there. The content period is the median (index n/2 of the sorted values) of the last 120 clean deltas: reported, the nominal's fallback and the nominal band's reference. **Rate match** (S11): decimation always on a measured period (no dead band), on a nominal one only past 0.05 %, never with none, by an accumulator L, the display's lag behind the content in ns: at each frame L = max(L − Δ_k, −w_k) (0 for a collapsed frame), the frame dropped when L ≥ w_k, else kept and L += T_d, w_k the nominal duration (Δ_k while it is 0). A dropped frame keeps its slot in the cadence, so what is dropped never moves what is kept. **Display period** (S12): from feedback, Δt/Δseq summed over the steps between consecutive presented samples whose own Δt/Δseq lies within 10 % of the median step's; from a blocking sink's returns, each interval counted as round(interval / base) refreshes, the base the mode's refresh when given, else the mean of the intervals within 10 % of the smallest (the plan's rule), an interval off every multiple by more than 10 % left out, the period their sum over their refreshes. **Found, and built otherwise than the plan:** (D1) the plan's accumulator, (T_d − T_c)/T_c per kept frame with T_c the median, is this one with every delta equal to the median, and the median loses a source's clock: the virtual STC maps a source onto house time with its rate, the bus carries 90 kHz ticks, and a source 30 ppm fast arrives as 1800-tick deltas with a 1799 every ≈ 18.5 frames, whose median is 1800. On a display 40 ppm slow the median form sees a 40 ppm deficit where 70 ppm is: 7 drops in the hour where 12.6 are due, and the display's lateness grows 112 ms (case 13). Each frame's own delta keeps the clock, the ticks' rounding cancelling in the sum. (D2) The lag may run one frame below 0, never more and not across a collapse: a display faster than the content repeats frames and banks a frame at most. Without a floor 10 min of 50p on a 60 Hz display bank 100 s and the next hour of 60p drops nothing (+144 ms, case 14); the frame of credit kept across the switch's DISCONT costs a drop and +27 ms there. (D3) The decision reads content time, never a release: a sink that blocks (kmssink at its vblank, 0008 while the display is behind) feeds its own slowness back into the releases, and a lag summed from release intervals never drops (60p into a 50 Hz kmssink: 12 s behind after 72 s, case 2). (D4) A frame released at its arrival after a collapse is lateness falling into a gap, so it is not `late` (the plan counted every r_k = a_k > r_(k−1) + Δ_k). (D5) Presented samples across an output switched off whose MSC stood still, or across an MSC reset, would read the outage as refreshes: such steps are left out. E = F − m; alone δ* = clamp(E / 30 s, 0, 0.5 %), slewed at 500 ppm/s (a DISCONT or GAP steps it), engaged at 20 ms and let go at 5 ms; no drain until 30 s were sampled since a window clear (a device relock or stall's flush, caps, a flush, PAUSED; not a DISCONT, GAP or outage), nor while an audio starvation runs, nor for 30 s after one. **The margin:** audio and video start at their floors, 20 ms and 1 frame (fix round 1: the design's 60 ms and 2 frames sat above the live trough, about 0 at this head, so a drain ended that far above where the link had played), ceiling 500 ms; an audio starvation (the sink's own, below) of at most 250 ms raises it at its end whatever the drain did (B3), longer is an outage (counted, no raise); a video release past its drained slot raises it only while δ > 0 or within 30 s after (B4), one more than 250 ms late is an outage, one under a quarter frame late is the release's jitter (no underrun, no raise: fix round 1; seen 15 µs to 3.2 ms, which raised the player's margin 40 → 80 → 160 ms while it drained and left the group 120 ms up); late frames within 1 s are one episode. What the queue is for: the thread boundary that keeps a stall of the bus egress off srtsrc's thread, on which the restamp reads arrival at chain entry (OQ-19), and a stop for an output that no longer drains. Back-pressure (`buildBackpressureQueue`) would hold srtsrc and the restamp through a stall past its bound: everything behind it arrives late by the stall, which the clock reads as an envelope step and relocks on (the lane saw a relock on a 41.5 ms one), and libsrt, whose ARQ runs on its own threads, fills its receive buffer and then drops what it counts as network loss. The other ingests: RIST Input's queue was bounded by bytes alone (4 MiB, leaky, its sheds uncounted); MPEG-TS IP Input's is `buildBackpressureQueue(jitterMs)`, non-leaky on udpsrc's arrival stamps, and never sheds; the HLS Player has no GStreamer queue on its output (`mr-bus-fanout` sheds per consumer by age, counted as "shed buffers"). **As built:** `buildIngestQueue()` (`tsHelpers.ts`), `queue name=ingestq leaky=2 max-size-time=0 max-size-buffers=0 max-size-bytes=4000000 flush-on-eos=true`: 500 ms at 64 Mbit/s (`tsQueueByteCap`, the bus edge queue's byte cap), 800 ms at 40 Mbit/s, 1.14 s at 28 Mbit/s, in SRT Input and RIST Input. mr-gst-runner's `shed_watch.cpp` counts each buffer that meets a queue named `ingestq…` full (its `overrun`: with a byte bound and buffers of one size, one shed buffer each, and one too many when the output resumes as the last is signalled) and emits one plugin event `queue_shed` per episode (an episode ends after 1 s without an overrun; one still open at 10 s is reported once as it stands, and one open at a stop is reported then), which `GstPluginBase` writes as one WARN line ("Queue ingestq full: N buffers dropped in T ms (its output stopped draining)"). with several programs, a waiting program's PES records are written when they go on, after other programs' records of the meantime, so such a trace may replay a few PES misplaced (one program replays as recorded); what waits at EOS is not pushed (at most 300 ms of one program); a PMT version change during a wait applies before what waited. Found 2026-10-28 by W6's p3-13 builder (B-139, "Not this item, measured"), fixed the same day by c8 (the orchestrator's call, engineering calls for the owner's veto). **Seen:** a 50 fps `videotestsrc` into `videorate drop-only=true ! video/x-raw,framerate=25/1` gave 50 of 100 frames with timestamp-offset 0 and 100 of 100 with a 1 h offset, and the transcoder's string with a 12 fps rendition fed a 25 fps fixture passed 200 of 200 frames (p3-13). c8 again, frames from an appsrc on a segment from 0: from 1 h and from 10^6 s, 100 of 100 out at 25, 50 and 12 fps; from 0, 50, 100 and 24. Through the transcoder's own description on both runners (protocol case TR, 25i H.264 deinterlaced to 50p, a 25 fps rendition): 198 and 199 of 200 fields out, 20 ms apart. x264enc as a VBR rendition of 1,200 kbit/s sets it (ultrafast, GOP Length 50), 10 s of 50 fps 640x360 noise into 25 fps: 500 frames encoded, 2,430 kbit/s, 10 keyframes and 1.89 s of encode CPU, against 250, 1,229 kbit/s, 5 and 1.02 s with the fix. **Cause:** in drop-only mode videorate keeps each input PTS and passes a frame whose PTS is at or past its next slot (`gstvideorate.c` 1.28.2:2047-2056), the slot one output frame on from the base for each frame passed (853-858, PTS left as they came at 873-880); without skip-to-first the base is the segment's start (`gst_video_rate_compute_next_ts`, 1882-1884). The transcoder runs with base time 0 and its decoded frames carry house time, the box's uptime (3.4 × 10^6 s on the dev Pi; the transform retime puts every access unit on K + its PES), while tsdemux's segment starts at 0 (the bus input's TIME segment, copied in `tsdemux.c`'s `calculate_and_push_newsegment`): every frame is past its slot, and the grid, one slot per frame passed, would catch up only after as long as the house time again, so it never dropped (the 2026-09-16 comment at `transcoderPipeline.ts` named the same condition for its dup storm). The Video Encoder runs on a natural base time (`liveCaptureClock`, `VideoEncoderModule.ts`:287; chapter 4.6 keeps it): its capture PTS start near 0, so its drop-only conformed after a catch-up of about its first frame's running time; measured with a live 50 fps source into its raw tail, 25.00 fps out with the old string (50.00 on a pinned base, 25.00 there with the fix). **Fix (as built):** `videorate drop-only=true skip-to-first=true` on the transcoder's string (`transcoderPipeline.ts`) and on both of the encoder's (`videoEncoderPipeline.ts`: the raw tail and the MJPG pre-drop); the comments keep drop-only's reason, say why skip-to-first is there, and no longer say a slower source is delivered at its rate (see Limits). No flag. | skip-to-first anchors the grid on the first frame the element sees, whatever the base time: base_output_ts, base_input_ts and next_output_ts take its PTS (1870-1879), so drops are judged on the stream's own times. drop-only stays: nothing is ever duplicated (the 2026-09-16 dup storm), and the decision keeps zero latency. On the encoder it changes nothing measurable on this line and makes its conform independent of its base time. | **What happens now (measured, 50 fps in):** the first frame passes and sets the grid. A forward PTS jump of J passes every frame for about J × D_in / (D_out − D_in) of input (J at 50 to 25 fps: 1 s, then the rate; 75 of the 100 frames after a 1 s jump, 10 frames at full rate after 200 ms), never a duplicate. A step back of B with no flush or new segment drops every frame for B (1 s: 50 frames, a 1 s freeze), a step of one frame (a re-sent PTS) that frame alone; a FLUSH, or a segment whose start moves past the grid, re-anchors on the next frame (no run of drops with the PTS 1 s back); an identical segment changes nothing; an input DISCONT is not read (its flag is set or cleared on the frames passed, 809-813). On this line no step back reaches the transcoder's videorate: the ingest restamp writes no PES behind its PID's last (`ts_restamp.cpp`:804-806, R18), the transform retime keeps every access unit on its content time across a source rewind (protocol case M), the decoder raises a decreasing PTS to the last one (`gstvideodecoder.c`:3183-3191) and the deinterlace guard drops re-sent fields (#817); the last field a stop drains, 20 ms behind the one before, now goes too (case TR's egress stepped back there with the old string). A forward jump comes with an outage of the input: after one of J a rendition below the source's rate sends every frame for about J. The encoder's v4l2src (meta-custom's patch) follows a driver timeline that moves back for good by less than 100 ms: at most that long of drops, once. **Limits:** a source slower than the target was not delivered at its rate, as the comments said, but refused at negotiation, as before: in drop-only mode videorate's source caps offer only rates up to the input's (490-538, 529-532), so 25 fps into a 50 fps string stopped "not-negotiated" (also behind x264enc ! avdec_h264; without drop-only it plays). A Video Transcoder at 50 fps (the default) fed 1080p25 or 720p25, a 29.97 or 59.94 source set to 30 or 60, and a Video Encoder whose capture rate is below the request (raw takes the mode's nearest rate, MJPG the next above, else the nearest) did not start: B-188 (2026-10-29) fixes it, the caps naming the set rate, then a range up to it, so such a source runs at its own rate. GOP Length counts frames at the set rate (50 frames = 2 s at 25 fps), as its description says: with the bug a 25 fps rendition of a 50p source made a keyframe every second. Found on the way, not this item: the encoder writes a raw mode's V4L2 fourcc as the GStreamer format, so a YUYV or YU12 mode gives `format=YUYV` or `format=YU12`, which no element accepts (GStreamer's names are YUY2 and I420; checked: it cannot link); B-189 (2026-10-29) fixes it. **Tests:** vitest: `transcoderPipeline.test.ts` (+1: one drop-only videorate with skip-to-first under auto, force and off deinterlacing and with burn-in; 3 strings), the golden strings (their header says so), `TranscoderModule.test.ts` (+1: the file snapshot `plugins/transcoder/tests/videorate-plan.json`, the module's description at 25 and 50 fps for one 320x180 rendition on arm64 without a hardware scaler, `@SOCK@` for the socket directory, `vitest -u` rewrites it), `videoEncoderPipeline.test.ts` (+2: every videorate, the MJPG pre-drop's too; the file snapshot `plugins/video-encoder/tests/videorate-strings.json`, NV12 and MJPG 50 fps modes at 25 and 50; 9 strings), `VideoEncoderModule.test.ts` (1 string): the two plugins 166 → 170 tests. Protocol case TR (`native_runner_protocol_test.py`, 14 checks, both runners): the module's description from the snapshot, fed 4 s of x264enc 25i H.264 (320x192, top field first) stamped as a contract producer's egress, its rendition's egress attached: at 25 fps 100 of the 200 fields, every step 3,600 ticks; at 50 fps 198 or 199, steps 1,800 (and 3,600); the protocol test 524 → 538 checks. On 726b7c42's strings every 25 fps check fails (the suite: 100 of 100, 20 ms apart; TR: 198 and 199 of 200). **Mutants,** 6 of 6 caught: skip-to-first left out of the transcoder's string (vitest 8, suite 2, TR 6), of the encoder's raw tail (vitest 9, suite 2), of the MJPG pre-drop (vitest 5, suite 2); drop-only left out of each (vitest 8, 9 and 5; the suite's forward jump: 150 of 100 with repeats, twice, and 76 with repeats; TR passes, it has no jump). **Device check** (next round): the Pi 5 test box, a TEMP Video Transcoder on the gate pull (1080i) with one 640x360 25 fps rendition: 25 frames a second out (`record-bus`, PES per second) and the runner's CPU against DEV4a's 1.45–1.94 cores; the Pi 4 test box, a TEMP Video Encoder on the ATEM's USB video at 25 fps: the capture's own rate first (`v4l2-ctl`), then 25 frames a second out and its CPU against DEV4a's ~1.07 core (no change expected: its base time is natural). **Phase 3 line:** the same strings (p3w3 `transcoderPipeline.ts`:236, `videoEncoderPipeline.ts`:104 and :131) under the same condition (mrtsdemux's segment from 0 with house-time PTS): the fix goes there at the next carry merge, as B-139 notes, with the snapshots, the suite and case TR (its description then without `alignBranchesToStamps`, which B-139 deletes).
