Found on the Phase 3 line by W5's p3-14 builder (`7dd83eaf`, its row B-134: "A 302M input dark for more than 5 s would have met the same since Phase 2; no test reaches it"); reproduced on this line and ported 2026-10-28 by c9 (engineering calls, for the owner's veto). **Seen** (this line's build on the Pi 5 dev box, load under 0.5; notes in scratch wf13/rcbatch2/c9, data in `mr-captures/wf13/c9`): the fan-in branch from its demux on, as `build302mMixBranch` makes it (`mrtsdemux select=audio/x-smpte-302m ! avdec_s302m ! audioconvert ! audioresample ! audio/x-raw,rate=48000,channels=2 ! mralignwatch … hold-on-eos=true`), fed a remote's 302M TS whose link drops 6 s while the remote encodes on, as an SRT or RIST link that drops does. The first thing back is the demux's GAP over the hole, from the last PES's end to the new PES (`ts_select.cpp`:195-196; a bus gap marker gives the same GAP, :237), and `avdec_s302m` passes it on as it came (no PLC, `gstaudiodecoder.c` 1.28.2:2270ff). Every run where that GAP came first read level-time 6,000 ms (6,020 on the runner) in the input's return report, against its 5,000 ms bound: the element test's rig, Audio Processing's shape and the audio mixer's own start command on the native runner. That reads as full only when the next PES reaches the aligner before its task has taken the GAP, 0.25-0.5 ms after it (the decode between them). At a pace no longer than the returning input's own lag, the first PES back ended at the horizon and was discarded before the full check (the mix had the input again 10 ms after its return): never full in 62 runs. At the 300 ms pace a later input sets, a `full` report came at the return in 1 of 10 runs on the idle 4-core box, 10 of 10 with the demux's thread and the aligner's task on one core, and 2 of 6 runs of the audio mixer's own start command (`fixtures/aligner/pipelines.json` mixer2 on the native runner, unixfd edges, the other input delivered 300 ms late). A `full` report makes the module's health a warning, "Input <name> queue full — upstream held", until a report reads half that level, about a second (`alignerWatches.ts`:147-156, `latenessReporter.ts`:327-330, `GstPluginBase.ts`:431-442); the input's thread waits until the task takes the GAP, far less than the pace its data waits anyway, so its sound was mixed again from its return in every rig run, with a `full` report or without. **Paths on this line:** every 302M fan-in aligner (`audio302mHelpers.ts`:214, through `build302mMixBranch`:223): an Audio Output (302M) with two or more sources (`AudioOutput302mModule.ts`:194; one source has no aligner), the Audio Mixer (`audioMixerPipeline.ts`:60, every source), the N-1 Audio Mixer (302M)'s input fan-ins (`n1Mixer302mPipeline.ts`:177) and Audio Processing's with two or more sources (`audioProcessingPipeline.ts`:103 and :116); also Audio Processing's per-channel aligners into its interleave (:81) behind a single-source programme, since deinterleave passes the GAP to every channel (both read 6,000 ms, 10 of 10). Not met: the N-1 mixer's matrix links (`n1Mixer302mPipeline.ts`:148), fed by the input mixers' continuous output; the MPEG-TS Muxer's routes (`mpegtsMuxerPipeline.ts`:116), whose tsdemux 1.28.2 makes only zero-length GAPs, (0, 0) on a sparse pad and (PCR − 800 ms, 0) to a stalled stream (`tsdemux.c`:2413, 2507 and 3120), which the retime lets through as they are (`branch_retime.cpp`:608-617): no span to count (on the Phase 3 line the muxer's mrtsdemux in demux mode makes the long GAP, p3-14's case); the Video Player has no aligner on this line. **Cause:** `aw_level_time` counted from the first timed item's start, here the GAP's, though `aw_release` clips a GAP at the horizon (or drops it whole): what lies behind the horizon is never queued time. **Fix (as built):** `7dd83eaf`'s hunk, byte for byte but the comment's row tag: the level counts from the later of that start and the planner's horizon (`gstmralignwatch.cpp` `aw_level_time`); `plugins/README.md`'s queue sentence says so, as there. | B-188 | A Video Transcoder rendition or a Video Encoder whose source is slower than its Frame Rate stopped "not-negotiated" and restarted over and over: a drop-only videorate offers no rate above its input's, and the caps after it named the set rate alone (c8's finding, B-186's limits) | Release line (v2.0.0.100). Found 2026-10-28 by c8 (B-186's limits), fixed 2026-10-29 by c10 (a range, the orchestrator's call; its form, and the rest, engineering calls, for the owner's veto). **Seen** (c8): 25p H.264 into the transcoder's 50 fps description on the native runner gave no frame, an "Internal data stream error" and "streaming stopped, reason not-negotiated (-4)", with B-186's string and without. c10, frames from an appsrc at house time on a segment from 0, under the dev Pi's videorate (Debian's 1.22.0, which the gate's suites load: the 1.28.2 install there carries no videorate) and under the image's 1.28.2 (its release tarball's `gstvideorate.c`, built into a private plugin directory for this): with the set rate alone, 25 fps into 50, 29.97 into 30, 59.94 into 60, 24 into 25, 23.976 into 24 and 12.5 into 25 all stop not-negotiated, and x264enc and x265enc behind it get no caps. **Cause:** in drop-only mode videorate's source caps are its input's rate, then the range from 0 up to it (`gst_video_rate_transform_caps`, `gstvideorate.c` 1.28.2:490-538, the range at 529-532), so caps that name a higher rate alone meet nothing. The Video Transcoder's Frame Rate defaults to 50 (24, 25, 30, 50 or 60), so a 25p source failed at the default; the Video Encoder captures a raw mode at its rate nearest the request and an MJPG one at the lowest rate above it, else the nearest, so a device whose picked rate was below the request did the same. **Fix (as built):** the caps after each videorate name the set rate, then a range up to it: `video/x-raw,framerate=N/1;video/x-raw,framerate=[1/1,N/1]`, written inline in the description (`gst_parse_launch` takes it, on both runners), on the transcoder's string (`transcoderPipeline.ts`, `rateCaps`) and on the Video Encoder's two (`videoEncoderPipeline.ts`, `rateCaps()`: its raw tail, and with `image/jpeg` its MJPG pre-drop, whose input is always faster). drop-only and skip-to-first stay; the builders' comments say why the set rate comes first. No flag. | videorate fixates its source caps on their first structure, at the rate nearest its input's (`gst_video_rate_fixate_caps`, 656-676): a slower source fixates its own rate and a faster one the set rate, so wherever the set rate alone negotiated, the same caps negotiate now. The set rate goes first for a source whose caps carry no rate (framerate 0/1: an H.264 stream without VUI timing, which avdec_h264 reports so): under 1.28.2 the range alone fixated it to 1/1 and passed 2 of 100 frames (1 fps), and a range from 0/1 gave 0/1 and no conform (100 of 100 at a 25 fps setting); with the set rate first it gets the set rate, as with that rate alone (at 25 fps, 50 of 100). 1.22.0 refuses a 0/1 source with every form but the range from 0/1, which aborts the process on a frame without a duration (`gstvideorate.c` 1.22:740, an assertion); the range's lower bound, 1/1, keeps 0/1 out of it. | **What happens now** (measured, the same under both videorate versions unless said): a slower source runs at its own rate, every frame: 25p into 50 and into 30 (25/1, 50 of 50, 40 ms apart), 29.97 into 30 (30000/1001), 59.94 into 60 (60000/1001), 24 into 25, 23.976 into 24, 12.5 into 25 (25/2). An equal or faster source runs as before: 50 into 50 all 100, 50 into 25 50 of 100 40 ms apart, 60 and 59.94 into 50 100 of 120, 50 into 24 48 of 100. The encoders get the negotiated rate, fixed: x264enc and x265enc take 25/1 for 25p into 50 and for 50p into 25, 30000/1001 for 29.97 into 30 and 60000/1001 for 59.94 into 60, the parsers and mpegtsmux carry it, and every frame is encoded; under 1.28.2 a 0/1 source into 25 gives them 25/1 and 50 of 100, as with the set rate alone. Through the transcoder's own description on both runners (case TR): 25p into the 50 fps rendition, 100 of 100 frames, every step 3,600 ticks, its SPS saying 25 fps; 29.97p into the 30 fps one, 119 of 120, its SPS 29.97, every step 3,003 ± 2 ticks (90 kHz rounding: the fixture's own PES step 3,002 to 3,004) but one of two at the start: the second frame, about 11 µs early against its slot, the first after the anchor, is dropped (B-186's first early frame). **Limits:** equal rates are as they were, since the range changes nothing there (the same output rate, the same grid): 15,000 frames of 50p into 50 lose 0 on time and 40 ppm slow, 1 at 40 ppm fast and 3 at 200 ppm fast, with either caps, under both versions, on the transcoder's string and on the encoder's raw tail; a slower source at its own rate is such a case (25p into 50, 40 ppm fast: 1 of 7,500). Nothing small makes equal rates pass every frame: drop-only decides each frame in transform_ip, `in_ts >= next_output_ts` (2047-2056), on slots exactly one output frame apart (853-858), with no tolerance; its source caps offer no rate above the input's, so there is no finer grid; basetransform's passthrough would still call transform_ip (`transform_ip_on_passthrough` TRUE, `gstbasetransform.c` 1.28.2:347, used at 2201; videorate keeps it); `average-period` mode, a moving-average limiter, drops more (40 ppm fast: 48 of 15,000 with a 1 s period, 195 with 0.2 s, measured). Only a path without videorate at equal rates would pass every frame, which needs the source's rate when the string is built (the module does not have it) or a runner-side bypass: not small, so B-186's equal-rate limit stands, for the owner's veto. GOP Length counts frames at the rate the rendition runs: with a 25p source its default of 50 makes a keyframe every 2 s. The cards' Framerate shows the set rate (`TranscoderModule.ts`, `videoEncoderStatus.ts`), not the running one. A source slower than 1 fps is still refused. Not tested here: the Video Encoder's bare negotiation (no mode probed), where v4l2src may now fixate a rate below the request, and v4l2h264enc, v4l2h265enc and the VA encoders (none on the Pi 5 dev box; they get the same fixed rates). Found on the way, not this item: the encoder writes a V4L2 mode's fractional rate as `framerate=29.97/1` (`parseFormats` keeps "(29.970 fps)" as 29.97), which GStreamer reads as a string field and cannot link: a device whose picked rate is 29.97 or 59.94 does not start. **Tests:** vitest: `transcoderPipeline.test.ts` (+1: at 24, 25, 30, 50 and 60 fps the caps are the set rate, then a range up to it, and no other field names a rate; B-186's case and the deinterlace and burn-in strings carry the new caps), the golden strings (their header says so), `TranscoderModule.test.ts` (the plan snapshot gains `rendition30`), `videoEncoderPipeline.test.ts` (+1: a raw and an MJPG mode at 25 under a 50 request capture at 25 with the new caps after them, and the MJPG branch's three rates; the full strings; the snapshot gains `raw30`), `VideoEncoderModule.test.ts` (2 strings): the two plugins 170 → 172 tests. `videorate_conform_test.py` 16 → 37 checks, passing under both versions: 25p into the transcoder's 50 and 30 fps strings and the encoder's 50 fps tail (25/1, every frame), 29.97p into both 30 fps strings (30000/1001, every frame on its own PTS), the equal-rate losses above against the set rate alone on the same input, x264enc and x265enc behind the transcoder's 25, 30 and 50 fps strings (the rate each takes, the frames encoded), and a 0/1 source, which ends as with the set rate alone (from 1.28: 25/1, 50 of 100). Protocol case TR 14 → 36 checks: the egress's SPS rate on the four 25i runs, and 25p into 50 fps and 29.97p into 30 on both runners (no error, the frames out, the steps, the SPS rate); the protocol test 538 → 560 checks. **Mutants,** 6 of 6 caught: the set rate alone back, in the transcoder (vitest 8, the suite 7 under each version, TR 16) and in the encoder (vitest 13, the suite 2); the range's top dropped (`[1/1,2147483647/1]`), in the transcoder (vitest 8, the suite 4, TR 6: 50p fields into 25 send every field) and in the encoder (vitest 13, the suite 4); the range alone, without the set rate first, in the transcoder (vitest 9; the suite 1 under 1.28.2, its 0/1 source at 1 fps, none under the gate's 1.22.0, which refuses a 0/1 source either way) and in the encoder (vitest 15; the suite 2 under 1.28.2, 1 under 1.22.0: the MJPG string check). **Device check** (next round, not run): the Pi 5 test box, a TEMP Video Transcoder at the default 50 fps with one 640x360 rendition on a 25p source (the dev Pi's ffmpeg sending a 1080p25 file over SRT): it starts and stays up with no restart, 25 frames a second out (`record-bus`, PES per second) with its SPS at 25 fps; the same transcoder on a 50p source with Frame Rate 25: 25 frames a second (B-186). **Phase 3 line:** the same set-rate-alone caps (p3w3 `transcoderPipeline.ts`:236, `videoEncoderPipeline.ts`:104 and :131): the fix goes there with B-186's at the next carry merge, with the snapshots, the suite and case TR. Texts: this row and the intro, B-186's limits, the release notes (Fixed), the builders' comments, the golden strings' header. |
| B-189 | A Video Encoder on a raw YUYV or YU12 capture mode never started: its caps after v4l2src named the mode's V4L2 fourcc as the GStreamer format, and GStreamer's names for those two are YUY2 and I420 (c8's finding on B-186's way) | Release line (v2.0.0.100). Found 2026-10-28 by c8 (B-186, "Found on the way, not this item"), fixed 2026-10-29 by c11 (the mapping, the orchestrator's call; its form and the rest, engineering calls, for the owner's veto). **Seen** (c8): a YUYV or a YU12 mode gave `video/x-raw,format=YUYV` or `format=YU12` after v4l2src, which cannot link. c11 on the dev Pi (v4l2src 1.22.0; the parse needs no device): `v4l2src ! video/x-raw,format=YUYV,width=640,height=360,framerate=30/1 ! fakesink` stops at the parse, "could not link v4l2src0 to fakesink0, v4l2src0 can't handle caps video/x-raw, format=(string)YUYV, …", and `format=YU12` the same; with YUY2, I420, NV12, NV16, YV12 or UYVY the parse links (and fails only on the missing device). The runner reports a parse that fails as "Pipeline parse error: …" and starts nothing (`runner.cpp`:322-331), and the module's health goes to error with that text (`GstPluginBase.ts`:291-305), at every start. The same caps are on every line since the raw mode pin came in (f71451f2, 2026-04-30), v2.0.0.98's c3b3309c and v2.0.0.99's 08d7fe9d among them. **Cause:** `parseFormats` keeps the fourcc `v4l2-ctl --list-formats-ext` prints ('YUYV', 'YU12'), and `buildV4l2SourceForModes` wrote it as the caps' format. v4l2src names a mode by GStreamer's format from gst-v4l2's table (`gst_v4l2_formats[]`, `gstv4l2object.c` 1.28.2; its raw caps take `gst_video_format_to_string` of the entry, 1746-1748): V4L2's YUYV is YUY2 (202) and its YU12 (`V4L2_PIX_FMT_YUV420`) is I420 (199); NV12 (220), NV16 (229), YV12 (201) and UYVY (205) keep their name, so those modes, and MJPEG, worked. **Fix (as built):** `captureModes.ts`'s `RAW_FORMAT_PREFERENCE` is now the table: the six raw fourccs the encoder pins, in the old order, each with its GStreamer name (YU12 → I420, YUYV → YUY2, the other four the same); `FORMAT_PREFERENCE` takes its keys, and `gstVideoFormat()` gives a picked raw mode's caps format, throwing for a fourcc the table lacks instead of writing it; `videoEncoderPipeline.ts` writes that name. The mode chosen, every other string and the device list's `formats` (V4L2's names; nothing in the UI shows them) are unchanged. No flag. | The caps after v4l2src must meet what v4l2src offers, and it offers a mode only under GStreamer's name, so that name is the one that links. The table is the preference list, so no format can be pinned without its name, and a lookup that misses stops the string's assembly with the fourcc in its message, not the parse. | **What happens now** (measured): the encoder's own string for a 640x360 50 fps mode of each of the six formats, its v4l2src replaced by a live 50 fps videotestsrc behind caps in gst-v4l2's name for the fourcc (a device in that mode), passes 20 of 20 frames in that format (10 more runs of each: 60 of 60, every step 20 ms); the YUYV and YU12 strings with the fourcc put back stop at the parse, "could not link …, can't handle caps video/x-raw, format=(string)YUYV" (YU12 the same). The mode picked is as before: MJPEG first, then NV12, NV16, YU12, YV12, YUYV and UYVY, at the set size when there is one, else in the first of those formats the device has at any size. **Limits:** formats the encoder does not pin (NV21, NV61, YVYU, VYUY, RGB3, BGR3, GREY and the rest) still leave v4l2src to negotiate on its own, as before; pinning one needs its gst-v4l2 name in the table, in the vitest's reference and in the suite's, and each test fails until it has one. Not this item, still open: a mode whose picked rate is fractional (29.97, 59.94) gives `framerate=29.97/1` and does not start (c10's finding, B-188). Not tested here: a real YUYV or YU12 device (none on the dev Pi; the device check below). **Tests:** vitest `videoEncoderPipeline.test.ts` +9: the table is gst-v4l2's name for exactly the six fourccs; per mapping, a mode in that fourcc gets that name as its only format; the full strings of a 1080p50 YUYV and YU12 mode; MJPEG and RGB3 have no name (an error); the upscale case's YUYV expectation, which held the bug, says YUY2; the snapshot `plugins/video-encoder/tests/videorate-strings.json` gains `formats`, one 640x360 50 fps mode per table key (`vitest -u` rewrites it): the two plugins 172 → 181 tests. `videorate_conform_test.py` 37 → 45 checks (section 9: the six strings, and the YUYV and YU12 ones with the fourcc put back), under the gate's videorate 1.22.0 and under 1.28.2. **Mutants,** 4 of 4 caught: the mapping removed from the caps builder, HEAD's behaviour (vitest 5, the suite 2); YU12 and YUYV mapped to themselves in the table (vitest 7, the suite 2); YU12 mapped to YV12, a valid name with the chroma planes swapped (vitest 4, the suite 1, through its device-format caps: a bare videotestsrc would take YV12); NV21 added to the table without a reference name (vitest 2, the suite 1). **Device check** (next round, not run): the Pi 4 test box, each capture's raw modes with `v4l2-ctl --list-formats-ext` (read only); if a raw YUYV mode exists at a size the Pi can carry, a TEMP Video Encoder on it for 2 minutes (the CMA guard; never the Cam Link): it starts with no error on its card and sends at the mode's rate, then it is deleted. **Phase 3 line:** the same caps (p3w3 `videoEncoderPipeline.ts`:155, `captureModes.ts`:15; p4w1 the same): the fix goes there at the next carry merge, with its tests, the snapshot's `formats` and the suite's section 9. Texts: this row and the intro, B-186's found-on-the-way sentence, the release notes (Fixed), the comments in `captureModes.ts` and `videoEncoderPipeline.ts`. |
| B-190 | A producer relaunched while its old runner still served an edge could leave that edge with no listener and its consumer waiting forever: the new runner's bind beside the live socket failed and its error containment unlinked the old runner's path, or the old runner's stop unlinked the new one's (the owner's MR-001) | Release line (v2.0.0.100). Found 2026-10-30 on ZA-SCC-FRA-Master01 by the fleet's apply lane, at both switches to '302M' (the owner's bug log MR-001), fixed 2026-10-30 by c13 (the orchestrator's call: a new runner waits while the path is held, and a runner unlinks only its own socket; the private bind path, the hand-over before the drain and the rest, engineering calls, for the owner's veto). **Seen** (the box's engine journal, 10:18 and 10:50Z): the MPEG-TS Muxer relaunched 3 to 4 times within about 8 s while BusFanout re-attached its input producers (`BusFanoutCoordinator.reattachProducer` relaunches a consumer launched before its producer); one relaunch's attach logged `bus_attach: live producer already on /tmp/mr-bus-40011-5eca6c.sock — not unlinking`, and from 2 to 5 s later the kept 'Rist gateway 2500' SRT Output logged `Waiting for producer bus socket(s)` every 30 s, the path absent on the box (`ls`); restarting only that output fixed it within 5 s (its connections' re-apply sent the current muxer runner a detach and an attach with no file there). **Cause** (the runners' code, and GStreamer 1.28.2's source from the build's downloads): (1) unixfdsink binds without unlinking first (`gstunixfdsink.c`:452), so beside a live listener its start fails and basesink posts "Failed to start" (`gstbasesink.c`:5897-5905); the busedge containment (`runner.cpp`:486-497 at 6a2b1751) tears that branch down, and the teardown's unconditional `unlink` of the edge path (`bus_edges.cpp`:395 at 6a2b1751, the python twin's `_finish` the same) deletes the OLD runner's live path, which serves on an orphaned file until it stops; nothing re-attaches, so the new runner has no edge. (2) unixfdsink's stop unlinks its socket-path whoever owns it by then (`gstunixfdsink.c`:501-502, at READY to NULL; 1.24.13 the same, so the runners' "does not unlink its socket file on NULL" was wrong), and a relaunch retires the old runner while the new one starts at once (`GstRunner.ts`:731-738), its EOS drain up to 6 s: a path a newer runner bound in that window went with the old runner's stop. (3) The new runner cannot tell: its sink still takes buffers, so the stall watchdog sees progress. The first switch's journal reads as both in turn: the third launch warned beside the live second, the fourth attached with no file there, and its consumer found none 0.25 s later. Reproduced on the dev Pi with HEAD's runners (an old runner serving, a new one attaching): the new runner's warning, its branch, "bus edge failed (unixfdsink0) … state change failed", and the old runner's path gone 1 s later while it still ran. **Fix (as built),** in both runners (`bus_edges.cpp` with the path rules in a new `edge_path.cpp`, and the python twin in `gst-pipeline-runner.py`, which still hosts bus producers): an attach whose edge path a live listener holds stays pending on the 250 ms retry, with one warning per pending attach, a duplicate attach included ("live producer already on <path> — attach waits until the path is free"), and logs "<path> free again — attached" when it attaches; a file nothing listens on is removed as before. The edge's unixfdsink binds a private path (`<path>.<pid>`), started to READY before the branch joins the pipeline, so a failed bind posts to no bus and costs a warning ("cannot serve <path>"), never the producer; the runner publishes that socket at the edge path with link(2), which never replaces a file (EEXIST counts as held), and removes the private name, so GStreamer's stop-time unlink only ever meets the private name. A runner unlinks the edge path only while it names the runner's own socket (st_dev and st_ino at publish) and while its sink still listens: in a branch teardown before the branch goes to NULL, and for every edge at the top of the pipeline teardown, before the EOS drain. An attach on a pipeline whose target state is NULL stays pending. The consumer gate's indefinite wait is unchanged. No flag. | A path has one listener, and only a runner that knows the path is its own may remove it: a bind beside a live listener can only fail, and an unlink by path deletes whoever holds the path at that moment. GStreamer's own unlink cannot be kept off the path while the sink runs (socket-path and socket-type are refused once started, `gstunixfdsink.c`:229-244), so the sink never binds the path itself. Unlinking while still listening means a successor finds the path live or gone, never stale, so it cannot replace the path between the owner's check and its unlink; doing it before the drain hands the edge over at once while the old runner's connected consumers drain. | **What happens now** (measured on the dev Pi, GStreamer 1.28.2): a producer relaunched while its old runner serves the edge (native, python, and python to native): the new runner's attach waits with one warning over retries and a duplicate attach, the old runner's path untouched; the old runner, stopped with a ~2 s EOS drain, hands the path over before it, the new runner publishes it while the old one still runs, and after the old runner's exit the path still names the new runner's socket and accepts, a consumer receiving from it; an old runner killed hard leaves a stale file, which the waiting attach clears. By design the new runner publishes at most one 250 ms retry after the old runner's stop command, not after its drain. **Limits:** a second live producer on one path (a configuration error) keeps the attach pending, with its one warning, for as long as it listens; a path deleted from outside stays unpublished until its edge is attached again. **Found on the way, not this item:** the native runner's `g_teardowns` set is erased by the teardown probe (`teardown_probe_cb`), which can run on a streaming thread, while the main loop reads and writes it; the python twin runs under the GIL. B-193 (2026-10-31) fixes it and closes a corner of this item with it: an edge still being torn down at a stop kept its path until its probe fired (with `eosDrain: false` perhaps never, leaving a stale file for the successor's retry to remove); the stop now releases it. **Tests:** `native_runner_protocol_test.py` case edge-handover (B-190), 59 checks: the three runner pairs above, each also with a stale file at the path before the first attach and a bind into a read-only directory, and the hard kill on each runner, ending with another socket at the path that the stop must leave; the suite 619 PASS (560 before), 0 FAIL. `gst_bus_edge_test.py`'s socket-path check reworded. **Mutants,** 3 of 3 caught: HEAD's runners (27 checks fail, the old runner's path deleted by the new runner's containment and no listener at the end among them), the private bind path removed (the old runner's stop deletes the new runner's path), the ownership check removed from the release (a path another socket took is unlinked at the stop). **Device check** (next round, not run): on a test box, switch 5 times to a profile in which an MPEG-TS Muxer feeds an SRT or RIST output, and restart the muxer 5 times quickly: the output never stays on "Waiting for producer bus socket(s)", and the muxer runner's journal shows at most one "attach waits" warning per relaunch per edge, each followed by "free again — attached". **Phase 3 line:** the same code (p3w1 to p3w3 and p4w1: `bus_edges.cpp`:121-128 and 394-395, `gst-pipeline-runner.py`'s `_remove_stale_bus_socket` and `_finish`): the fix goes there at the next carry merge, with its case. Texts: this row and the intro, the release notes (Fixed), the runners' comments. |
| B-191 | A module restart did not apply a setting its plugin copies in `onInit`: a device picked again for an Audio Input (302M), Audio Output (302M), Audio Input or Audio Output stayed half-applied through Restart and through Disable then Enable, and a module waiting for hot-plug went on waiting for its old device (the owner's MR-002) | Release line (v2.0.0.100). Found 2026-10-30 on ZA-SCC-SWA01 (a Pi 4) at the SCC field test (the owner's bug log MR-002), fixed 2026-10-30 by c14 (the orchestrator's call: a restart applies every changed setting, for every plugin, at the engine where that is safe; the rest, engineering calls, for the owner's veto). **Seen** (the box's engine journal and module states, 10:41Z): the owner picked the SSL 2's devices again for Mic 1 and Mic 2 (audio-input-302m) and for Audio Output (audio-output-302m); the manager stored them and sent the engine, for each module in turn, a settings patch (12, 12 and 11 ops) and then `moduleRestart` (the restarts at 10:41:15, 10:41:20 and 10:41:26Z). Each module went on reporting `Audio device "<old name>" not connected — waiting for hot-plug` (`…HiFi__ssl2_mono_in_S2_0_0__source`, `…_S2_0_1__source`, `…HiFi__hw_S2__sink`) while its settings named `…HiFi__Mic2__source`, `…HiFi__Mic1__source` and `…HiFi__Line__sink`, `pendingRestart` false, and the mics' connections failed "has not assigned a bus channel yet". An engine stop and start (11:36Z) applied the devices; both mics then ran. **Cause** (the code at 6a2b1751): the four audio I/O plugins copy `device` into `this.deviceName` in `onInit` (`AudioInput302mModule.ts`:102, `AudioOutput302mModule.ts`:68, `AudioInputModule.ts`:43, `AudioOutputModule.ts`:44) and use the copy for `onStart`'s presence check, for the hot-plug watchdog, and in audio-input and audio-output for the remap module. `ModuleInstance.start` ran `onInit` only while `_initialized` was false (`ModuleInstance.ts`:125), which only a start that threw (:155) or a destroy (:226) resets. `moduleRestart` on a running module (one waiting for hot-plug counts: its `onStart` returns) is `ModuleLifecycle._restart`'s stop and start of the same instance (`ModuleLifecycle.ts`:378-379), and Enable starts the existing instance (:439); neither ran `onInit`. `applyConfigUpdate` stored the change in the config the plugin holds and set `pendingRestart`, which the restart's start then cleared. An engine start (`_startAll`) builds new instances, which is why the engine restart worked. A running 302M module whose old device was still present did open the new device at Restart (its `buildPipeline` reads the config) while its presence check and watchdog kept the old name. **Fix (as built):** `ModuleInstance.start` runs the plugin's `onInit` again, on the instance's current config, when a change is pending a restart (`pendingRestart`), as it did after a failed start; a start with nothing pending, or with only live changes applied, does not. That covers Restart, Disable then Enable and the routing layer's own restarts of a module, for every plugin. The scan of every `plugins/*/engine` module (28 classes, all on `GstPluginBase`): 12 override `onInit` (audio-decoder, audio-encoder, note, video-encoder, video-player, the four audio I/O plugins, n1-mixer, mpegts-muxer, audio-processing; 11 here until B-194's recount); besides the four device copies, n1-mixer's `pairCount` (read again in `onStart`), the muxer's seed of input keys and PIDs (written only where one is missing), audio-processing's graph publish and audio-input's and audio-output's format detection (run again for the new device) are safe to run twice, and no plugin keeps a setting across a stop anywhere else. The one allocation in any `onInit` was `GstPluginBase`'s per-instance logger: `createLogger` pipes a stream into stderr that is never closed (one close, finish, error and unpipe listener on stderr each, measured); it is now made once per instance. `onDestroy` takes no part: `GstPluginBase.onDestroy` removes every listener, the engine's forwarders among them. No flag. | `pendingRestart` is exactly a stored setting the running plugin has not applied (FDS 9.3: the pending changes are applied when the user restarts the module), so the start that clears it is the start that must read the settings again. At the engine one rule covers every plugin, present and future, where a fix in the plugins covers only those found. Running `onInit` again on the same instance keeps the instance, its listeners and its ports, which rebuilding the instance, as an engine start does, would drop and make anew. A start with nothing pending still does not run it, so the routing layer's frequent restarts of a consumer do not repeat `onInit`'s side effects (a detected-format write, the muxer's legacy-offset warning). | **What happens now** (the engine's tests on the dev Pi): a settings patch, then `moduleRestart`, through the engine's own patch router, command dispatcher and lifecycle: a running module opens the device picked again; a module waiting for hot-plug opens it, or, while it is absent, waits for it and not for the old one (the old one plugged in does nothing, the new one opens); Disable then Enable opens a device picked again while disabled or while running; the base's logger is not made again. Each of the four plugins under the engine's `ModuleInstance`: after Restart it captures from, plays to or remaps the device picked again and watches it, and one waiting for hot-plug waits for that device. **Limits:** a 302M module waiting for hot-plug whose old device comes back before the Restart builds its pipeline from the stored new device (its `buildPipeline` reads the config) while its watchdog watches the old one, as before; the Restart puts both on the new device. A setting stored while a start is under way counts as applied by that start, which clears `pendingRestart`, as before (B-194: it stays pending now). B-103's start check of a value past a bound is not run again at a re-init; the manager's write check holds a patched value to the same rules. **Tests:** `restartSettings.test.ts` (new, 5), `ModuleInstance.test.ts` (+2: a pending change re-inits once, a live one does not, nor a start with nothing pending; a change stored while stopped re-inits at the next start), and 2 in each of the four plugins' tests. **Mutants,** 3 of 3 caught: the start's condition back to `!_initialized` (all 15 new tests fail, the engine's and the plugins' on the old device, the 302M ones waiting with the field's text), the logger made at every `onInit` (the engine's running-module test fails), `onInit` at every start (the existing stop-then-start test and the new pending-change one fail). **Device check** (next round, not run): on a test box with a USB audio interface, pick another device for a Mic (Audio Input 302M) and press Restart: the module opens the new device without an engine restart; the same through Disable then Enable; and with the Mic waiting for an unplugged device, a device picked again and Restart wait for and open the new one. **Phase 3 line:** the same code (p3w1 to p3w3 and p4w1: `ModuleInstance.ts`:125, `GstPluginBase.onInit`'s logger): the fix goes there at the next carry merge, with its tests. Texts: this row and the intro, the release notes (Fixed), `PluginModule.onInit`'s comment, plugins/README.md (Lifecycle), FDS 9.4. |
| B-192 | An Audio Output (302M) with several sources played nothing until every source ran: the runner's socket gate waited for the edge socket of every source in its mix, so one source that never started held the others back (the owner's MR-003) | Release line (v2.0.0.100). Found 2026-10-30 on ZA-SCC-SWA01 (a Pi 4) at the SCC field test (the owner's bug log MR-003), fixed 2026-10-30 by c15 (the orchestrator's call: start with the sources that run, as the live-input mixers go on without a lost input; the rest engineering calls, for the owner's veto). **Seen** (the fleet lane's restart log, the engine stop and start at 11:36Z, checks 3 to 9): the translator's Audio Output, wired to four Audio Transcoders (Master, ENG IN, SWA IN, Chat IN) of which only Master ran (the IN legs' SRT callers had no peer), showed `Waiting for upstream module(s): audio-transcoder-… (audio-in), …` with one to three names, `running` flipping, `sources: 4`, and played nothing, so the translator did not hear Master either. **Cause** (the code at 6a2b1751): `GstRunner.startPipeline` launches only once every `unixfdsrc` socket of the description accepts (`waitForBusSockets`, ADR-0010), and the output's mixer arm put every wired source's branch into its one string (`buildAudioMixInput`, not in live-input mode: ADR-0008's 2026-10-02 addendum kept it on the classic restart "for now"). A transcoder with no input data is gated, restarting or not yet attached, so its edge socket is not there: the output waited for it, and a dark transcoder's restart sent it back to the gate (the data wait's `bus_producer_restarted`, rule 4's relaunch). Measured on both runners with the output's own string (scratch c15 `exp_silent_input.py`): a branch whose socket does not accept fails the whole start ("Failed to set pipeline to PLAYING"), while one whose socket accepts but carries nothing does not hold the mix (PLAYING at +2.1 s, W). The N-1 mixer the owner compared it with goes on without a silent input inside its mix the same way, but its own start also waits for every source's socket. **Not an owner's rule:** ADR-0010's wait converges chains; ADR-0008's consequences say one dark contributor must not take the others down; chapter 6 part 4.3 and the Phase 2 release notes say an input that goes silent is "left out, not waited for"; the output's restart path was kept "for now". **Fix (as built):** (1) `PipelineDescription.liveInputs`: an aggregator's input branches apart from `pipeline`. The runner host's gate (`waitForLiveInputs`, `busSocketGate.ts`) waits for the pipeline's own sockets and for one input whose sockets all accept, then launches with every input there, each linked `( name=… ) ! <mixer>.sink_<i>` (`liveInputLaunchText`), and reports the others at the gate's opening (`busGate {pending: [], absent}`; every gate opening sends `absent`, empty for a plain description). The stored description keeps every input, so a relaunch or a crash replay chooses again; while none is there the gate waits and names them all, as before (ADR-0010 rule 5). (2) `GstPluginBase`: what a launch goes without is its lost-input set, made anew at each gate opening and cleared at a fresh start: "Input from <module> (<port>) lost — continuing without it", shown over ok or its own text and again at PLAYING (whose healthy mark used to wipe it); a description refresh drops the names of inputs no longer wired; `isLiveInputLost`. (3) Routing: a branch the consumer runs without is added once its producer plays (`rejoinLiveInput`: wait for the edge socket, add, refresh), at that producer's PLAYING when the consumer launched after it (rule 4 sees nothing stale there, and nothing added it), and at the consumer's own PLAYING for producers already playing (`BusFanoutCoordinator.rejoinLostInputs`, from `MediaRouter.onProducerPlaying`). A stale consumer keeps the re-link and its relaunch fallback. A live add on a wiring change no longer waits 5 s for the edge of a producer whose gst pipeline is not launched (`producerAway`): the runner contains the dead branch at once and the producer's PLAYING adds it, where the engine's connection apply used to wait 5 s per dark source (B-194: no add before that edge accepts; the module runs without it until then). (4) audio-302m-core `buildLiveMixInput`: the live arm in parts; `buildAudioMixInput`'s live arm renders through it, byte-identical. (5) audio-output-302m: from two wired sources the aligned mixer and its tail are the pipeline and every source a live input, with `getLiveInputBranch` on Audio In (null below two); one source keeps the direct branch, the classic restart and its string. No flag. | The wait comes from the gate, so the choice is made there: the runner host is the one place that knows at each launch which sockets accept, the replays included, which the module never sees. The module choosing its sources by its producers' state would race the gate (a producer gone between the build and the probe) and need a wake of its own from an idle start. The live verbs, the error containment and the lost-input warning are the live-input mixers' (#787), reused. audio-mixer and n1-mixer-302m keep every branch in `pipeline`: their start still waits for every source, the same limit, not asked here (B-197: they hand the runner their sources apart too; a relaunch with a producer down waited for it). | **What happens now** (the engine's tests on the dev Pi, the engine's own routing and runner host, Python faked, the edge sockets real): four sources wired, Master's alone up, the output launches with Master's branch and names the other three lost, all four named for containment; ENG IN starting later is added to the running mix, no relaunch and no restart; SWA IN, launched before the output with its socket up only later, is added when it plays (the new path); Chat IN playing while the output still starts is added at the output's PLAYING; ENG IN going away (`input_branch_lost`) leaves Master playing and is named. (Corrected by B-197, 2026-11-02: these were the engine's tests with the runner faked, which say what is launched and added, not what plays. On .108 an output restarted while a source was dark launched with the others as said, then played nothing: the dark source, re-linked into the running mix, brought its producer's last output lateness as a seed, which held the mix's pace above the sink's D.) On real GStreamer, both runners, the module's own description for four sources launched as the runner host composes it with one (pulsesink as fakesink; scratch c15 `exp_output_composed.py`, log `mr-captures/wf13/c15/exp_output_composed.log`): PLAYING at +0.73 s, the second source added live is heard (meter 11 to 12 blocks), its producer stopping drops its branch (`input_branch_lost`, its watch absent), the first plays on, no error, exit 0. **Limits:** before the output's first PLAYING (about 2 s) a source in the launch whose socket is re-created fails the launch (`bus_producer_restarted`, the runner's data wait), which relaunches and chooses again; a socket gone between the gate's probe and the runner's start fails that start the same way; wiring a second source to one, or going back to one, still restarts the output (the two arms differ); the warning says "lost" also for a source that never ran this session (B-194: "not running"; and the second source's restart comes without a refused add first). **Tests:** `AudioOutput302mModule.liveInputs.test.ts` (new, 5), `GstRunner.liveInputs.test.ts` (new, 4), `GstPluginBase.liveInputs.test.ts` (new, 6), `busSocketGate.test.ts` (+4), `BusFanoutCoordinator.test.ts` (+4), `MpegTsBusExecutor.test.ts` (+2), the output's module test (+3, 2 updated), audio-302m-core (+1, 2 updated), the start-payload field list; `FakePythonProcess` records the start and can play the runner's replies. **Mutants,** 11 of 11 caught, among them the gate waiting for every input (10 tests fail) and the output's old string (7). **Device check** (not run, no box in this lane): on a box with an Audio Output (302M), wire two sources and run only one: it plays, with the other named lost; start the second: it joins without a break in the first; stop the first: the second plays on. **Phase 3 line:** p3w1 to p3w3 and p4w1 have the same gate and the output's old fan-in (p3w1's with `mixInputDemuxes`): the fix goes there at the next carry merge, adapted, with its tests. Texts: this row and the intro, ADR-0010 (rule 5), ADR-0008 (amendment 2026-10-30), the release notes (Fixed), plugins/README.md (Live Input Branches), audio-302m-core's README, `PipelineDescription.liveInputs` and `PluginModule.isLiveInputLost`. |
| B-193 | The native runner's list of edges being torn down was changed by a teardown probe on the producer's streaming thread while the main loop read and changed it, unlocked: a crash or a corrupt list was possible while an edge was removed (the owner's MR-018) | Release line (v2.0.0.100). Found 2026-10-30 in the code by c13 (B-190, "Found on the way"; the owner's bug log MR-018; not seen on a box), fixed 2026-10-31 by c16 (the orchestrator's call: the bookkeeping stays on the main loop; the hand-over, the stop's release of a still-detaching edge and the twin, engineering calls, for the owner's veto). **Cause** (the code at 07ca4024, and GStreamer 1.28.2's `gstpad.c`): `teardown_branch` put the socket into `g_teardowns`, a `std::set` (`bus_edges.cpp`:495), and added an IDLE and BLOCK_DOWNSTREAM probe on the tee src pad. GStreamer runs that probe inside `gst_pad_add_probe` when the pad is idle, but while a push is in flight through the pad it runs it on the pushing thread as the push leaves (`gstpad.c`:1497-1505, then :4860-4865 for a buffer and :5719-5723 for an event), so on the producer's streaming thread, or during a stop on the decoder-drain thread, whose EOS passes the tee (`runner.cpp`:142-146). `teardown_probe_cb` then erased the socket there (`bus_edges.cpp`:444) while the main loop's `try_bus_attach` (:115, every 250 ms retry and every attach), `teardown_branch` (:495) and `clear_pending` (:472) read or changed the same tree. The inventory of everything the probe callbacks and the runner's other threads touch in `bus_edges.cpp`, `edge_path.cpp` and `runner.cpp` (c16's notes) found no other unsynchronised access: `g_branches`, `g_pending`, `g_tee_progress` and the timers are the main loop's; the progress probes write only atomics; an edge's GStreamer handles pass to its teardown probe with the probe and are no longer read on the main loop; `ipc::emit` and `ipc::log` lock. **Fix (as built),** in both runners: (1) The records are the main loop's. `g_teardowns` maps the socket to its edge. The probe still does its GStreamer work where it fires, with the pad blocked, and then drops the record at once when it ran on the main loop (an idle pad: `g_main_context_is_owner`), or hands it to the main loop with `g_idle_add` and an owned payload; only that same edge's record is dropped. (2) B-190's corner, recorded only in c13's notes: an edge whose teardown probe had not fired when the pipeline stopped was already out of `g_branches`, so the stop did not release its path; with an EOS drain the probe released it on the EOS, with `eosDrain: false` it might never fire, leaving a stale file the successor's next retry removed ("unlinked stale bus socket") before publishing. The stop now keeps the records (`clear_pending` drops only queued attaches) and `release_paths` releases those edges' paths too, while their sinks still listen. A probe and the stop may then release one path at once, so `release_path` claims and unlinks under one mutex (`edge_path.cpp`); the probe stops its sink only after its release returns. (3) The python twin (`gst-pipeline-runner.py`) was memory-safe under the GIL (each set operation one builtin call), but with (2) its stop reads the records while a probe may finish, and a dict changed by another thread while it is iterated raises: it gets the same shape (`_bus_teardowns` maps the socket to its entry, a `GLib.idle_add` hand-over, `_bus_release_lock`). No flag. **Fix round 1** (2026-10-31, after the batch gate; engineering calls, for the owner's veto): the gate's one failure was `gst_udp_silence_test.py` (the python twin, in process), two checks of a resume ("input_resumed is reported once", "a fresh silence after data is reported again"), in its run and alone. Not this item's change, which that test reaches only at its first stop, after those checks and with no edge: a race in both runners' udp silence watch since it was written (2026-09-15, the native port 09-18), seen in gate logs since 10-17 and failing the same way with 07ca4024's runner (the gate's A/B). **Cause** (GStreamer 1.28.2's `gstudpsrc.c`:1014-1044): udpsrc posts `GstUDPSrcTimeout` from its streaming thread and waits again; the packet that ends the wait goes out on that thread next, through the gate's buffer probe (`gst_source_gate.py` `on_buffer`, `source_gate.cpp` `udp_buffer_cb`), while the runner meets the message later, on the main loop. When the probe ran for the first packet back before the loop met the last timeout, it ended the silence and queued the resume, and that stale timeout then started a new silence, which the next packet ended again: "input_silent input_silent state_change input_resumed input_resumed input_silent" in the gate's debug copy, where a pass reads "input_silent state_change input_resumed input_silent". The test sends its packets on its fifth 300 ms tick, about 0.2 ms from it, so a few runs in a hundred failed; with the field's 5 s timeouts, a stream that comes back on a tick reports its silence twice. **Fix (as built),** both runners: the probe records the time of each buffer (`last_data`, natively an atomic `last_data_us`), the bus handler passes the message's own `timeout` field, and `on_udp_timeout` skips a timeout met with a packet less than half a timeout before it. The test's last section, an audiotestsrc started and stopped at once, now stops once PLAYING: its stop during the change to PLAYING met the drain's deadlock (Limits) in about 5 runs in 100, on the base runner too. | One owner per structure: the main loop owns the edge bookkeeping, so there is no lock to take on it and no lock order to keep, and a streaming thread only hands over what it has finished. The probe's work stays where it fires: it unlinks and stops the branch with the tee src pad blocked (the dynamic-unlink recipe of 2026-07-17), and moved to the main loop it would keep the producer's tee blocked until the loop ran, which a stop's EOS drain holds for up to 6 s while its EOS waits at that very probe. Not `g_main_context_invoke`: with no owner (after the loop) it runs the function on the calling thread. Dropping the record at once on the main loop keeps a quiet edge's detach and re-attach (the coordinator's re-apply, the stall watchdog's reset) immediate instead of one 250 ms retry later. The release takes a mutex because it must happen before the probe stops its sink, synchronously, so a successor finds the path live or gone (B-190). Fix round 1: udpsrc posts a timeout only after waiting a whole timeout with no packet since its last push, so a packet less than half a timeout before the loop meets the message came after it: the input is not silent. Half leaves room for the wait's millisecond rounding and the loop's dispatch delay (2.5 s with the field's 5 s timeouts). Not a resume message on the bus behind udpsrc's own, which would order the two exactly: more code in both bus handlers for the same answer. The test's stop waits because the deadlock needs a fix of its own (the drain's EOS during a state change), not this item's. | **What happens now** (the dev Pi, GStreamer 1.28.2): a new native test, `tests/bus_edges_thread_test.cpp` (the runner's `make test`, so `make native-test`), runs the runner's own sources but `main.cpp` on a real appsrc ! tee, its events read from the runner's event fd. ThreadSanitizer does not run on the dev Pi (a 47-bit address space: "unsupported VMA range"), so a test probe holds the producer's push into the edge, the tee src pad stays in use, and each teardown probe fires on the streaming thread: in 40 of 40 such cycles the record stays until the main loop runs (an attach right after the probe waits) and the main loop's drop lets the attach through; an idle pad detaches inside the call and an attach right after binds at once; a stop while a probe is still pending releases the edge's path with its sink listening, and the late probe leaves a socket a successor put there alone; 400 cycles with buffers at about 5 kHz, two new edges each and one edge detached and re-attached whenever attached (12 to 19 of 798 detaches finished on the streaming thread, over five runs), end with every edge attached and detached once, no warning and nothing left in the socket directory. 19 checks, 11 s. `gst_bus_attach_pending_test.py` +8 (24) for the twin: the idle pad, 10 held cycles, the stop. **Limits:** the release mutex is not mutant-tested (that needs an interleaving inside `release_path`). Not this item, seen on the way: a detach removes the edge's one-shot progress probe by an id the probe has already spent (the single-writer rule keeps it until the watchdog's tick), and GStreamer warns "pad … has no probe with id" (`gstpad.c`:1595) at most detaches of a flowing edge, in both runners (41 lines from mr-gst-runner in the 31 Oct journals of ZA-SCC-SWA01): noise only. And a stop while a pipeline is still going to PLAYING could deadlock the EOS drain in GStreamer (the drain's `send_event` held the pipeline's state lock and waited for the source's stream lock, which its streaming thread held while the sink waited to preroll, and the async state change that would free it waited for the state lock): `gst_udp_silence_test.py`'s last stop (the python twin, in process) hung so, here and on HEAD's twin, and the native runner's drain went ahead in the same state; a runner so caught sat out the stop until the engine killed it, 8 s later. Fixed by B-202 (c25, 2026-11-02): before PLAYING the drain sends its EOS to each source, not under the pipeline's state lock, and that last stop comes at once again. **Tests:** the new native test; `gst_bus_attach_pending_test.py` (+8); the engine's python suites that attach, detach or stop edges, one at a time at load < 3 (the gate's patched-queue GStreamer, a registry of their own): gst_bus_attach_pending 24, gst_bus_edge 12, gst_bus_stamper 32, gst_drain 27, gst_playing_watchdog_data_gate 19, gst_mrtsstamp_element 76, gst_ingest_restamp 32, gst_native_plugins 123, gst_lateness_protocol 18, gst_live_inputs 58, gst_capture_rt 156, gst_latency_ratchet 30, `native_runner_protocol_test.py` 619 (edge-handover 59 of 59) and aligner_conformance 159, all PASS, the gate's counts but gst_bus_attach_pending's (16 before); gst_udp_silence, which has no edge, hung at its last stop (the deadlock above), then passed 14 of 14 in 4 of 5 runs alone (HEAD's twin: 5 of 8, 2 timing failures and the same hang). vitest: the child-process suites, BusFanoutCoordinator, busRunnerContract and busHelpers, 19 files, 265 tests, all pass. No TypeScript changed. **Mutants,** 5 of 5 caught: HEAD's runner (3 checks fail: the record gone off the main loop in 40 of 40 cycles, and the stop's two), the record always handed over (2: the idle pad's re-attach waits a retry), the stop not releasing still-detaching edges (2), the stop forgetting the records first (2); HEAD's twin with the new python checks (3, the same three). **Device check** (next round, not run): on a test box, restart a muxer that feeds two outputs 20 times quickly: no runner crash, no lingering `<path>.<pid>` file in /tmp, every output flowing. **Phase 3 line:** the same code (p3w1 to p3w3 and p4w1: `bus_edges.cpp`:53 and 414, the python twin's `_finish`): the fix goes there at the next carry merge, after B-190's, with its tests. **Fix round 1, what happens now:** a new section of `gst_udp_silence_test.py` (20 checks, 14 before) and a new native test, `tests/source_gate_udp_test.cpp` (the runner's own start, bus watch and gate on udpsrc ! fakesink; 10 checks, 6 s), hold the main loop while udpsrc posts a timeout and the packets then pass the probes, so the loop meets that timeout after them in every round: in 5 of 5 rounds it is no new silence, the packets resume once, a later packet does not resume again, and each silence after the data is still reported; the native test also pins the restart bound. Mutants, 6 of 6 caught: HEAD's code (python and native: "no new silence" and "a later packet does not resume again", 0 of 5 each), a check that skips every timeout after any data (4 python and 3 native checks: the silences after data go unreported) and the bus handler passing no field (2 and 2). The suite alone, 20 runs at load below 0.4: 20 of 20 passed, no hang; beside two busy loops (load 0.7 to 1.8) 8 of 8, and the native test 8 of 8 (before, in the gate's runs: base 57 of 60 and head 79 of 90 passed). c16's suites again, one at a time: gst_playing_watchdog_data_gate 19, gst_bus_attach_pending 24, gst_bus_edge 12, gst_drain 27, gst_live_inputs 58, gst_bus_stamper 32, `native_runner_protocol_test.py` 619 (612 s, no retry), the runner's `make test` 29 (19 and 10); vitest, the child-process suites, busRunnerContract, busHelpers, BusFanoutCoordinator and the MPEG-TS IP and AES67 inputs: 23 files, 344 tests; all PASS. Limit: one watch serves every udpsrc of a pipeline, as before; with two (none in the field: a UDP input has one, `netsrc`), a timeout from one is skipped while the other delivers, where before it flapped between silent and receiving. The drain deadlock was a finding for the bug log (MR-022), fixed by B-202, which stops that section at once again. The udp silence code is the same on the Phase 3 line: the fix goes there with this item's. Texts: this row and the intro, B-190's row ("Found on the way" points here), the release notes (Fixed: this item, and the UDP input of its fix round), the runners' comments, the heads of `gst_source_gate.py`, `source_gate.h` and `gst_udp_silence_test.py`. |
| B-194 | A connection whose producer had no bus channel yet failed at level 50 three times and was dropped, and nothing applied it when the producer started by itself later; a live input added on a wiring change raced its producer; the waiting texts named socket paths and module ids (the owner's MR-005, the MR-003 device-test notes of 31 Oct) | Release line (v2.0.0.100). Found 2026-10-30 and 2026-10-31 on ZA-SCC-SWA01 (a Pi 4; the owner's bug log MR-005, DEV-FIX1's MR-003 notes) and in the Fable reviews of c14 and c15, fixed 2026-10-31 by c17 (the orchestrator's brief: a producer that is there but has no channel is waited for, on an event, not retried; the rest engineering calls, for the owner's veto). **Seen** (the box's engine journals, DEV-FIX1): at each engine start (06:39:49Z on the fix build, 06:50:55Z on v2.0.0.100) the engine logged 24 level-50 lines, for six connections (Audio Mixer to the SWA, ENG and Chat OUT transcoders, each OUT transcoder to its SRT output) whose producer had no channel (`MPEG-TS producer <id>:<port> has not assigned a bus channel yet`): the router's `Failed to execute connection — removed` three times each (1 s, then 2 s apart), 18 lines, and the ConnectionApplier's `Connection failed after 3 attempts` once each, 6 lines; 18 s of the start; all six came up when Mic 1 to the mixer was applied. On 30 Oct Mic 1 and Mic 2 waited for renamed devices (MR-004) and the mixer said "No sources connected". At 06:47:30Z, Chat IN enabled with its transcoder gated, the engine sent `bus_input_add` to the Audio Output (302M) runner before the transcoder listened; the runner dropped the branch ("state change failed … branch dropped"), the engine logged "Live input added" all the same, and c15's re-link added it 90 ms later. On v2.0.0.100 the output showed `Waiting for upstream module(s): /tmp/mr-bus-40010-bd647b.sock` once Chat IN was disabled (S2), and FRA-Master01 on 30 Oct a module id. **Cause** (the code at 55faa24a): `MpegTsBusExecutor.execute` threw for a producer without a channel (:86); `MediaRouter.createConnection` deleted the record, logged it at level 50 and re-threw (:345); `ConnectionApplier.connectWithRetry` retried twice and gave up at level 50 (:237, :254). The ordered set (`requiresOrderedApply` ports: the mixer's output, the transcoders') is sorted only among itself, so Mixer to OUT ran before Mic to Mixer, while the mixer, with no input yet, had built no output. **What applied a dropped connection again:** only `ModuleLifecycle`'s start, restart and enable of either end (`reapplyModuleConnections`, :350, :395, :464) and the cascade after a classic consumer restart of the producer for a bus connection into it (`onConsumerRestarted`, `MpegTsBusExecutor.ts`:149; not on the live add or the live swap). `BusFanoutCoordinator.reattachProducer` (on PLAYING) walks the applied connections only. So a producer that starts by itself later, an Audio Input (302M) on hot-plug (`onDeviceReconnected`, :150, its build taking the channel, :220), never got its connections back: in the engine's own lifecycle with HEAD's routing (c17 notes), the mic absent at the engine start gave 12 level-50 lines and nothing connected, and 3 s after the mic was plugged in still nothing; a Restart of the mic, or a device picked again and Restart (B-191), brought all three back. The live add skipped the edge wait for a producer whose pipeline was not launched (`producerAway`, `LiveInputBranch.ts`:64, B-192) and sent the add at once. The gate's text named `<module id> (<port>)` through the applied connections and fell back to the raw path for a socket no applied connection named (a stale replay after a disable; `GstPluginBase.ts`:535); the lost-input text used module ids (`liveInputBranches.ts`:61). **c15's review minors:** `handleBusGate` showed the lost-input text again only at a gate opening (`absent`), so a data wait's `waiting_for_data` then `data_arrived` left the module ok while it ran without inputs (:514); a source that never ran was "lost"; a second source wired to a one-source Audio Output (302M) got a branch from `getLiveInputBranch` (:146 counts the wired sources), so the add went to the direct pipeline, which has no mixer ("element 'mixin' not found", journal 06:40:11Z), and the warning "Live input add failed — module restart instead" came before the restart. **c14's:** `ModuleInstance.start` cleared `pendingRestart` after `onStart` (:133), so a change stored between the re-init and the end of that start was lost for the next Restart; B-191 counts 12 plugins that override `onInit`, not 11. **Fix (as built):** (1) A producer the engine knows but whose channel is not assigned throws `BusChannelPending` (an unknown producer stays a plain error). `MediaRouter` keeps such a connection out of the applied map in `waiting`, logs one info line naming both modules (`Connection [Mic 1 → Audio Mixer] waits for Mic 1: its output is not up yet`) and resolves. (2) The event: `BusChannelManager.onAcquired` tells the router of each allocation an owner did not hold; the waits on that producer (its module, or its module and port) run a tick later (the producer is inside its build), one at a time, under the lifecycle lock (`setWaitingScheduler`), so none runs inside a start, restart or engine start, nor two into one sink at once. A woken connection runs only while it still waits and its producer holds the channel; a sink that is not running keeps it (its own start applies it; corrected by B-196: only a start by the lifecycle re-applied, so a sink restarted outside it, by a consumer restart, kept the wait for ever; every start of the sink runs it now). Removing the connection, unregistering either module's ports and stopping or restarting the engine end a wait; a channel map edited meanwhile goes with it. No retry loop and no timeout (B-196 adds one check 10 s into each wait). The wait covers a producer that takes the channel at a build of its own; it does not cover one that is never rebuilt with the input that makes the output (corrected by B-196: an N-1 Audio Mixer (302M) given its first source on an input through a live add it could not take ran without it, so its output for that input never came). The ConnectionApplier logs no "Connected" for a wait and does not retry it; real failures (an unknown module or port, a type mismatch, capacity, a failure once the channel exists) stay loud. (3) A live add waits for the producer's edge socket before it sends `bus_input_add`: at once when it accepts within the 5 s wait; otherwise, or for a producer not launched, the module runs without the branch ("not running") and a background wait (`waitForBusSockets`, aborted once the branch is back, unwired or the module relaunched) adds it once the socket accepts; "Live input added" follows the runner's reply. The add clears the module's mark before it is sent, so a loss the runner reports after it stands (the field's order cleared it), and puts it back if the runner refuses. The producer's PLAYING (re-link, rejoin) stays the safety net. (4) `handleBusGate` shows the lost-input text after its own clearing whatever `absent` is; `LostInputs.lose` takes a kind: a launch without the input or a waiting add say "Input from X not running — continuing without it", a branch the runner dropped "lost"; Audio Output (302M) answers `getLiveInputBranch` only while the pipeline it launched is the mixer (a description refresh, which has a runner, leaves that), so a second source restarts a one-source output without an add, and a source disabled and enabled again on a two-source one still joins live. (5) Texts name modules: the gate's and the data wait's text by display name (`MediaRouter.moduleName`), a socket off the applied map by the module that holds, or last held, its channel port (`busSocketProducer`, `BusChannelManager.ownerOf`), "unknown module" only when no channel ever named it, never a path; the lost and not-running texts by display name. (6) `ModuleInstance.start` takes and clears `pendingRestart` before the re-init, puts it back if the start fails. No flag. **Fix round 1** (2026-10-31, the Fable review's minors; engineering calls, for the owner's veto): the patch router's and the local API's live connect line says `Live connect waits for its producer` for a connection that only waits (it said `Live connect`, next to the router's line that it waits). | Waiting is what a connection to a producer that is there but not up should do: the producer will take its channel when it builds, and that moment is the one event that says so, so a wait costs nothing and has no deadline, where a retry loop either gives up (the dropped mic) or polls for ever (B-196: so long as something builds the producer with the inputs that make that output; a wait is now checked once, after 10 s). In the router, because every apply path (the start's applier, a restart's re-apply, the patch router's live connect, the local API) meets in `createConnection`; in the lifecycle lock, because a woken apply restarts a sink and the lock already serialises every other restart. The live add's background wait is the gate's own (ADR-0010: unbounded, aborted when superseded), moved off the apply so a gated producer never holds the lock. | **What happens now** (the engine's tests on the dev Pi): through the engine's own lifecycle, applier and router with SWA01's chain (`connectionWait.test.ts`, new): an engine start with the mic present logs no level-50 line and all three connections come up (the mixer's and the transcoder's waited for their outputs, by name); a mic waiting for its device: no level-50 line, nothing retried meanwhile, all three up when it is plugged in, with no restart; a device picked again and Restart brings them up; a Restart of the mixer while the mic waits keeps the wait with no error; a wait woken during another module's Restart runs after it, no two relay starts at once. Live adds: no add before the edge socket accepts, then the add; a waiting branch gives up once added by another path or the sink relaunched; in the output's integration test, Chat IN enabled while the output plays is added only once its socket accepts and is never said lost, and a second source wired to a one-source output restarts it into the mix with no add tried and no warning. **Limits:** a connection into a sink at capacity is not counted while it waits (it fails loud when it runs); the woken apply holds the lifecycle lock for its executor's work (up to the 5 s edge wait of a live add); a live add's branch added at the producer's launch is still re-linked once at its PLAYING when the module predates it (rule 4's whole-module test), a short gap on that new input; the timing section's input rows and the aligner warnings still name `<module id> (<port>)`, and a connection reject's text `(from <module id>:<port>)`. **Tests:** `connectionWait.test.ts` (new, 5), `MediaRouter.waiting.test.ts` (new, 8), `BusChannelManager.test.ts` (+2), `busHelpers.test.ts` (+1), `ConnectionApplier.test.ts` (+1), `ModuleInstance.test.ts` (+2), `MpegTsBusExecutor.test.ts` (2 rewritten, +3), `GstPluginBase.liveInputs.test.ts` (texts, +3), `GstPluginBase.busGate.test.ts` (3 rewritten, +1), `liveInputBranches.test.ts` (2 updated, +1), the output's module test (1 updated, +2) and integration test (3 texts, +2; its fake runner refuses an add to a mixer its pipeline lacks, as the runners do). **Mutants,** 20 of 20 caught, among them no wait (11 tests fail), no wake (6), the executor's plain error (11), no lifecycle lock (1), the away producer's add at once (3), the mark cleared after the add (1), the data wait hiding the text (1), the old gate text (4) and the pending flag cleared at the end of a start (1). vitest: every engine and plugin suite, 228 files, 3548 passed, 4 skipped; typecheck: the engine and the 302M plugins, 0 errors; `gst_live_inputs_test.py` 58 and the native runner's live-input cases of `native_runner_protocol_test.py` 40, all pass (no runner changed). **Fix round 1, what happens now:** tests for two paths the review's mutants showed untested: a wait woken by its producer's port key (the mixer's and the transcoders' channels are per port, as SWA01's six were; `MediaRouter.waiting.test.ts` +1), and `Live input added` logged only after the runner's reply, on the spot and in the background join, never for a refused add (`MpegTsBusExecutor.test.ts` +2); the live connect line (`EnginePatchRouter.test.ts` +1, `CommandDispatcher.test.ts` +1). Mutants, 6 of 6 caught, the review's two among them. **Device check** (next round, not run): engine restart on a box with a 302M chain: no level-50 line, every connection up; an input waiting for its device for 3 minutes, then plugged in: its connections come up without a restart; enable a source of a running Audio Output (302M): no "lost" line before "Live input added". **Phase 3 line:** the same router, executor, applier and gate texts (p3w1 to p3w3 and p4w1): the fix goes there at the next carry merge, with its tests. Texts: this row and the intro, B-191's count and B-192's limits, ADR-0010 (amendment 2026-10-31), the release notes (Fixed), plugins/README.md (Live Input Branches), `PluginModule.noteLiveInputAbsent`. |
| B-195 | An audio input whose PipeWire stream died under it stayed "ok" and captured nothing until it was restarted by hand: after the Device Manager restarted PipeWire, both Audio Input (302M) captures lost their stream without a word (the owner's MR-021) | Release line (v2.0.0.100). Found 2026-10-31 on ZA-SCC-SWA01 (a Pi 4; the owner's bug log MR-021, the Device Manager's PipeWire restart for MR-019's buffer change), fixed the same day by c18 (the orchestrator's brief: a signal that names the cause first, a data stall as the backstop, a rebuild once PipeWire and the device are back within about 10 s, bounded and quiet while PipeWire stays down, never a restart on silence; the rest engineering calls, for the owner's veto). **Seen** (the box's journal 05:41:15-05:42:55Z, pw-top at 05:41:50Z, `wf13/ops2/swa01-dm/after-1.txt`): pipewire-pulse, WirePlumber and pipewire stopped and started again between 05:41:30.06Z and 05:41:30.27Z. The Audio Output (302M) runner got `Disconnected: Connection terminated [element: sink]` (`pulsesink.c` `gst_pulsering_is_dead`) and restarted itself 816 ms later. The two Audio Input (302M) runners (`pipewiresrc` on the SSL 2's Mic1 and Mic2 sources) posted nothing; at 05:41:32.37Z the engine logged level-40 `VU meter stalled` (gap 2700 and 3002 ms) for both, and nothing more: both modules ok and running, their `MR_PW_` nodes gone from the graph, the mic sources suspended, until module restarts at 05:42:38Z; each stop then waited out a 6 s EOS drain. **Cause** (PipeWire 1.6.3 = the image's recipe, SRCREV cc3d0d11, read from the build's git mirror; GStreamer 1.28.2): the daemon's hang-up reaches the client as a core error, `-EPIPE` (`module-protocol-native.c`:1096-1155); `gstpipewirecore.c`:19-30 only logs it, and `stream.c`:1506-1516 sets the stream UNCONNECTED; `gstpipewiresrc.c`'s `on_state_changed` (:893-935) posts an error only for ERROR; its `create()` returns `GST_FLOW_FLUSHING` for UNCONNECTED (:1578, :1697-1701), and `gstbasesrc.c`:3136-3188 pauses the task on FLUSHING with no error and no EOS (by design, for flushing seeks). The pipeline stays PLAYING with a dead source. `on-disconnect` (:614-690, default none) acts on buffer removal only, which a hang-up never does, and in error mode would fail a benign buffer re-allocation too. Reproduced on the dev Pi with a private daemon (PipeWire 1.2.7 there): after a kill and restart, no ERROR, EOS, WARNING or CLOCK_LOST, level messages 10/s to 0, the source task PAUSED, the stream node gone from the new graph. **What the engine did** (at 692a2610): the VU stall watch only logs (`GstPluginBase.ts`:78-82, ticks at :328); the device watchdog polls `hasDevice` every 2 s (`DeviceWatchdog.ts`:60, :111) on a listing cached 1 s (`AudioDeviceOps.ts`:108), so a 0.2 s outage never shows the device absent, and a longer one said "Device disconnected" (error, :118). While PipeWire stayed down, each failed `pactl list` logged a warning (`AudioDeviceOps.ts`:199) and `execFileSync` passed pactl's own stderr (2 lines) to the engine's stderr, the journal (`PaCommandQueue.ts`:60): about 3 lines a second. **Each PipeWire module on a restart, before and after:** Audio Input (302M), `pipewiresrc` on the device: before, the field case above (a restart longer than a poll: "Device disconnected", rebuilt when listed); after, rebuilt (below). Audio Output (302M), `pulsesink` on the device: before, the runner restarted it about 1 s later, recovered; while PipeWire stayed down, a runner restart every 1-5 s (about 8 lines each) until a poll saw the device absent; after, the sink's failure waits for PipeWire and the device (no restart loop), rebuilt within one poll of their return. Audio Input (deprecated), a remap-source in pipewire-pulse and a meter `pulsesrc`: before, the remap-source and its consumers' pw-links died with pipewire-pulse, the meter's error stood as a health error, no recovery; after, rebuilt, its outgoing pw-links re-executed. Audio Output (deprecated), a remap-sink and a meter on the device monitor: before, the same; after, rebuilt, its incoming pw-links re-executed (its existing reconnect path). AES67 In and AES67 Out: no PipeWire stream (`udpsrc`/`udpsink`), untouched before and after. Audio Encoder, Audio Decoder, Audio Dynamics and N-1 Audio Mixer (all deprecated): their null sinks and loopbacks die with pipewire-pulse, the encoder's `pipewiresrc` silently like the 302M input's, the decoder's and dynamics' `pulsesink` restarting into a null sink that is not there; they do not recover, before or after (not fixed: deprecated PipeWire-graph routing, neither inputs nor device outputs; a module or engine restart recovers them). **Fix (as built):** (1) The cause signal: `pactl info`'s `Cookie:` is the PipeWire daemon's core cookie (`impl-core.c`:417 `pw_rand32`, served by `pulse-server.c`:3350), new at every daemon start. `AudioDeviceOps.daemonInstance` reads it without blocking (`PaCommandQueue.execImmediateAsync`, shared per 1 s TTL); the device watchdog records the daemon the module's streams run on (at start, at each rebuild, and at every PLAYING, `adopt`), and a poll that finds another one tears the pipeline down ("PipeWire restarted"), checked before presence: right after a restart the device is often not listed yet (WirePlumber not back), and that is no unplug. (2) `DeviceWatchdog.lose(cause)`: the same teardown for a stream that failed or went silent, queued behind an in-flight poll. The health text names the cause: "PipeWire restarted — rebuilding the stream once PipeWire and the device are back"; a cause given while pactl gets no answer reads "PipeWire is not answering — …", and a restart found while waiting renames it. A later poll with the device listed rebuilds through the module's `onDeviceReconnected`, the unplug path. Losses in a run wait 0, 2, 4 … 60 s before their rebuild; a rebuilt stream that runs 60 s ends the run. One warning per loss, one line per rebuild. (3) A stream's own failure: `PipelineDescription.pipeWireElements` names the elements that hold it (the 302M input's `pipewiresrc name=capture`, the 302M output's `sink`, the deprecated pair's meter `pulsesrc name=capture`); the runner host marks their error `pipewire_lost` and turns its own restart off for that runner, error and exit alike (`GstRunner.ts`), and `GstPluginBase` hands it to the watchdog (`losePipeWireStream`) and keeps it from health error. (4) The backstop: `GstPluginBase.captureStallMs` (`PIPEWIRE_CAPTURE_STALL_MS`, 4 s; the 302M input and the deprecated input): no meter reading for that long while PLAYING is a lost stream; PLAYING arms it, any other state disarms it. A silent input still sends a reading a second (the runners' heartbeat), so silence is never a loss. (5) A device list nobody answers is unknown, not an unplug: the watchdog tears nothing down for it (a dead stream reports itself), `isAvailable` follows the listing, and the outage logs one warning and one line when pactl answers again; `execImmediate` keeps pactl's stderr in its error (`stdio` pipe). (6) A PA module is unloaded only while its ID still names the node it was loaded as (`PipeWireManager.unloadModule(id, name)`, `releaseAll`): pipewire-pulse hands the same IDs to the next loads after a restart (536870912 before and after on the private daemon), so a stale ID could unload another module's fresh remap. (7) The deprecated Audio Input re-executes its outgoing pw-links after a rebuild (`MediaRouter.reexecuteOutgoingPwLinks`, beside the incoming one). (8) The Audio Input (302M) sets `eosDrain: false`, the rule for audio-only bus producers: its drain timed out (6 s) at every stop on SWA01, and on the real test with it the rebuild came 9.6 s after PipeWire's return instead of 3.5 s. No runner changed, no flag. **Fix round 1** (2026-10-31, the Fable review's minors; engineering calls, for the owner's veto): (6)'s check asked `pactl list short modules` synchronously, on the event loop at every stop of a deprecated module, and took a listing with no answer for "gone", so a pactl hiccup while PipeWire ran would leave the module loaded and the next load of the same name collide; it now asks without blocking (`execImmediateAsync`), and a listing with no answer tries the unload, as before B-195; when that fails too, PipeWire is gone and its modules with it: an info line, not a warning. Its log line carried the node under `name`, pino's key for the component, so the line read as the node's: `node` now. The deprecated Audio Output gets no stall backstop: its meter reads the device's monitor, where a stall is an unplug (the poll's) or WirePlumber re-linking a pinned stream, which heals itself; its remap-sink is read by no meter, so no stall can show it lost; a PipeWire restart is found by the daemon's change and the meter's own error, as before. | `pipewiresrc` cannot report the hang-up, so the engine must notice it; the daemon's cookie names exactly the event that kills every PipeWire stream at once, costs one `pactl info` a second at most while a module watches, and cannot fire for a daemon that did not change. The stall covers what no event names (a stream unlinked, a node gone on the same daemon). The device watchdog already knew how to tear a module down and build it again once its device was listed (the unplug path, including the remap modules and their links); a PipeWire restart is that, with a cause. Rebuilding only once the device is listed is what keeps a long outage quiet: the runner's own restart loop restarts blind every 1-5 s. | **What happens now** (the dev Pi): with a private PipeWire daemon and pipewire-pulse under their own runtime dir (no D-Bus, ALSA or WirePlumber; never the desktop session's) and the real Audio Input (302M) on the native runner, real pactl, pw-dump and pw-link (`pipewireRestart.test.ts`): the daemons killed and restarted in about 0.2 s, the stream node gone from the new graph, the module warned "PipeWire restarted — …" and captured again 3.5 s after PipeWire was back, its node in the graph again; stopped 20 s, it warned "PipeWire is not answering — …", started no runner and wrote no log line and no pactl stderr for 15 s, and captured again 1.7 s after PipeWire's return.
