With the runner host real and the runner faked (`AudioInput302mModule.pipeWireLoss.test.ts`): the field case rebuilt within two polls, never a health error; three restarts in a row each rebuilt within 10 s, waiting 0, 2 and 4 s; a capture gone quiet on the same daemon rebuilt by the stall; 90 s of a silent mic, no rebuild; a failed capture element not restarted while its device is gone, rebuilt once it is listed. The Audio Output (302M)'s sink failing while PipeWire is down: no runner restart, rebuilt on the poll after its return. **Limits:** a PipeWire restart is found on the watchdog's next poll after pipewire-pulse answers again (up to 2 s, plus the 1 s TTL), and the rebuild comes one poll later (WirePlumber's device back first); an Audio Output (302M) on a quick restart now plays again after up to a poll more than the runner's own 1 s restart did; a restart of pipewire-pulse alone does not change the cookie (the daemon's), so the 302M input's `pipewiresrc`, which does not use it, is rightly left alone, and the pulse users report it themselves; the deprecated processing modules above are not covered. **Tests:** `pipewireRestart.test.ts` (new, real PipeWire, 2; skipped, saying why, without PipeWire, its GStreamer plugin, the elements or the runner), `AudioInput302mModule.pipeWireLoss.test.ts` (new, 6), `GstPluginBase.pipeWireLoss.test.ts` (new, 7), `PipeWireManager.test.ts` (new, 4), `DeviceWatchdog.test.ts` (+10), `AudioDeviceOps.test.ts` (+3), `GstChildProcess.inProcess.test.ts` (+2), `GstChildProcess.test.ts` (+1, the payload keys), `MediaRouter.test.ts` (outgoing re-link), the 302M input's (4 updated: the element's name, its `pipeWireElements` and no drain), the 302M output's module (+1) and integration (+1) tests, the deprecated Audio Input's (+2, 1 updated) and Audio Output's (+2, 1 updated). **Mutants,** 23 of 23 caught: no daemon check (4 tests fail, the field case among them), presence checked before the daemon (1), no stall backstop (4), the host's restart left on (1) or no `pipewire_lost` at all (3), the loss a health error (1), no back-off (2), a back-off that never ends (1), an unanswered list as an unplug (2), a log line per failed pactl (1), pactl's stderr inherited (the real test), any ID unloaded (3), no adoption at PLAYING (1), the warning before the teardown (1), no outgoing re-link (1), the 302M input's drain (2), the stall while not PLAYING (1), no arming at PLAYING (1), the failure not routed (4), no rename while waiting (2), a second teardown (2), the elements not declared (2 and 2). vitest: every engine and plugin suite, 232 files, 3589 passed, 4 skipped (the real test among them: capturing again 3.5 s after a restart, 1.7 s after a 20 s outage); typecheck: the engine and twelve audio and capture plugins, 0 errors; no python or native file changed, so no runner suite was run. **Fix round 1, what happens now:** the Audio Output (302M) on a real PipeWire (`plugins/audio-output-302m/tests/pipewireRestart.test.ts`, new, 2: a private PipeWire with a virtual sink, a 302M tone from a runner off PipeWire so only the output's recovery is timed, the real module on the native runner, a pw-link loop doing WirePlumber's linking of the stream): the daemons restarted in about 0.2 s, its `pulsesink` failed (`Disconnected: Connection terminated [element: sink]`), the runner restarted nothing, the module warned "PipeWire stream failed (Disconnected: Connection terminated) — …", never an error, and played into the sink again 1.5 to 1.8 s after PipeWire was back (the field's runner restart: 0.8 s); down about 16 s, no runner started or restarted and no log line but the outage's one warning, playing again 0.7 to 2.5 s after the return. The input's real test shares the private PipeWire (`packages/engine/src/audio/testing/privatePipeWire.ts`): 3.5 to 3.6 s and 1.6 to 1.7 s, as before; the output's test passed 13 runs of 13 on the dev Pi and the input's 11 of 11, one of each inside a full engine and plugin run and one side by side. `PipeWireManager.test.ts` 4 → 9: a listing with no answer still unloads, PipeWire gone is an info line and an answered failure a warning, the ID left alone is PipeWireManager's line naming the node, no synchronous pactl. Mutants, 8 of 8 caught, in a copy of the tree: a listing with no answer skipping the unload (the review's point; 2 tests fail), the listing asked synchronously (2), the failed unload while PipeWire is gone as a warning (1) or an answered one as an info line (1), the node under `name` on either line (1 each), the 302M output's sink not declared (the real test: an error, never the warning) and the runner host's own restart left on (the real test: its restart line). **Device check** (next round, not run here): on a test box with an audio input and a 302M chain, Restart PipeWire in the Device Manager: every audio module captures or plays again within 10 s with no manual action (time the Audio Output (302M) too, from PipeWire's return to sound from the device: 1.5 to 1.8 s on the dev Pi), the status shows the warning while PipeWire is down; three times; then PipeWire stopped for 60 s (`systemctl --user stop pipewire.socket pipewire-pulse.socket pipewire pipewire-pulse wireplumber`, started again after): no restart storm, one warning per module. **Phase 3 line:** the same watchdog, base and runner host (p3w1 to p3w3 and p4w1): the fix goes there at the next carry merge, with its tests. Texts: this row and the intro, the release notes (Fixed), plugins/README.md (Device Watchdog), `PipelineDescription.pipeWireElements`, `GstPluginBase.captureStallMs`. |
| B-196 | A connection held back at start-up waited for ever: an N-1 Audio Mixer (302M) output whose mix needs an input wired after the mixer had started never got its bus channel, because the mixer was never rebuilt with that input, and nothing warned (the owner's MR-027, a regression of B-194's fix build) | Release line (the fix build a59beb53, on no box). Found 2026-11-01 on the .103 test box by the device round DEV-FIX2, 2 times of 2: at the deploy's engine restart (18:36:41Z) and at a profile activation (19:01:04Z); v2.0.0.100 recovered the same start in about 4 s, 3 times of 3. Fixed 2026-11-02 by c19 (the orchestrator's brief: no connection may wait without an end while both its modules are enabled and its producer runs, with c17's gains kept, and a bounded check with one warning naming both modules wherever a wait could still outlive its cause, never a silent forever; the rest engineering calls, for the owner's veto). **Seen** (the box's engine journal, `j-deploy-183630-183930.txt`): 18:36:43.857Z `Producer port has no live branch — restarting producer for [N-1 Mixer (test rig) → N1 Out 1 meter]`, 44.114Z `Connection [N-1 Mixer (test rig) → N1 Out 1 meter] waits for N-1 Mixer (test rig): its output is not up yet`, then nothing for that connection through 18:39:16Z: the meter showed "No sources connected — wire 302M audio to Audio In", the Audio Transcoder behind it "No input connected", the N-1 Mixer ran ok, and its out-0 channel was never allocated (out-1 and out-2 at 43.85Z and again at 44.11Z). **Cause** (a59beb53; the cold check's reading corrected): an N-1 output takes its channel only at a build with a contributing input other than its own (`activeOutputIndices`, `n1Mixer302mPipeline.ts`:123); at 43.85Z only in-0 (N1 In 1) was applied, so out-0 rightly had none. N1 In 2 → in-1 ran at 44.593Z while N1 In 2's runner was not launched yet, so B-194's live add went to the background (`LiveInputBranch.ts`:79) and the connection counted as applied with no restart of the mixer; but `getLiveInputBranch` answered a branch for any wired input (`N1Mixer302mModule.ts`:52) and in-1 had no fan-in in the running pipeline. At N1 In 2's PLAYING the re-link sent the add, the runner refused it (`element 'inmix1' not found`, 44.690Z), and the fallback relaunched the same description (`BusFanoutCoordinator.ts`:171, `GstChildProcess.restartPipeline`), which also ended the background join without a word; the same for in-2 (45.010Z). So the mixer ran in-0 alone from then on: out-0 never came, the meter's wait was never woken, and N1 Out 2 and 3 meters carried one tone where they should have carried two. v2.0.0.100 sent that add on the spot, was refused (19:03:36.495Z `Live input add failed — module restart instead`) and restarted the mixer with in-0 and in-1, whose build took out-0 (36.761Z); the cascade then applied the meter's connection (36.763Z). The second lock the cold check named, `applyWaiting`'s return for a sink that is not running (`MediaRouter.ts`:429), did not hold on .103: it reads `ModuleInstance.running`, true for an idle Audio Mixer or Audio Transcoder from the end of its start (`ModuleInstance.ts`:136; an idle build returns no pipeline, `GstPluginBase.ts`:295), and the meter had started at 43.100Z; the manager's run=false is the plugin's PLAYING. It does hold for a sink stopped by a restart outside the lifecycle lock (a live connect's or a live remove's consumer restart, a live swap window's expiry, a producer bounce for another connection): the woken wait returned, and that start re-applies nothing of the sink's, so the wait had no end. **Fix (as built):** (1) The N-1 Audio Mixer (302M) answers `getLiveInputBranch` only for an input with a fan-in in the pipeline its runner runs (`launchedInputs`, set by a start's build, the one with no runner yet, as B-194's Audio Output (302M)); the first source on an input gets no branch, so the engine restarts the mixer into one at once (v2.0.0.100's outcome, without the refused add and its warning), and that build takes the outputs the input feeds, whose waits run on their channels. (4) audio-output-302m `SilentOutputWatch`: while PLAYING, a mixer arm with no meter reading for 1.5 s, 5 s on: "Plays nothing: its mixer delivers no audio — relaunched", and one relaunch (one per episode, at most one a minute); either arm, the sink's input lateness window's minimum more than 40 ms past ts-offset + its declared latency for 5 s: "Plays nothing: every buffer reaches the sink N ms past its playout time", no relaunch (it would replay the same pace and restart the re-anchor's hold); withdrawn when it plays again. on a chrony box the text is unchanged. **Phase 3 line:** the four files the fix changes are the same there (p3w1's head, 2026-11-02): it goes there at the next carry merge, with its tests. WI-P5-9 extends `ptpStatus.ts` (PARENT_DATA_SET's grandmaster, the domain), and its error under PTP, the larger of `estErrorUs` and the offset in µs (chapter 9 part 4.6, WI-P5-9), is always the kernel's 16 s: it should take `ptp.offsetNs`. | B-199 | While PipeWire was down, the engine started a PulseAudio daemon of its own, which took the sound cards and stayed after PipeWire came back (the owner's MR-028) | Release line (v2.0.0.100). Found 2026-11-01 on .108 (a Pi 4 test box, v2.0.0.100 image) in the c18 field check's 60 s PipeWire stop (DEV-FIX2), fixed 2026-11-02 by c22 (the orchestrator's brief: no PulseAudio client the engine starts may start a daemon, fixed in the engine so it ships with the app, today's behaviour while PipeWire is up, the image's part a finding for a later Yocto WI; the rest engineering calls, for the owner's veto). The row follows B-198 on this line: B-196 and B-197 are bug batch 3's, written at the same time on another clone, and the orchestrator orders the rows at the merge. **Seen** (`wf13/fix2/108/a4-mr021/down-window.txt` and the cold check `chk-108`): right after the stop (19:20:38Z) the engine's journal carried '[pulseaudio] pid.c: Stale PID file, overwriting' and 'module-alsa-card.c: Failed to find a working profile': a real PulseAudio (`/usr/bin/pulseaudio --start`) had taken the ALSA devices. The outputs played through it, the ATEM mic failed ('Failed to set pipeline to PLAYING'), the default sink moved to the KT USB card and the Cam Link source came back renamed '.2'; it stayed after PipeWire's return, one was there again after an engine start at 19:40Z, and only killing it cleared it. MR-029 (the Audio Output (302M) silent 36 s after that outage) was measured with it present. **Cause** (libpulse 17.0, the image's, read from the build's `pulseaudio-17.0.tar.xz`): a client that names no server tries the per-user socket (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/pulse/native`, pipewire-pulse's; `core-util.c`:1759-1806), then a system-wide one, and then forks `/usr/bin/pulseaudio --start` once (`context.c`:978-1060, :840-866, :688-756). Autospawn is on by default (`client-conf.c`:66), the image's `/etc/pulse/client.conf` leaves it commented, and the image ships the daemon (`pulseaudio-server` in `local.conf`'s IMAGE_INSTALL). The engine named no server: `pactl` on all three paths of `PaCommandQueue.ts` (the device watchdog's listings, the B-195 cookie, module loads and volumes) and every `pulsesrc` (`pulsesrc.c`:1015 connects with no flags: the deprecated Audio Input's capture, the deprecated Audio Output's meter, Audio Dynamics, the base class's VU pipeline) could start it; `pulsesink` asks libpulse for no autospawn itself (`pulsesink.c`:553). B-195's real-PipeWire tests never met it: their harness names the server. **Fix (as built):** `packages/engine/src/audio/pulseServer.ts` (new): the Engine's constructor, before anything starts, sets `PULSE_SERVER` in its own env to `unix:` and `$PULSE_RUNTIME_PATH/native`, else `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/pulse/native`, else `/run/user/<uid>/pulse/native`, unless a server is named already. libpulse turns autospawn off whenever `PULSE_SERVER` is set ('We disable autospawning automatically if a specific server was set', `client-conf.c`:110-116), after reading any client.conf, so it holds even against `autospawn = yes`. Every pactl call copies `process.env` (`PaCommandQueue.ts`), both runners are spawned with a copy of it (`runnerEnv()`, `PythonProcess.ts`) and `ManagedProcess` merges it, so every client the engine and its plugins start carries it. No flag. | It names the socket libpulse tries first today, where pipewire-pulse listens (its default `unix:native` in that dir), so while PipeWire is up every client connects as before; while PipeWire is down they fail with the same 'Connection refused' as before, pactl and the GStreamer elements alike, so B-195's handling is unchanged, and no daemon is tried. `PULSE_CLIENTCONFIG` with `autospawn = no` works too, but libpulse then reads only that file, never `/etc/pulse/client.conf` or its `.d` (`core-util.c`:1947-2017), and it needs a file on disk; a server per call site (`pactl -s`, an element's `server`) misses the next client. | **What happens now** (the dev Pi, `pulseServer.test.ts`): a private runtime dir with no server, a stand-in daemon named by `PULSE_BINARY` (libpulse execs its daemon by absolute path, never from PATH), a client.conf with `autospawn = yes` (the image's default; this Pi's Debian libpulse turns it off): with no server named, the engine's pactl wrapper on its three paths and a `pulsesrc` on each runner started the stand-in, five calls, the field's case; pinned as the engine does, the same seven clients failed with the same 'Connection refused' and started none. The rig before the code (`mr-captures/wf13/c22/rig/`) showed the same with `pactl` and `gst-launch-1.0` directly, and a stand-in first on PATH never called. **Limits:** a PulseAudio client started outside the engine (a pactl typed over SSH, the Device Manager, other apps on the box) still autospawns: the image's part below; an engine started with `PULSE_SERVER` already set keeps that server. **Image (finding, for a later Yocto-repo WI):** install `/etc/pulse/client.conf.d/50-media-router.conf` with `autospawn = no` (libpulse 17.0 reads `client.conf.d/*.conf` after client.conf, `conf-parser.c`:222-291), the way OE-core's `pulseaudio-client-conf-sato` installs its drop-in: a small meta-custom recipe added to IMAGE_INSTALL (`build/conf/local.conf`). Leaving the daemon out is the other way, but OE-core's `pulseaudio.inc` packs `${bindir}/pactl` into `pulseaudio-server` with it (`FILES:${PN}-server`), so dropping that package drops the pactl the engine needs. A `~/.config/pulse/client.conf` would hide the drop-in (libpulse reads one main file); no image recipe installs one. **Tests:** `pulseServer.test.ts` (new, 5: the address 2, the pin 1, the rig 2), `Engine.test.ts` (+1). **Mutants,** 10 of 10 caught: the pin a no-op (3 tests fail), no pin in the constructor (1), a named server overwritten (1), `PULSE_RUNTIME_PATH` ignored (1), no `pulse` subdir (5), the wrong variable (3), the runners' env without it (1: two calls) and each of pactl's three paths without it (1 each: one call). **Device check** (next round, not run here): on .108, stop PipeWire for 60 s, its sockets too: no pulseaudio process appears; after PipeWire returns every audio module comes back (MR-021's checks), and the Audio Output (302M)'s return time is measured again (MR-029). **Phase 3 line:** the Engine's constructor, `runnerEnv()` and `PaCommandQueue` are the same there (p3w1's head, 2026-11-02): it goes there at the next carry merge, with its tests. Texts: this row and the intro, the release notes (Fixed), plugins/README.md (pulse elements). |
| B-200 | A hung PipeWire froze the engine: the audio device listing ran `pactl` synchronously, so while pipewire-pulse took the call and never answered, each 2 s poll held the event loop for up to 10 s, and the UI, the API and every module with it; and the asynchronous pactl calls read such a timeout as an empty answer (the owner's MR-023) | Release line (v2.0.0.100). Found 2026-10-31 in c18's code review (the owner's bug log MR-023; not seen on a box), fixed 2026-11-02 by c23 (the orchestrator's brief: the device listing asynchronous and non-blocking, one at a time, its answers in order, its timeout kept; "no answer yet" unknown to the device watchdog, never "device gone"; every other synchronous child-process call listed, the hot-path ones converted where safe; the rest engineering calls, for the owner's veto). The row follows B-199 on this line: B-196 and B-197 are bug batch 3's, written at the same time on another clone, and the orchestrator orders the rows at the merge. **Seen** (in the code, and on the dev Pi, `mr-captures/wf13/c23/rig/`): `PaCommandQueue.execImmediate` ran `execFileSync('pactl', …, { timeout: 5000 })`. `AudioDeviceOps.listDevices` called it twice (sources, then sinks) on each cache miss, for the two PipeWire device providers' 2 s polls, the manager heartbeat's device snapshot (10 s), the devices API route, each audio module's device watchdog (2 s), the audio modules' init, start and reconnect (`hasDevice`, `getDeviceInfo`, the format helpers) and the 302M modules' `buildPipeline`; `waitForSink`, `waitForSource` (50 ms polls in the starts and rebuilds of modules with a null sink or a remap source) and `cleanupOrphans` (engine start and reset) called it too. Real pactl against a socket that accepts and never answers (`rig/hang.txt`): `execFileSync` held the event loop for the whole timeout, then threw ETIMEDOUT. The asynchronous calls went wrong the other way. On `execFile`'s timeout Node sends SIGTERM; pactl handles it itself and ends with status 0 and no output ("Got SIGINT, exiting.", `pactl.c`:2527-2530 and :3239-3240 in the image's pulseaudio-17.0; `rig/pactl-sigterm.txt`), and `execFile` reports a child that ends with 0 as success (Node 20's `exithandler`; `rig/killsig.txt`). So c18's `pactl info` read a hung PipeWire as an answer (the outage's warning and "answers again" line would alternate at every poll), its `list short modules` as "gone or no longer ours" (the module left loaded, where B-195 meant to unload it), and a queued `unload-module` or `set-*-volume` as done. **Every synchronous child-process call in the engine and the plugins, before c23:** `PaCommandQueue.ts`:60 (`execImmediate`, through `AudioDeviceOps.ts`:205 and `PipeWireManager.ts`:205, :224 and :324: the readers above, the listing periodic, the waits on every start and rebuild); `plugins/video-encoder/engine/videoEncoderPipeline.ts`:201 (`execFileSync('v4l2-ctl', ['--device', …, '--list-formats-ext'])`, 2 s timeout, in `buildV4l2Source` from `VideoEncoderModule.buildPipeline`: once per start of a V4L2 capture, neither periodic nor PipeWire); test code only: `audio/testing/privatePipeWire.ts`:11, :24, :185, :209 and `child-process/testing/ingestQueueRig.ts`:14, :42 (`spawnSync`), `examples/test-engine.ts`:48 (`execFileSync` of pkill at exit). The python runners and sidecars run in processes of their own and start no subprocess at runtime. **Fix (as built):** (1) `PaCommandQueue` has no synchronous call: `execImmediate` is gone, its readers ask with `execImmediateAsync`. One `run()` serves it and the queue, with `killSignal: 'SIGKILL'`: a timeout always ends pactl killed and fails as "no answer within 5000 ms" (the timeout unchanged, a constructor argument for tests). A queued command's caches still drop before its caller goes on. (2) `AudioDeviceOps.listDevices`, `hasDevice` and `getDeviceInfo` return promises. A listing runs one at a time (`SharedRead.ts`, new): readers that come while it waits share it, its answer is kept for the 1 s TTL after it lands, and a mutation that settles while one runs (`onMutation`) makes the next reader's listing start when that one is done. So no two overlap, answers land in the order they started, and none is older than the last mutation before its reader asked. Its two lists are asked together, sources first in the result, each with its own timeout: a hung PipeWire costs a reader 5 s, not 10. `pactl info` (B-195's cookie) goes the same way, one at a time, where c18 started another every TTL while one hung. (3) The device watchdog awaits the listing and the daemon together. A listing that waits changes nothing, a timed-out one is unknown (`isAvailable` false, as c18 made it), never an unplug, and no listing piles up behind it (the in-flight guard skips the ticks). A stream lost meanwhile is torn down when that listing settles. (4) The device providers' `list()` awaits the listing; `detectDeviceFormat`, `resolveDeviceFormat` and `tryResolveDeviceFormat` are async; Audio Input, Audio Output and both 302M modules await `hasDevice`. (5) `buildPipeline` is synchronous (the base calls it so), so the 302M modules read their device's width with `getDeviceInfo` before every start and reconnect build and keep it for that run. (6) `waitForSink`, `waitForSource` and `cleanupOrphans` ask without blocking. Left: the Video Encoder's v4l2-ctl probe (a capture's start only, bounded at 2 s, not PipeWire; it needs the probe in the module's own `onStart`, inside the V4L2 enumeration blackout, a later WI). No flag. | Asked without blocking, a hung PipeWire waits only on its readers. One listing at a time keeps the order the synchronous code had for free and the listing cache's spawn rate, and piles no pactl processes up on a daemon that does not answer. SIGKILL is the one end pactl cannot turn into a success; a read-only call loses nothing by it, and a mutating one whose request was sent is in the same place after SIGTERM. A width read before the build keeps `buildPipeline` synchronous for every plugin; a device does not change its width under a run (an unplug rebuilds). | **What happens now** (the dev Pi): against a stand-in pactl first on PATH that hangs as pactl does, with the engine's real pactl path (`hungPipeWire.test.ts`; the built engine in `rig/hung-e2e.txt`): over 2.5 s hung, 75 polls (the watchdog and two providers, every 100 ms) asked 1 listing and 1 `pactl info`, a 20 ms timer was at worst 1 ms late, the watchdog changed nothing and `isAvailable` went false; answering again, the device was listed 0.2 s later with nothing rebuilt; an answered unplug is still one. The built engine with real pactl and a socket that never answers (`rig/built-engine.txt`): the listing, the cookie and the orphan cleanup, asked together, all failed as no answer at the 1.5 s timeout, with the outage's one warning and the cleanup's own, the device unknown, a 20 ms timer at worst 11 ms late. **Limits:** a reader still waits for the answer up to the 5 s timeout: a module started while PipeWire does not answer says "not connected — waiting for hot-plug" after 5 s and starts when PipeWire answers (as before, without the freeze); a teardown meanwhile takes about 10 s (its module listing, then the unload), off the event loop; the device pickers list nothing while PipeWire does not answer (as since B-195); the Video Encoder's v4l2-ctl probe still blocks up to 2 s at a capture's start. **Found on the way** (not fixed here): `pw-dump` and `pw-link` handle SIGTERM the same way (`pw-link.c`:856-861 and :1064-1065, `pw-dump.c`:1550 and :1668-1669 at the image's PipeWire, cc3d0d11): against a socket that never answers each ended with 0 and no output (`rig/pwtools-sigterm.txt`), so the engine's `PwLinkOps.ts` and `streamPortLinks.ts` calls (default SIGTERM) read a timed-out call on a hung PipeWire daemon as an empty answer (no links, a link made); the same `killSignal` and killed check fix it, a later WI. **Tests:** `PaCommandQueue.test.ts` (new, 5), `SharedRead.test.ts` (new, 5), `hungPipeWire.test.ts` (new, 1; with the stand-in in `audio/testing/fakePactl.ts`, skipped, saying why, where the tmp dir cannot run it), `AudioDeviceOps.test.ts` (+5, 6 updated), `DeviceWatchdog.test.ts` (+2), `PipeWireManager.test.ts` (+2, 1 updated), the 302M output's and input's (+2 each, their harnesses updated), `deviceFormat.test.ts` (16 updated), `pipeWireDeviceProvider.test.ts` (7 updated), `pulseServer.test.ts` (its pactl listing asked without blocking). **Mutants,** 14 of 14 caught, in a copy of the tree (`mr-captures/wf13/c23/mutants/`): c18's SIGTERM timeout (4 tests fail), a blocking listing behind a promise (4), no single flight (5), an invalidate that joins the running read (3), a read older than an invalidate kept (1), reads that overlap (2), the caches dropped after the caller (2), a failed listing marked available (3), no answer read as an unplug (3), each 302M module's build asking PipeWire itself (2 each), no width read before the output's start build (1) or either module's reconnect build (1 each). **Device check** (next round, not run here): on .108, freeze pipewire-pulse (`kill -STOP`) for 15 s: the engine's API and the manager's view keep responding; after `kill -CONT` every audio module recovers. **Phase 3 line:** p3w1's head (c6038d39, 2026-11-02) has neither B-195 nor this, its listing the synchronous one: this goes there after B-195, at the next carry merge, with its tests. Texts: this row and the intro, the release notes (Fixed), plugins/README.md (Device Watchdog, Available Services). |
| B-201 | An Audio Transcoder with no source logged 'MpegTsProbe No audio caps detected' at every re-probe, every 10 s, and a few idle transcoders pushed real errors out of the engine's 1000-line log within minutes (the owner's MR-006) | Release line (v2.0.0.100). Found 2026-10-30 on ZA-SCC-SWA01, ZA-SCC-SWA-Master01 and ZA-SCC-FRA-Master01 on '302M' by the fleet's apply lane (the owner's bug log MR-006), fixed 2026-11-02 by c24 (the orchestrator's brief: the first miss once, then only changes, and the wait in the module's status; the rest engineering calls, for the owner's veto). Rows B-196 to B-200 are written in parallel batches; this row sits after B-195 until the orchestrator orders them at the merge. **Seen** (the engine's log ring and journal, the session's `wf13/fleet/` and `wf13/fix1/` notes, the captures' `wf13/fix1/` and `wf13/fix2/`): FRA-Master01 30 Oct 10:19:00-10:20:42Z, all 21 warnings were this line; 31 Oct 06:12-06:22Z, of the 534 lines the engine logged, 120 were this warning and 120 the probe's 'Probing MPEG-TS stream' info line (two VV transcoders behind a TS Splitter that sent nothing, a probe each every 10 s, 3 s each); SWA-Master01 30 Oct 10:15:28-10:16:28Z, all 25 listed warnings (four transcoders); SWA01 30 Oct 10:40-10:43Z, 54 warnings and 54 info lines in 3 min (three transcoders behind SRT Inputs whose peers were down: a probe took 73 ms at the median, the edge socket absent, up to the 3 s timeout). **Cause:** `probeMpegTsStream` logged every run (info) and every miss (warning); the Audio Transcoder's re-probe loop (ADR-0009) runs it every 10 s while its build is the decodebin fallback, without end; and the ring keeps the last 1000 lines of every level (`LOG_RING_MAX`), the boxes running pino at debug (LOG_LEVEL unset), so a debug line per run would churn it as well. The Audio Decoder (deprecated) probes once per start, never on a timer: four misses in the 30 s after FRA-Master01's rollback (two decoders, two starts each), then none in the next 28 min. **Fix (as built):** (1) The probe logs nothing per run; its result carries what it found. (2) The transcoder reports each result once per change (`probeReport.ts`, `ProbeReport`): the first, then only another (no audio caps, audio caps no classifier knows, a codec; with the producer), kept across its own restarts, so the self-heal cycle's start probe of a source just identified adds nothing. Each line names the module and its producer by display name (`MediaRouter.moduleName`), the producer's id, port and socket in the object: "FRA IN: no audio from VV yet — waiting for it" (info: a wait, as B-194's), "… no audio from VV any more — waiting for it" (a warning: audio from that producer was seen before, a loss, as B-195's), "… audio from VV is aac, 2 channels" (info, its caps in the object), "… has a codec the probe does not know — using the generic decoder" (a warning, with the caps). The per-start 'Stream probe' line and the self-heal's 'Source identified — rebuilding decoder chain' are these lines now. (3) The status with no audio at all reads "No source — waiting for audio from <producer> (checked every 10 s)", set by the build and re-asserted at each tick as before (the tick's result now goes to the hook), never logged; audio of a codec no classifier knows keeps the old text. (4) The Audio Decoder's per-start 'Stream probe' line carries the caps the probe's own line did. No flag, no other module changed. | A line per probe says nothing new after the first: the operator needs a change, and the module's status already shows what it waits for. Every level counts in the ring, so the probe's run line had to go too, not only its warning. The state is the module's, where the producer and the display names are known; the probe stays a function. | **What happens now** (the dev Pi): the built probe on real sockets (GStreamer 1.28.2, a private registry) wrote no line in 12 runs: 5 on a missing socket (27 ms each), 4 on an idle `unixfdsink` (3.0 s each, no caps), 3 on a live Opus TS (0.6 s, opus); with no classifier registered, the registry's once-per-process warning, as before. The transcoder module with the real probe (only gst-launch answered, `AudioTranscoderModule.probeLog.test.ts`), every logger recorded: 30 ticks of an idle source, one line in all, "FRA IN: no audio from VV yet — waiting for it", the status "No source — waiting for audio from VV (checked every 10 s)"; the source starting, one line ("… audio from VV is aac, 2 channels"), the restart, ok, no more probes; the source quiet and the module restarted, one warning ("… no audio from VV any more — waiting for it"), then nothing for 30 ticks; audio of an unknown codec found by a tick, one warning and the old text. **Limits:** a source that sends a stream in which the probe finds no audio (MR-007's A/V stream straight from an SRT Input) reads "No source" too; the TS Splitter's stats lines at debug (below) still fill the ring, now in about half an hour on FRA-Master01. **Findings** (other lines that repeat in the 30 Oct to 1 Nov logs; not fixed here): (a) the TS Splitter's `{"stats":…}` line at debug every 2 s per splitter: 294 of FRA-Master01's 534 lines in 10 min (31 Oct); 352 lines from four splitters in 2.8 min on the Pi 5 test box (1 Nov); (b) Audio Processing's status poll asking its dynamics element for `reduction-level-meter` and `sidechain-level-meter`, which it lacks (the Pi 5 test box, the #689 rig, 1 Nov 18:36-18:39Z): 314 debug lines 'getElementProperty failed' in 2.8 min (`GstPluginBase.getElementProperty` logs every failed read), and as many 'Command error' lines in the journal; (c) an SRT Input caller whose peer is down restarts its runner every 5-11 s for good, and each consumer of it with it ('producer bus socket … went away while waiting for its first data — reconnecting'): on SWA01 30 Oct 10:40-10:43Z, 82 pipeline starts in 3 min, at attempt 164, journal only; (d) 'Waiting for producer bus socket(s)' every 30 s per gated runner (FRA-Master01 30 Oct, B-190's case), journal only; (e) bursts at a start or a switch, not timers: 'Consumer pipeline predates its producer — … relaunching' with 'Live input re-link failed' and 'Live input add failed' (FRA-Master01 30 Oct 10:50Z: 5, 3 and 3 in 15 s; the Pi 4 test box 1 Nov: 5 in 3.4 min), the 'has not assigned a bus channel yet' retries and errors (B-194's, fixed on this line), 'VU meter stalled' once per stall. NYA-Master01 (2 Nov, the apply lane's notes): this line 60 a minute. **Tests:** `AudioTranscoderModule.probeLog.test.ts` (new, 2), `probeReport.test.ts` (new, 7), `MpegTsProbe.spawn.test.ts` (+1: 61 runs, no line from any logger), `AudioTranscoderModule.test.ts` (+1, three texts updated), `reprobeLoop.test.ts` (the tick's result handed over). Mutants, 13 of 13 caught: the probe warning per miss, a debug line per run, no dedup, the producer ignored, the loss as info, no loss branch, the old text always, the module's own name for its producer, the tick's or the start's result not reported, a report made afresh at each start, the start's text kept at a tick, the loop dropping the tick's result. **Device check** (next round, not run here): on a box with an idle Audio Transcoder, 10 minutes of log: at most one 'no audio' line per transcoder, and its status shows the wait. **Phase 3 line:** the same probe and transcoder; the fix goes there at the next carry merge, with its tests. Texts: this row and the intro, the release notes (Fixed), ADR-0009's amendment. |
| B-202 | A module stopped while its pipeline was still going to PLAYING could wait out the stop until the engine killed its runner, 8 s later: the EOS drain deadlocked in GStreamer, in both runners (the owner's MR-022) | Release line (v2.0.0.100). Found 2026-10-31 by c16's test gate (`gst_udp_silence_test.py`'s last stop hung in about 5 runs in 100, on the base runner too; B-193's Limits; the owner's bug log MR-022; not seen on a box), fixed 2026-11-02 by c25 (the orchestrator's brief: no deadlock at a stop before PLAYING, the drain of a PLAYING pipeline unchanged, both runners alike; the brief's proposed shape, no drain before PLAYING, replaced by the one below, an engineering call, for the owner's veto). Rows B-196 to B-200 are written in parallel batches; this row sits after B-201 until the orchestrator orders them at the merge. **Cause** (GStreamer 1.28.2: `gstbasesrc.c`:1955-1960, `gstbin.c`:2569 (an async sink's PLAYING held back) and :3210 (the continuation's state lock), `gstbasesink.c`:2526-2534 (the commit, then the preroll wait); c16's gdb trace of the hang): the pipeline is READY or PAUSED with PLAYING pending, and a source's streaming thread, holding its pad's stream lock, is parked in a sink's preroll (the bin holds an async sink's PLAYING back until it prerolls, so the sink commits PAUSED and waits). The sink's ASYNC_DONE schedules the pipeline's continuation to PLAYING, which takes the pipeline's state lock first. The drain goes ahead in that state, the pending state checked on purpose (at 3b6f7bf3: `eos_drain`, `runner.cpp`:158-186; `_eos_drain`, `gst-pipeline-runner.py`:227-272), and its `gst_element_send_event(pipeline, EOS)` holds that state lock while `gst_base_src_send_event` waits for the stream lock. Nothing moves until the engine's kill. Live and non-live sources alike (a non-live one flows data in PAUSED up to the preroll); a queue between the source and the sink keeps the source's thread free. Reproduced every time with the first buffer held before the sink (identity's sleep) and the stop inside the hold: the bare live source, a non-live one, a second sink that never prerolls, two live sources into `audiomixer`. **Fix (as built),** both runners (`send_drain_eos`, `_send_drain_eos`): before PLAYING the drain sends the EOS that `gst_bin_send_event` would, to each source child (`gst_bin_iterate_sources`) under that child's own state lock, but not under the pipeline's. The continuation then runs: it sets the sinks to PLAYING first, the parked thread moves on and frees the stream lock, and the continuation meets the source's state lock (`gstbin.c`:2454) only after that. A PLAYING pipeline (or a lone element) still gets `gst_element_send_event` as before; the errored path, the decoder-branch drain and the 6 s budget are unchanged, and so is the rest of a stop: the edge paths released before the drain (B-190, with B-193's edges still detaching), queued attaches dropped and teardown records kept, the keyframe gate and the shedder stopped after the drain. No flag. | Not the brief's skip ("nothing has flowed" before PLAYING): data does flow. The deadlock itself has a buffer in the sink's preroll, a non-live source flows in PAUSED up to the preroll, and a decoder decodes its preroll frames; the drain checks the pending state for that reason (its docstring since 2026-08-05: a stateless HEVC decoder stopped mid-decode takes a Pi 4 down). A skip would land NULL in a decoder's first-frame burst whenever a stop came there, and the Video Player's decodebin3 bootstrap is stopped by its own codec report right after it starts (the `tsprobe:videoinfo` rebuild): when its first keyframe has just come, that stop is before PLAYING, and today's drain covers it (the player's queues keep it out of the deadlock). Sent source by source, the EOS keeps that drain and drops only the lock that held the change to PLAYING. Not a wait for PLAYING before the EOS: a bounded wait costs every stop of a pipeline with no data yet, and a first keyframe arriving at its end puts the decoder mid-burst at NULL all the same. | **What happens now** (the dev Pi, GStreamer 1.28.2): a live pipeline whose first buffer is held 1.5 s before the sink, stopped inside the hold, stops in 1.5 s in both runners and is still drained: its `wavenc` has written the WAV header's final size, which it does only at EOS (`native_runner_protocol_test.py`, new case stop-while-starting, 4 checks a runner); the base runners deadlock and are killed at 6.5 s. (2) A member whose counted lateness (the B-57 level, once it counts) is over the ceiling, or 1 h or more ahead (a stamp off the clock), is `beyond`: its peaks leave the window as on a leave, so the pace falls at once by the B-82 rule (by at most 1 s, then 1 s every 2 s) and reports no steadiness; it comes back once its level is 1 s under the ceiling (`BEYOND_BACK_NS`: 3 s). No flag. | A pace is the delay every input of the aggregator takes, and each input's queue holds 5 s: past that an input on time is held upstream and, behind a 5 s leaky bus ingress, cut; so a pace past the queue can align nothing and only loses content. 4 s leaves 1 s for jitter; paces in service are tens to a few hundred ms (FRA's healthy 'VV' muxer 131 ms, the bus's mux budget 1.2 s). Beyond is judged on the counted level, not a sample: a lone late buffer is no reason, and the B-57 rules already tell a steady lateness from a drain. Its peaks leave at once because the group goes on without it: its old needs would hold every other input up for fall-after for nothing; the others' needs keep B-82's window (the owner's Q4, steady for minutes). So once every input is steady the pace comes down at B-82's rate, 1 s every 2 s (0.5 s a second; from the ceiling in 8 s), and that is safe: a skip releases at most 1 s of content already queued in every input's queue (at most 4 s of 5 s), continuous, nothing lost or repeated (B-82's F1); downstream gets at most 1 s more every 2 s (1.5 times real time), which a 5 s aligner queue and a network receiver take; and no remaining input turns late, since the target is never under a need that counted. The 1 s back keeps an input that hovers at the ceiling from flapping, each rejoin costing B-80's 2Δ + 0.5 s. The stream rule keeps the catch-up off the re-anchor's case, a source that is late rather than out (B-205's re-anchor in batch 7): such an input loses its first second, not its lateness. GAPs too: a stale GAP set a mix's start as far back as a stale buffer. At the ingress taps, not the watches where it was built first: there the decoder thread freed the burst's unixfd memory at full speed beside the thread that reads the socket, and GStreamer's unixfd deadlock (Limits) came in 11 of 13 rig runs of a 120 s stop, against 2 of 8 with no catch-up. The seed cap: up to the ts-offset the sink plays from its whole ring, past it every buffer is late; a cap at the budget (ts-offset + 100 ms) left the real test silent (90 ms of ring). The playout watch reads the sink's own lateness per buffer in the runner, so the reason shows within about a second. A raise as state: the brief's fourth point; the raise itself stays until the head's offset is edited (memory only, unchanged). | **What happens now** (the dev Pi, the .108 rig on a private PipeWire, `pipewireRestartMix.test.ts`, new, 3 cases): PipeWire down 6 s with the mics, the mics back as the output rebuilds: the mix 1.2 s after the rebuild, never raised, no "Plays nothing", no silence in the 18 s after (past the re-anchor's hold), health ok, one "Caught up at the start: skipped 7.6 s of Mixer, …" line; rebuilt 1 s after the Mixer's burst, with a seed read during it: it plays at its own D; the mics back 5 s after the rebuild: the SRT leg 2.8 s after the rebuild (the silent Mixer input gapped at its W, MR-003's bound), the mix 0.9 s after the mics, no silence after. The scripted repro of run 2 (scratch, `mr-captures/wf13/c29/repro-*`): PipeWire down 6 s, 4 of 4 clean on the final build (the pace at most 7 to 17 ms after the rebuild, no "queue full", no raise, the mix heard 1 to 2 s after the rebuild), where the base runner latched 4 of 4 (1.9 to 3.5 s, raised); with the probe at the watches, 6 s ×4 and 3 s ×6 clean as well; a 120 s stop with the mics, 5 of 5 clean, both channels 1.6 to 1.9 s after the rebuild (the base runner: 2 of 8 wedged, Limits (a)). `restartWhileDark.test.ts` 5 of 5 (the mics 1.0 s after the restart, a dark leg costs them 30 to 90 ms, the late leg's "Plays nothing: every buffer reaches the sink 413 ms past its playout time" until the raise lands), c18's real tests (the output back 1.5 s and 0.6 s after PipeWire returned, the inputs 3.6 s and 1.8 s), the N-1's `absentInput.test.ts` 1 of 1. A routine start logs its edge backlog in the line, 20 to 43 ms at the taps. **Limits:** (a) **GStreamer's unixfd deadlock** (found on the way; gdb stacks `mr-captures/wf13/c29/wedge-r2/`): 1.28.2's unixfdsink sends each buffer to its consumers under its object lock, and unixfdsrc tells its producer a buffer is free under its own; a burst big enough to fill the socket both ways (the Audio Mixer's 120 s, tens of thousands of buffers) blocks both sends, and the threads that would read each socket wait on those locks: the producer's main loop then blocks on the sink's lock in `gst_bin_get_by_name` (its RPCs time out, its meter stalls), and the consumer's pipeline stays PAUSED pending PLAYING (its continuation waits on the source's lock) until its 10 s watchdog relaunches it and the stop runs into the kill, about 20 s; after it the Mixer runs about 1.2 to 1.4 s late (its pace from the mic content held meanwhile, MR-034's mechanism, B-204 in batch 7) and the output raises its route for that late source, as the brief's second point asks. In the rig's 120 s stop: 2 of 8 runs with no catch-up, 11 of 13 with the catch-up at the watches, 0 of 5 at the taps. A 4 to 5 s burst (a Device Manager restart) never wedged. Not fixed here: the fix is the elements' (send outside the lock, a patch in the image like B-68's queue) or a producer that does not send its stall at all; it is the likely cause of MR-037. (b) The Audio Mixer still sends its stall as a burst: the output skips it, but the Mixer's own fresh audio comes behind it (its producer side; the Mixer's pace after a stall is B-204's). (c) An input that sends nothing at all at a launch is gapped at its W (2.8 s after the rebuild in the rig, MR-003's 3 s), and the others wait that long. (d) "ok" can show at a launch for up to about 1.2 s, until the playout watch's first verdict; from it on, and across a relaunch, it is never ok while late. A rebuilt pipeline that never reaches PLAYING (the wedge in (a)) shows ok: the device watchdog sets ok right after the rebuild starts (B-195's), a finding. (e) The route head keeps its own warning while a raise stands (unchanged); the raise itself stays until the head's offset is edited. (f) A source late from its first buffer loses its first second at a launch (the stream rule), or its lateness if that is under a second; content that late could not have played on time. (g) Native only; and only with the image's `mrlateness` (the taps), which every box with this output has. **Tests:** native_runner_protocol_test.py: CU (new: a stream 2 s behind skipped for its first second, then passed; one report at the deadline with a dark input, at once when every input delivered; a branch added live reports alone), CB (new: a backlog 4 s back skipped whole, as buffers and as GAPs) and PW (new: missing after 1 s of late buffers, once, playing again after 200 ms in budget), and the whole suite 661 PASS at load under 3 (627 + 34); the runner's `make test`. vitest: `pipewireRestartMix.test.ts` (new, 3, real PipeWire), `restartWhileDark.test.ts` (its rig now `mixRig.ts`, shared), `catchUp.test.ts` (new, 2), `busHelpers.test.ts` (+1, the tap name), `backlogShed.test.ts` (+2), `GstPluginBase.playoutReanchor.test.ts` (+2), `GstChildProcess.test.ts` (+1 and the payload field list), `silentOutputWatch.test.ts` (the late reason from the watch: 3 new, 2 replaced), `AudioOutput302mModule.test.ts` (+3: the taps, the watch, the seed cap), `AudioOutput302mModule.playsNothing.test.ts` (+2: the watch, the INFO line); the engine's and the plugins' unit suites, 231 files, 3,609 tests, all pass; the engine and six plugins typecheck clean. **Mutants,** 12 of 12 caught. Native, on CU, CB and PW: the base runner (12 checks fail), the catch-up as first built (buffers only, no stream rule: 3), no stream rule (2), GAPs passed (1); and the probe point: the watches instead of the taps, measured in the rig's 120 s stop above (11 of 13 wedged). TS: the seeds uncapped (1 test fails), the watch's event unwired (1), the late reason waiting for a tick (4), no `catchUp` in the description (1), the INFO line not matched to its tap (1), the raise never settling (1); and in the rig, the base runner on the run-2 repro (4 of 4 latched). **Device check** (next round on .108, not run): the A3 drill again, 12 Device Manager PipeWire restarts with the recorder early, late and none, then a 120 s PipeWire stop: no silence over 2 s after the output's re-link in any restart (the recordings and the engine's own "Plays nothing" lines), no "Playout re-anchor: … route raised" and no "Arrived … past the playout budget" after a restart, renderMs back to its value before, health warning within 3 s whenever the sink plays late; one "Caught up at the start" INFO line per rebuild naming the Mixer. The 120 s stop the same, and no runner killed ("Force killing") and no "Runner request timeout" for the Audio Mixer; should either still wedge (Limits (a)), `gdb -p <pid> -batch -ex "thread apply all bt"` on the output's and the Mixer's runners before anything restarts them. **Phase 3 line:** the same output, runner and helpers on p3w1 to p3w3 and p4w1: the fix goes there at the next carry merge, with its tests. Texts: this row and the intro, the release notes (Fixed), ADR-0029 (302M fan-ins: a launch's catch-up), plugins/README.md, the runner's and the output's comments. |
| B-207 | While PipeWire did not answer, the engine's audio device lists read empty: the device picker showed a box with no audio devices, and an audio module started meanwhile said its device was not connected; c23 had meant a pactl call with no answer to be no answer, never an empty one (the owner's MR-042) | Release line (the fix build ebd26037). Found 2026-11-03 on the .108 test box (DEV-FIX4a A5(b), PipeWire frozen by SIGSTOP for about 35 s), fixed 2026-11-03 by c30 (the orchestrator's brief: while PipeWire does not answer or does not run, every audio device list the engine serves keeps its last good list, marked stale with the reason and since when, never an empty one, and says "no answer" when there is no good list yet; a module's device check reads no answer as unknown, so a running module does not stop or start waiting for hot-plug because of a hang and a waiting one is not told its device is gone; MR-021's recovery and MR-002's re-pick unchanged; the UI changed only if it needs to be; whether anything of ours restarts PipeWire when it does not answer, read only; the rest engineering calls, for the owner's veto). Rows B-203 to B-205 are bug batch 7's, written in another clone; this row follows B-206 until the orchestrator orders them at the merge. **Seen** (`mr-captures/wf13/fix4a/108/a5-hang.out`, `a5-hang/`, `log/a5-hang.jsonl`; SIGSTOP 09:00:59.8Z): `GET /api/v1/system/devices/audio-source` answered HTTP 200 with 0 items in 1.46 s (+4 s) and 1.05 s (+18 s), audio-sink 0 items; the engine logged "PipeWire does not answer pactl: audio devices read as absent until it does" at 09:01:05.9Z ("pactl list sinks … no answer within 5000 ms") and "PipeWire answers pactl again" at 09:02:02.9Z (downMs 57036). With PipeWire stopped for 120 s (`a5-stop/`): 0 items in 0.06 s, pactl failing at once ("Connection failure: Connection refused"). **Cause** (ebd26037): `AudioDeviceOps.fetchDevices` returned what it had parsed, nothing or half a list, whenever either pactl call failed, and only `isAvailable()` said it was no answer. The device watchdog read that (c23); the device providers did not, so every list served was empty; the readers joined a listing already in flight (`SharedRead`), hence 1 to 1.5 s, not 5. The four audio modules' starts read `hasDevice` false and said "Audio device … not connected — waiting for hot-plug" (B-200's Limits). Where the lists go: `registerPipeWireDeviceProvider`'s `list()` on the `DeviceProviderRegistry`, read by the local API route, the registry's 2 s diff poll (its `deviceList` goes to the router's own tree, `/devices/<type>`, and to the manager, whose `devices:<type>` and tree path `/engines/<id>/devices/<type>` the UI's device picker reads through `tree/mirror.ts` and `useDeviceStore`) and the 10 s heartbeat's snapshot; nothing else reads them. **Fix (as built):** (1) `PaCommandQueue`: a pactl killed at its timeout rejects with `PactlNoAnswer` (new), any other failure with a plain error. (2) `AudioDeviceOps.deviceListing()` (`listDevices` is gone): PipeWire's answer, or, while a listing gets none, its last whole answer with `stale: { reason, since }`: "PipeWire not answering" (the timeout) or "PipeWire not running" (failed at once), since the ask time of the first listing of that reason with no answer; `devices` is null when it never answered, and one list answered with the other not is no answer. `hasDevice` is `null` while stale (unknown, never gone), `getDeviceInfo` null; `isAvailable()` means "not stale". The outage's one warning now says the lists stay as PipeWire last answered. (3) The provider serves a stale list's devices with `meta.stale` (`{ reason, since }`, since an ISO second) and the label ending " — PipeWire not answering since 2026-11-03T09:01:00Z"; with no device of its kind to carry the mark (never answered, or none in the last answer), one nameless entry ("No answer: PipeWire not answering since …", or "No device in PipeWire's last list — …"). Sinks are held at unity only from a fresh list. Every path still carries an array. (4) The device watchdog reads `null` as unknown: no unplug while running, no rebuild while waiting, and a waiting module rebuilds only on PipeWire's own answer. (5) `GstPluginBase.startWaitsForDevice` (new) is the four modules' start check: not listed, "not connected — waiting for hot-plug" as before; no answer, "PipeWire is not answering — starting once PipeWire and the device are back"; either way the watchdog starts the module once PipeWire lists its device. `detectDeviceFormat` gives no "not found" warning while the device is unknown. (6) The UI (`ModuleSettingsPanel.vue`): a nameless entry is the picker's header, never a choice, and a selected device off such a list reads "(that note)", not "(Disconnected)". A stale list with devices needed no change: the picker lists them as the engine labels them. No flag. | The lists stay arrays because a manager and UI of v2.0.0.100, which engines of this release meet (the test boxes report to one), use them as device lists: an object would break their settings panel, and a field beside the list would be dropped on the way. So the mark rides on each device, in the label every UI shows and in `meta.stale` for programs, and a list with no device gets the one nameless entry, the only in-band place an empty array lacks. Unknown rather than the last list's answer: a list from before the hang must never start or rebuild a module against a PipeWire that does not answer; it is for people to pick from. "Since" is the first unanswered ask, the last moment PipeWire was asked and gave no answer; it answered before that. A timeout and a failure at once are told apart because they are different faults on the box (a hung daemon, one that is down). | **What happens now** (the dev Pi, the engine's real pactl path with a stand-in pactl first on PATH that hangs or fails at once, `staleDeviceList.test.ts`, new, 3): hung, the API's audio-source list answers within the 1.5 s test timeout with the last list, its device marked "PipeWire not answering since …" from the first unanswered listing, audio-sink too; the registry pushes the marked list once, never an empty one; `hasDevice` is null and a running module's watchdog does nothing; the next answer pushes the fresh list once, the mark gone, nothing rebuilt. Failing at once: "PipeWire not running since …", well inside the timeout; a hang after it is its own reason and since. An engine started during the hang lists one nameless "No answer: PipeWire not answering since …" entry; a module waiting for its device is not started from it, and the first answer lists the device and starts it. The built engine with the real pactl (16.1 on the dev Pi, `mr-captures/wf13/c30/real-pactl.txt`): a socket path nothing listens on reads "PipeWire not running" in 110 ms, a socket that accepts and never answers "PipeWire not answering" at the 1.5 s timeout. **Limits:** (a) a reader still waits for a hung listing up to the 5 s timeout (B-200's), then gets the stale list. (b) Two checks that are not the device check still stop a module during a hang, as before: c18's capture stall (no audio for 4 s) tears a mic capture down with "PipeWire is not answering — rebuilding the stream once PipeWire and the device are back", and an Audio Output (302M) whose mixer delivers nothing relaunches (c20's watch) into a pipeline that cannot connect to a frozen PipeWire; both rebuild once PipeWire answers (DEV-FIX4a A5(b)). They are MR-021's recovery and were left as they are; holding them while pactl gets no answer would be its own item. (c) A UI older than this release shows a nameless entry as an option: picking it clears the module's device. (d) The modules' loss text says "PipeWire is not answering" for a PipeWire that is down as well (B-195's), where the lists say "not running". (e) The last list lives in the engine's memory: an engine started during an outage says "No answer" until PipeWire answers. **Found on the way** (read only): nothing of ours restarts or kills PipeWire when it does not answer. The engine restarts it only in `Engine.resetEngine()` (`systemctl --user restart pipewire`), on the user's Reset (the UI, a dashboard's reset action, the router tree's reset call), which logs "Resetting engine..." (not in `a5-hang.jsonl`); its pactl timeout kills only pactl. The Device Manager restarts it only on its audio page's Restart PipeWire (`restartPipewire()`, the socket's `requestRestartPipewire`) and in `hdmi-audio-hotplug.sh` on an HDMI connect, opted in by `/data/pipewire/hdmi-hotplug-restart`: both `systemctl --user restart pipewire pipewire-pulse wireplumber`, all three at once, a manual restart that systemd does not count in NRestarts. The run's NRestarts=1 is systemd's own `Restart=on-failure` (the stock unit, no `WatchdogSec`): the pipewire daemon itself exited with an error or died by a signal about 25 s after the CONT. Why it did is PipeWire's or the kernel's, not this code's; the device check below reads it. **Tests:** `staleDeviceList.test.ts` (new, 3, with `fakePactl.ts`'s new `fail` mode), `AudioDeviceOps.test.ts` (+5, 8 updated), `PaCommandQueue.test.ts` (+1, 1 updated), `pipeWireDeviceProvider.test.ts` (+5, its stub on `deviceListing`), `DeviceWatchdog.test.ts` (+3), `deviceFormat.test.ts` (+1), the four modules' (+2 each; the 302M harnesses take a PipeWire that does not answer), `ModuleSettingsPanel.test.ts` (+3), `hungPipeWire.test.ts` (on `deviceListing`); c18's real-PipeWire tests (the input and output `pipewireRestart.test.ts`), c29's `pipewireRestartMix.test.ts` and `restartWhileDark.test.ts` and the N-1's `absentInput.test.ts` on a private PipeWire, all pass; the unit suites of the engine, the manager, the manager UI and six audio plugins, 233 files, 2,871 tests, all pass; the engine, the manager UI, the four audio plugins and the seven other plugins that use the PipeWire or device API typecheck clean. **Mutants,** 12 of 12 caught: c23's empty or half list on no answer (8 tests fail), `hasDevice` from a stale list (4), stale devices unmarked (4), an empty list for no device (3), a timeout that is no `PactlNoAnswer` (4), "since" moved by each listing (1), a waiting module rebuilt with no answer (1), a start reading no answer as not connected (4), "not found" while unknown (2), the UI offering the note as a choice (1), sinks set from a stale list (1), a running module unplugged on no answer (4). **Device check** (.108, not run): freeze pipewire 30 s (SIGSTOP, a box timer for the CONT): `devq.py audio-source audio-sink` at +4 s and +18 s answers within 5 s with the last list, each device's label ending "— PipeWire not answering since <the freeze>" and `meta.stale`, never 0 items; after the CONT (or PipeWire's own restart) the list is fresh again within a few seconds, labels plain; no module says "Device disconnected" or "not connected — waiting for hot-plug" (the engine log and the manager's watch), a module restarted during the freeze says "PipeWire is not answering — starting once …" and starts when PipeWire answers; the mics' capture-stall rebuild of Limits (b) may still show. PipeWire stopped 60 s: "PipeWire not running since …" in under 1 s. And `systemctl --user show pipewire.service -p NRestarts,ExecMainCode,ExecMainStatus` plus `journalctl --user -u pipewire` (or the system journal with sudo) after the freeze, to read how the daemon ended if it is restarted again. **Phase 3 line:** B-200's listing is not on p3w1 yet; this goes there with it, after B-195, at the next carry merge, with its tests. Texts: this row and the intro, the release notes (c23's bullet amended), plugins/README.md (Device Watchdog, Available Services). |
| B-208 | A live input's loss no longer leaves an Audio Mixer free-running from running time 0: a running aggregator keeps its last input pad for the next add. An Audio Mixer whose only input was lost at a profile switch restarted its output at running time 0 and ran about 49 times real time, silent and hours off the house clock (the owner's MR-046, first logged as MR-044) | Release line (the fix build 0f7c683f; the fault is older and hidden on v2.0.0.100). Found 2026-11-03 on the .103 test box (DEV-FIX4b's 1 h soak, profile 'default'), diagnosed the same day offline and cold-checked (scratch wf13/mr044: `mr044.md`, `coldcheck.md`, `plan.md`; data in `mr-captures/wf13/fix4b/103`), fixed 2026-11-04 by c31 (the orchestrator's brief: exactly the plan's WI-1: a running GstAggregator's last sink pad kept on a branch drop, unlinked, by aggregator name, and taken by the next `bus_input_add` for that aggregator; an aggregator with more inputs releases as before; `clear()` frees the kept pads; one log line per keep; both runners; the GStreamer patch for the image, the plan's WI-4, not part of it; the rest engineering calls, for the owner's veto). Bug batch 9's first row. **Seen** (`mr-captures/wf13/fix4b/103/soak/`, the drill journal): at the switch back to 'default' at 13:33:15Z the N-1 Mixer (302M) started three times, and 'N1 Out 1 meter', an Audio Mixer whose only source is its output, lost that branch 55 ms after its egress armed and took it back about 330 ms later; its first timing PES then read 25,902.533 s ahead, the 2^33 wrap less the house time modulo that wrap: PES − 1 h ≡ 0, running time 0. Its mix then ran at about 49 times real time (about 100 Mbit/s against 2.1 Mbit/s for its siblings), every PES 10.0 s ahead and timed by house now under c26's guard (6.7 million by 13:56Z, 16.1 million by 14:29Z), and every 33 min the sweep passed through the guard's window and froze the stamp: 8.4 → 38.5 → 68.4 s and 19.8 → 49.8 s late, about 90 s each, with "Output timing off the house clock" as its health; silence throughout. The same lost-and-back sequence runs at every start of that mixer on both builds (lost 96 to 173 ms after the start): 1 of 4 starts went wrong on 0f7c683f, none of 6 on 3a2ed1fe. **Cause** (GStreamer 1.28.2's `gstaggregator.c` and `gstaudioaggregator.c`, read and reproduced): both runners released the aggregator's request pad when they dropped a lost live input (`bus_inputs.cpp` `remove_bin`, `gst-pipeline-runner.py` `_remove_live_bin`). The aggregator's loop clears `first_buffer` once its pads have data (`gstaggregator.c`:574-575), negotiates, then aggregates outside the object lock (:1521-1534), so a release of its only pad in between left `aggregate()` with no sink pad. GstAudioAggregator, non-live, starts each round as EOS (`gstaudioaggregator.c`:2248), finds no pad to say otherwise and takes "last buffer incomplete" over none (:2559-2594): one buffer at its position with a garbage duration, then offset 0 and position `segment.start`, running time 0 (:2627-2628). The next pad's data selects no start, `first_buffer` being false already, so the mix runs from 0 at CPU speed towards its input's house time: about 125 h of silence at 49 times real time on .103. A second way in: an EOS on the only pad before any data leaves the offset at 0 after the all-EOS round, and the next stream resumes the task with it (the STREAM_START resets the position, not GstAudioAggregator's offset). Hidden on v2.0.0.100: no egress guard, the 1 h rule hides the offset (one "off the house timeline: not shown" warning per tap), and the mixer is silent with health ok. Reproduced on the dev Pi: `aggrace.py` (deterministic, GStreamer only), and the real native runner hosting .103's pipeline with its producer killed and its branch re-added as the engine does: 6 of 160 runs off the house clock on 0f7c683f, 2 of 160 on 3a2ed1fe, none of 160 with a prototype of this fix. **Fix (as built):** `bus_inputs.cpp`: `remove_bin` keeps the pad when its owner is a `GstAggregator` (`GST_IS_AGGREGATOR`; gstreamer-base is linked already) and it is its last sink pad: unlinked, a reference held under the aggregator's name, one log line "live input: last pad of <aggregator> kept for the next add (<pad>)"; `handle_bus_input_add` takes the kept pad first, while it is still one of that aggregator's, and says so ("bus_input_add: … -> mixin on its kept pad sink_0"); an add whose branch cannot link leaves the pad kept; `clear()` (the stop) and `declare()` (a start) give every kept pad back. With other inputs left, the lost one's pad is released as before. `gst-pipeline-runner.py`: the same in `_remove_live_bin`, `handle_bus_input_add` and the start and stop; it tells an aggregator by its GType's name, so the runner loads no GstBase typelib. | The kept pad leaves the aggregator a sink pad through the race: the round that follows the pads-ready check mixes the buffer it found there, and the position holds. Until the next add the mixer waits on it as it waited with no pad at all: non-live, a pad without data is not ready; live, a timeout mixes silence either way. What the old branch left on it, the rest of a buffer being mixed or a GAP, is mixed or dropped by its running time like any input's data, never before the mix's position. Only the last pad: with another input left a round always has a pad, and an unlinked pad beside another one would hold a non-live mixer for ever. By aggregator, not by branch: the next add for that aggregator takes it, whichever source it brings (the engine re-adds the same branch; a changed source brings another). In the runners, not in GStreamer: a GStreamer patch is an image release, this ships with the app, and the patch follows as the plan's WI-4. | **What happens now** (the dev Pi, GStreamer 1.28.2): GStreamer alone (`gst_audioaggregator_last_pad_test.py`, new): with the only pad released while the first negotiation is held, the mix runs at 150 to 280 times real time, 4,003,263 s (the Pi's uptime) behind house time, reported as a known fault; with the pad kept instead it stays on house time (worst 53 ms, 1.08 times real time), as does the control with neither. Each runner's own drop code on that race (`gst_live_inputs_test.py` in process, `tests/bus_inputs_kept_pad_test.cpp`, new): the pad kept, the add takes it, the mix on house time (worst 45 ms, 1.08 times real time); the same cases on the code before this row restart the mix at running time 0 (4,003,641 s and 4,004,522 s behind). A kept pad holding the rest of a 15 ms buffer and a 20 ms GAP: mixed out, then the next branch's data from where the mix was, every output starting where the one before it ended. A pad never taken: the mixer waits, no error, the stop gives the reference back. With two inputs the lost one's pad goes and its re-add gets a new one; the engine's `bus_input_remove` releases one of two as well and keeps the last. Through the protocol on audio-mixer's own start (`last_pad_case`, both runners): one source whose producer dies and is back 300 ms later: "last pad of mixin kept", the re-add on it, every egress PES after it within 1 s of house time (the first 346 to 355 ms behind: the gap's silence) and no PTS stepping back, the source in the mix at its content time; two sources: the lost one released and re-added on sink_2, the other in every block; one that never comes back: nothing out a second after the loss, exit 0 at once. The statistical rig (`mr044/harness`, the native runner and .103's pipeline, in `mr-captures/wf13/c31/hunt`): none of 480 runs off the house clock in three passes of 160 (6 of 160 before); where logged, the pad kept and taken again in 319 of 320 runs, the other's driver failing before its result (the same settings ten times clean after). **Limits:** (a) The EOS way in stays: an EOS on the only pad before any data still rewinds the mix on stock GStreamer, pad kept or not (the new test's EK); the modules' 302M branches hold their EOS (`mralignwatch hold-on-eos=true`), so the aggregators they feed never get one, and the image patch (WI-4) is its fix. (b) A source taken away for good leaves its pad kept: the mixer waits on it as it waited with none, until the next add or the stop. (c) Only a `bus_input_add` for that aggregator takes a kept pad. (2) Nothing took a raise back down: it lives in memory only, cleared by an edit of the head's Playout Offset or an engine restart. A module's own Restart keeps the instance, which went on showing it. (4) A late timeline past what the route can still be raised was raised to the cap and stayed late: the sink's ring skips late samples, so the output played nothing at 'ceiling'. That is a one-source output, which has no aligner, 2 to 10 s late, or a mix whose aligners' pace lies between D + 2 s and their 4 s ceiling. A leg's request that comes within a hold plus the settle window (17 s) of its own raise landing, its excess within `REANCHOR_TOLERANCE_MS` (40 ms) of that raise's, is `held`: no raise, D kept; it is judged after the settle window and before the ceiling. Held, the leg's later requests within the tolerance stay held, also after the raise came down, until one's excess differs by more than the tolerance (fallen: as before; risen: it may raise again) or the leg's sink plays on time again (the 302M output's playout watch, `MediaRouter.notePlayoutOnTime`). The head's raise records the hold (`held`) and its reason and badge say so; the leg shows one warning, 'Plays N ms late at its device: a larger playout offset cannot help, so route head H is held at D ms; nothing dropped.', logged once an episode, as the engine's one WARN; and a 302M output's playout watch reading every buffer late is then its sink's pace, not 'Plays nothing' (`SilentOutputWatch.held`). A request is `backlog` only for a queue past the raise already standing (`judgeCause`: `queuedMs` less the raise and the leg's own offset). (2) A raise comes back down. Every module reports its content lateness on the house clock without D at each timing tick (`LatenessReporter.contentLatenessMs`: the latest bus-ingress tap's window mean or its aligners' pace, the later; `ModuleTiming`, then `MediaRouter.notePlayoutLateness`). Once every leg that asked and still plays from the head has reported under the head's configured D for `DECAY_HOLD_MS` (60 s), counted from the head's last raise too, the raise goes in one step: one fan-out, the head cleared, each leg told of a zero raise, and one INFO line, 'Playout re-anchor: SRT -> MUL back to its configured 60 ms, down 1940 ms in one step: the outputs that asked arrived on time for 60 s; about 1940 ms of held content skipped at each, its time passed'. A leg that asked and has no fresh report (no reading, stopped or dark: older than 10 s) holds the raise up; one that left the route does not. (3) A late timeline past the route's reach re-anchors its leg alone. A `timeline` request that the route's remaining headroom cannot cover, from a leg whose content itself arrives late (its last fresh report at or past the configured D), gives the leg its own offset (`legMs`: the excess plus 40 ms on the 20 ms grid, within `MAX_PLAYOUT_OFFSET_MS`), and its route is not raised; `effectivePlayoutOffsetMs` adds that offset. A late sink with the content on time (a mix's aligners are no queue elements, so its request reads `timeline`) is raised as before, then held, never re-anchored on its own. (4) A standing raise stays visible: `MediaRouter.getHeadPlayoutRaise`, `getHeadPlayoutNote` and `getLegPlayout` give the router's standing state, which `PlayoutReanchorState` reads at each start and each PLAYING. A new head instance shows its raise (section, badge, warning) from its start; a leg that asked shows its route's raise as its section (Configured, Raised to, Since), and one re-anchored on its own its warning; the leg's section gains Configured and Since. The manager pushes only for a new dgram session (`EngineConnectionManager`'s 'connection': `hello` and `pushActiveConfig`) or an activation. The client gives a dead link up after about 4.5 to 5.25 s (3000 ms, 3 misses), the server after about 7.5 to 8.75 s (5000 ms, 3 misses), so the client re-handshakes with the same nonce and `Server.handleConnect` re-acks the session it holds and returns before emitting 'connection': no `hello`, no push. The router then journaled every on-site change for good, sent whole states instead of `statePatch` (`states.disconnected()`, and no `hello` again), and a local Stop made the manager's 10 s run-state reconcile send Start, whose activation push dropped the journal. (2) `ManagerConnection` passes it on and logs 'Connected to manager (session kept)'. (3) `LocalChanges.resumed()`: when the link dropped after this session's push was merged, the journal goes up at once and changes go live; a session that dropped before its push was merged keeps waiting for it. (4) `ManagerStateSync` keeps `statePatch` on a kept session (`offered`). (5) Guaranteed sends take an ack callback: `Client.send` calls `onAck` once, on the first path's ack; `Socket.send` and `ReliableDelivery.track` carry it, never calling it on a give-up or a destroy. `LocalChanges` keeps what it sent and the manager has not acked (the latest op per path, and the last Start/Stop) and puts it back into the journal at `linkDown`. No manager or protocol change; no flag. | Engine only: an old manager (the fleet manager on v2.0.0.100) gets the fix with the router's update, and deploy order does not matter. The resume is read from the server's own answer (the same session id), not from timing. Ack-based, not a resend of whatever went out lately: a change the manager acked is never sent twice, and one it got without its ack reaching the router is sent again harmlessly, as on-site ops are leaf values and id-path removes. Not taken: the diagnosis's optional supersede part (a manager patch landing while the router journals drops the router's entries at or below its path). With the resume, a router journals with its link up only between a new session's 'connected' and its connect push, and every manager patch of a new session was made after that push (the manager marks the engine online and pushes in one tick, and sends patches only to an online engine); dropping the entry there would let the older push revert the router while the manager keeps its value, a divergence, where today the router's value wins on both sides. Left for an owner call. | **What happens now** (`managerSync.integration.test.ts`, new, 2: the real Manager and this engine's real comms, patch router, wiring, router tree and LCP server in one process over loopback, with Socket.IO clients for a router dashboard on `/tree`, the LCP and a manager dashboard; the drop: every packet lost both ways, then the path's watchdog firing, the link back on the kept session): a write sent into the dead link and one made while it was down show on the manager dashboard after the link is back, without a push, and then a router-tree write, an LCP write, an interlock unmute with the other member's mute, `enabled`, Stop on the tree and Start on the LCP, and a module restart's state each show within 1 s, the state as `statePatch`. (b) `clockSource.ts` `pollClockSource` reads `status.env` once a poll, beside `systemctl is-active` and whatever the source (a step's poll, which asks no pmc, too): its domain for pmc, its fallback as `ntpFallback`, left out without the file. 8 `sync_source` 0 none, 1 NTP (chrony, also on MR-048b's NTP fallback: no new value), 2 SNTP, 3 PTP; 9 `tai_utc_offset_s` (0 unset); 10 `ptp_domain` (0xFF when `ptp_valid` is 0); 11–18 `grandmaster_identity`, the EUI-64 `clockIdentity` (all ones when `ptp_valid` is 0); with `ptp_valid` 0 it writes 0xFF and all ones whatever the struct holds, and `decode` returns the wire as it is. `decode(data, len, &decl)` takes a descriptor from its tag: tag 0x05, `'MRHT'`, `descriptor_length` ≥ 24 inside `len`, `hc_version` ≥ 1 (0 is refused); it reads the fields it knows and ignores trailing bytes and reserved bits, so a 24-byte descriptor decodes with `timeline_id` 0 and a later version's longer one as version 1's fields. `find_in(program_info, &decl)` walks the loop itself, every registration descriptor (`registration_format` reads only the first, S4), and takes the first `MRHT` that decodes, a short one skipped; one that overruns the loop is none. `strip_from(program_info)` drops every `MRHT` registration (any length from 4, decodable or not) and keeps every other byte in order, an overrunning tail verbatim. `error_class(err_us)` = ceil(log2(max(1, err_us))) saturating at 31, negative or NaN 0xFF (the caller chooses `err_us`: under PTP p5-9's `\|offsetNs\| / 1000`, S2); `error_bound_us(class)` = 2^class µs, −1 unknown (Trust's `lo`). `parse_gm` takes pmc's `2ccf67.fffe.76e669` and eight pairs split by `:` or by `-` (RFC 7273's form, which the engine sends, p5-9), either case, and refuses other spellings (no separators, mixed ones); `gm_text` writes RFC 7273's upper-case form. `timeline_text` / `parse_timeline_text`: `timeline_id`'s one text form for the element property, messages, stats and the drain key, 16 lower-case hex digits, no prefix, `0000000000000000` = none; the parser refuses upper case, a prefix and any other length. **Tests:** `tests/ts_hcdesc_test.cpp`, 45 checks: the exact 34 bytes of a full declaration; round trips of the defaults, every field at its minimum and maximum, all 16 flag combinations and each sync source; `strip_from` removing two full `MRHT` and a bare one and keeping `KLVA` and ISO 639 byte-identical; `error_class(1200) == 11` and its edges; the three identity spellings and nine refused; the timeline text; the descriptor through `build_pmt_section`, `packetise_section` and `parse_pmt`. (2) Every PCR → `net_pcr27(t + E, D_e)`, t the clock read for that PCR, on any PID with its program's D_e, the input's flags kept; on the PCR PID a PCR-only packet (CC = the PID's last payload CC) is inserted before a packet once 35 ms passed since the last PCR on the latest clock reading, not while a header is held on that PID nor before a packet that carries its own PCR. (3) PCR_PID 0x1FFF: the first video ES, else audio, else the first ES (DemuxCore's `classify`), one `pcr-pid-assigned` per choice. (4) Every input PMT section is replaced at the packet that completes it (its earlier packets dropped) by the program's output section on the writer's own CC: the input program_info with every `MRHT` stripped and ours appended, the PCR PID out, the streams verbatim; the output version starts at the input's first and bumps by one whenever the section's bytes (version and CRC aside) change, so an input version-only bump is not passed on; a section that grows inserts packets (`pmt-grew` once per program), one that shrinks sends fewer. (5) λ = t − `house_from_mux_pts`(DTS else PTS, t) on `timing_pes` PES only, t the buffer's latest clock reading (its own or the last PCR's), so DTS − PCR ≥ headroom holds against the PCR in force; λ < 0 counts as 0, λ > 60 s is counted `latenessOffHouse` and ignored (S22). (6) D_e (part 4.4): floor + margin until the first timing PES, then max(floor, ceil10(λ + margin + \|ε\|)) (`d-e-start`); raised to ceil10(λ + margin + \|ε\|) when λ > D_e − headroom (`d-e-raise`, each ≥ 130 ms); lowered only at the first timing PES after a gap, to max(target, ceil10(D_e − g)) (`d-e-lower`); at `max` > 0 held there, one `d-e-max` per episode (the start included), the episode ended by a lower. (7) Each D_e change: the program's new PMT, then a PCR-only packet with `discontinuity_indicator`, both before the PES that caused it; a re-epoch (E or seq changed, E 0 → E included): event `re-epoch` (seq, from, ΔE) and, per program at the next buffer's head, the new PMT then the flagged PCR, the new E from each PID's next PUSI; any other declared field (a `timeline_id`, the published error class, the source…): the new PMT at the head, no flagged PCR, no D_e change. (8) Gaps: a GAP buffer's packets are consumed (`read_gap_length`) and dropped (S8), a bus silence ≥ 500 ms between buffers is a gap [last now, now]; g is the gap time no earlier gap covered (interval [end − length, end] in house ns), so one hole's markers on several PIDs, or an outage's growing markers, count once. counters `droppedBeforePmt`, `gapMarkers`, `gaps`, `ccLostIn`, `reEpochs`, `held`. **The CLI** (`python3 -m egress_core in.ts --clock case.clock.json [--bus sidecar] [--chunk N] [--out] [--expect]`, the contract `mrts_cli egress` ports): the content clock at a byte offset = the house time of the first PCR PID's PCRs (unwrapped, − 1 h;
